Alamance County tax office and housing snapshot

One county department lists, values and collects tax on everything taxable. It sits at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, opens weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and answers at (336) 228-1312. Graham is the county seat and Burlington is the largest community, with Elon, Haw River, Green Level, Ossipee, Swepsonville and Alamance inside the county lines and parts of Mebane and Gibsonville as well.

The 2020 count was 171,415 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 186,177 is 8.6% higher. Median home value for 2020 to 2024 was $241,500, owners live in 65.0% of homes, and builders took out 2,027 permits in 2025. Check your own parcel in the county property record search before you name a price.

Four things shape a sale here: the January 1 listing date, the September 1 due date, the 2027 revaluation, and a delinquent tax check at recording.

Tax calendar

The tax year is fixed on January 1: whoever owns a parcel that day is the person billed. Statements arrive in July, and a payment made by January 5 owes no interest.

Alamance County tax calendar and relief deadlines
DateWhat happens
January 1Listing date; owner on this day is billed
January 1 to 31Filing window for present-use and exemption applications
June 1Deadline for elderly, disabled, circuit breaker and disabled veteran relief
JulyBills mailed
September 1Bills due
January 5Last day to pay with no interest
January 6Delinquent; 2% interest added, then 0.75% on the sixth of each later month

A house bought after January 1 can still produce a bill in the seller's name, even after the deed is recorded and the record is updated. Correct the mailing address ahead of July so the bill finds you.

You can pay by mail (the postmark counts), in an indoor or outdoor drop box (credited as of the drop date), or online with a convenience fee. Registered vehicles are billed separately by the state through Tag and Tax Together when you renew your registration.

The 2027 revaluation

Every parcel in Alamance County is being revalued effective January 1, 2027, and notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023. North Carolina requires reappraisal at least every eight years under G.S. 105-286, and Alamance chose to do it every four.

Vincent Valuations, which helped with the 2023 work, is doing the 2027 appraisal. Staff spend roughly two years in the field checking property features, comparing sales and noting improvements. The target is to land at or close to 100% of market value.

Seeing a bigger value on the notice does not guarantee a bigger bill, since rates tend to fall as values rise, and a revenue neutral rate would keep the typical owner near last year's payment. A parcel that gained more than average pays more, and one that lagged pays less.

Planning to sell in 2027? Open the notice the day it arrives. Your appeal period runs from its date, and late filings are generally turned away. For revaluation questions, call the same number as the tax department, (336) 228-1312.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Alamance County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your property value

Start with an informal review by county appraisers. If that leaves a dispute, the Board of Equalization and Review hears it. The filing window depends on the kind of property.

  • Real property: during the annual listing period, with documentation such as sales, photos, repair estimates or an appraisal.
  • Business and individual personal property: thirty days from the notice of value.
  • Registered vehicles: thirty days after the due date shown on the combined tag and tax notice.

The local board starts deliberating about the first week of April and gives each side a fixed amount of time. Losing at the local level opens the door to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh. It works like a trial, applies evidence rules and places the burden on the taxpayer.

Common grounds include a value above the likely sale price, wrong square footage or condition on the record, and nearby sales that point lower. A comparable sales tool and a property record search are on the county site to help you gather proof.

Tax relief programs

June 1 is the usual filing deadline, and income caps change yearly, so ask the tax department for current figures. An online eligibility calculator on the county site covers four of the programs.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the home's taxable value, subject to an income cap.
  • Circuit breaker deferral: postpones part of the tax on a permanent residence, scaled to income. Owners must be 65 or older, or disabled, with five years of ownership and residence behind them.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: shelters the first $45,000 of assessed value for an honorably discharged veteran with a total, permanent service-connected disability, or for a surviving spouse. Age and income do not matter.
  • Present-use value: taxes qualifying farm, horticulture and forestry land on its use, but taxes deferred for the previous three years can be recaptured if the land leaves the program.

Selling while a deferral or present-use status is in place? Ask about payoff or recapture amounts before you agree to a closing date.

What the county checks when a deed is recorded

Since May 2, 2011, each deed to be recorded, except timber deeds and releases, goes to the county Tax Department first for delinquent tax certification (G.S. 161-31(b)). A seller with back taxes should clear them so the certification can be issued.

After recording, the change reaches the property record in a short chain. The Register of Deeds keeps the document and assigns it a book and page number. Land Records staff review it, update the owner name and mailing address, and send the change to the online record and GIS map. A simple sale of an existing parcel moves faster than a split or a new subdivision. If nothing shows up after several weeks, call Land Records with the book and page number.

When an owner has died, the county follows the estate file at the Clerk of Superior Court or recorded documents. Bills stay due on schedule meanwhile, and staff ask for the estate file number, the parcel number or address, and a mailing address.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Alamance County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Sort the tax side out before you set a closing date. Find out who is billed for the current year, since the January 1 owner gets the bill. Ask the tax department whether any back taxes would stop the deed from being certified. If a deferral or present-use status applies, get the payoff or recapture figure in writing. Then split the year's cost with the buyer at closing and check that the mailing address on the record is correct. A cash sale does not remove any of these steps, but it can shorten the wait around them.

Frequently asked questions

When are Alamance County property taxes due?

September 1. Interest starts January 6, so a bill paid by January 5 carries none. After that, 2% is added, plus 0.75% on the sixth of each following month.

Whose name is on the bill after an early-year purchase?

A bill can still arrive under the prior owner's name, because the county lists parcels to the January 1 owner. Divide the cost at closing and fix the mailing address before July.

When will new values from the 2027 revaluation arrive?

Notices of value are scheduled to be mailed February 15, 2027, for the January 1, 2027 effective date. Your appeal deadline is tied to the date on that notice.

What is the deadline for tax relief programs in Alamance County?

June 1 for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferral and the disabled veteran exclusion. Present-use and exemption filings fall in the January listing window.

Who do I call at Alamance County Tax Administration?

Call (336) 228-1312 or visit 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The same number handles revaluation questions.

Avery County tax office

The Tax Administrator's office at 200 Montezuma Street in Newland keeps property records, sets assessments and bills the taxes. It has two divisions: assessment at 828-733-8214 and collections at 828-733-8228. Hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Assessor mail goes to PO Box 305, Newland, NC 28657, and collection mail goes to PO Box 355 in the same town. An online lookup shows real estate, sales and tax bills, and a separate viewer shows tax maps.

Maps and records exist for valuation. The legal description of a parcel is whatever the recorded deed says, so read the deed rather than trusting a map line.

Avery County tax rates

For tax years 2023 through 2025 the county rate is 0.335 and the fire rate is 0.065, a total of 0.40. Ask the tax office how those figures apply to a bill. Towns that levy their own tax add a municipal rate on top, and each town has a code.

Avery County town tax codes and 2025 rates
CodeTownRate
01Banner Elk0.46
02Beech Mountain0.65
03Crossnore0.30
04Elk Park0.30
06Newland0.56
07Seven Devils0.47
08Sugar Mountain0.28

The county and fire rates apply to every parcel, and the town rate applies only where a town levies one. Ask the tax office which codes your parcel carries. Ten fire districts cover the county: Banner Elk, Crossnore, Elk Park, Fall Creek, Green Valley, Linville, Newland, Frank, Beech Mountain and Seven Devils.

Latest revaluation

Current values were set as of January 1, 2022, and notices went out that March. Counties must reappraise real property at least once in eight years, and the goal is a tax value that matches what a willing buyer and seller would agree on.

The county did the work with its own staff instead of hiring an outside appraisal firm. Its revaluation guide includes a sales ratio table for houses: 344 sales at a 91 percent ratio in 2018, 430 sales at 83 percent in 2019, 699 sales at 71 percent in 2020 and 675 sales at 60 percent in 2021. A ratio of 100 percent would mean tax value equals sale price, so values had drifted well below sale prices before the 2022 reset.

Owning a house for decades does not earn a lower value. State law requires uniform appraisal, so a long-held home is valued like comparable homes that sold recently.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Avery County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal a value

Start with the informal review named on the value notice. It is not an appeal. Use it to correct facts on your record, learn how the number was built and compare similar parcels. If you are still unhappy, ask in writing for a formal hearing.

The appeal board is made up of appointed taxpaying citizens rather than commissioners. It sits between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May, and requests must arrive by final adjournment, which is 3:00 p.m. on the closing Monday. Send appeal forms several days before adjournment so hearings can be scheduled. Sessions begin at 9:00 a.m. in courthouse Conference Room 106.

  • Pick up the application at the assessor's office or download it from the county site.
  • Bring record cards and sale prices for similar parcels nearby.
  • The board asks whether the value is accurate and fair. Ability to pay is outside its scope.

A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, by notice within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

Tax relief for homeowners

Three state programs plus a farm program are offered, and one owner can claim only one of the first three. Pick up forms from the tax department and return them to the assessor by June 1.

  • Age 65 or disability exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent home, with income capped at $38,800 for 2026.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: limits the bill to 4 percent of income when income is at or under $38,800 and to 5 percent when it is at or under $58,200 (2026 figures). The excess is deferred and carried as a lien, and you reapply annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes up to $45,000 of appraised value with no age or income test. An unmarried surviving spouse may also qualify.
  • Present use value: farmers with active income from land can ask the office for the criteria and an application.

Deferred taxes matter in a sale. When a circuit breaker owner transfers the property, the last three years of deferred taxes come due with interest on the transfer date.

The listing period

Owners list taxable property during January, and the duty is on the taxpayer even if a form never arrives. Items to list include untagged motor vehicles and motor homes, multi-year tagged trailers, improvements to real estate, income-producing personal property, business equipment, single-wide mobile homes, furnished rental property, and airplanes, boats and motors. Relief applications are taken at listing time too.

State law lets the commissioners extend the period by up to 30 days in a non-revaluation year. An individual with good cause can file a written request for more time before the regular period ends, though no extension runs past April 15.

Questions to ask the tax office before you list

A ten-minute call can head off surprises. Ask which town code and fire district your parcel carries, so you know the full rate a buyer will see. Ask whether any exclusion, deferment or present use status is attached to the parcel, since a deferment can bring back three years of tax at transfer. Ask when the next revaluation is expected, because a buyer will want to know. And ask whether the mailing address on file is current, especially if the house is a seasonal one that sits empty part of the year.

Selling with taxes owed

Bills are due September 1 and carry no interest until January 6, when 2 percent applies. After February 1, three-quarters of a percent accrues each month. The lien attaches on the listing date, so an unpaid bill stays with the parcel through a sale.

Median owner-occupied value is $265,800, and the county has 14,597 housing units against 6,791 households. With so many seasonal homes, bills often go to a second address, so make sure the tax office has a current mailing address.

Before closing, take these steps:

  • Call collections at 828-733-8228 for the exact balance, including any earlier year.
  • Call assessment at 828-733-8214 about any exclusion or deferment on the parcel.
  • Give the figures to the closing attorney so the bill is paid from the proceeds.
  • Give the township or town along with the parcel details so the right rates are applied.

Frequently asked questions

How do I reach the Avery County tax office?

Assessment is 828-733-8214 and collections is 828-733-8228. Visit 200 Montezuma Street in Newland between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

What is the Avery County tax rate?

The county rate is 0.335 and the fire rate is 0.065, a total of 0.40. Towns add their own rate, from 0.28 in Sugar Mountain to 0.65 in Beech Mountain.

When was Avery County's last revaluation?

Values took effect January 1, 2022. State law requires another within eight years, so ask the tax office for the next schedule.

How do I appeal my Avery County property value?

Ask the tax office for an informal review first, then file the written hearing application before the appeal board adjourns, at 3:00 p.m. on the first Monday of May.

Can I get a break on Avery County property tax if I am 65 or disabled?

Yes, when income stays within the 2026 limit of $38,800. The exclusion shelters the larger of $25,000 or half the value, and the assessor must receive the form by June 1.

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina

Selling in Bertie County? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who sends the bill and keeps the maps

One department at 106 Dundee Street in Windsor handles both Tax Collections and Tax Mapping. The tax line, (252) 794-5310, takes bill and payment questions. The mapping line, (252) 794-5311, covers parcels, maps and ownership by street address.

Under Online Services on the county website you will find a tax bill payment page and a real property search. Because the register of deeds indexes only by name, anyone who has just an address should call the mapping line first.

  • Bills and payments: (252) 794-5310
  • Parcels, maps and address lookups: (252) 794-5311
  • Recording and deed indexes: our Bertie County register of deeds page

Bertie County housing in brief

Farm and timber land dominate Bertie. Windsor is the seat, and eight towns are incorporated: Askewville, Aulander, Colerain, Kelford, Lewiston-Woodville, Powellsville, Roxobel and Windsor. Population is 17,086, drifting lower each year. The county has 9,116 housing units, with 72.7 percent of homes lived in by their owners and a typical value of $98,500. With homes that affordable, back taxes can eat a big share of a sale price, so tidy the tax record before you list.

Land records here carry a state-required flag on any tract lying within half a mile of a farm in a voluntary agricultural district, so a buyer searching title will learn about the farm next door.

Revaluation schedule

Current values in Bertie come from January 1, 2020. The state's schedule has the next reappraisal in 2028, which stays within the eight-year ceiling.

In the years between reappraisals, a value changes mainly through building, demolition or rezoning. A house valued off the 2020 schedules may sit far from what a buyer would pay today. For each year from 2012 through 2025, the tax department posts a locational sales report. Read the report for your area and request your property record card before you argue about a value.

The lien runs from the January 1 listing date, so an inflated number costs money on every bill until 2028 arrives.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bertie County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Tax rate, due date and late charges

Bertie's rate on the state's 2024-25 schedule is $.9300 per $100 of value. Each year the county board picks the rate, and towns levy a rate of their own on top. Use the current bill for the live rate.

Bertie County billing calendar
WhenResult
September 1Bill comes due
From September 1 to January 5No interest
January 62% interest attaches
After February 1Three-fourths of a percent added for each month or fraction of a month

A check sent by mail counts as paid on the postmark date, so keep the envelope or a receipt.

What happens when a bill stays open

If a bill sits unpaid, the county can sue in an action patterned on mortgage foreclosure. It ends with a public auction, and the winning bidder may need a deposit of up to 20%. You can still redeem until the court confirms the sale by paying the whole tax along with penalties, interest and costs. Selling the house during that stretch clears all of it at closing.

The county sells its own parcels through upset bids under G.S. 160A-269. A buyer's offer carries a 5% deposit and the newspaper runs a notice. For the next 10 days anyone may outbid it, raising the price by 10% of the first $1,000 plus 5% of whatever is above that. The board is free to reject any offer.

Tax relief for homeowners

A primary home can get help from three state programs. One application covers all three, but you may claim just one. The tax page also hosts a physician certificate form for disability claims, a motor vehicle exemption form and a general exemption application.

With so many residents 65 or older, the elderly exclusion and the circuit breaker reach a large share of owners, and each owner must pass the application's income test.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: subtracts either $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is larger, if the owner is 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled. Income has to be under $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: subtracts the first $45,000 of value regardless of age or income. The disability must be permanent, total and tied to service, and a surviving spouse who has not remarried may claim it as well.
  • Circuit breaker: holds each year's tax to 4% of income, or 5% once income runs between the cap and 1.5 times the cap. Anything above that is deferred and stays on the property as a lien.

File with the county assessor. January is the normal window, and late filings are still accepted through June 1.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bertie County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to challenge a value

Plan around the board of equalization and review, which meets between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May. You must file before it adjourns. If the notice reached you with fewer than 15 days left, you have 15 days from the mailing date instead. Rulings are mailed within a month, and anyone still unhappy has 30 days from that mailing to go to the Property Tax Commission. Take your property record card and the sales report for your area to the hearing.

Steps before you list a Bertie County house

Begin with the tax record, which is the cheapest thing to fix early. Call (252) 794-5310 for the payoff on this year's bill and any older ones. Call (252) 794-5311 to check the parcel number, acreage and owner of record. Compare the square footage and condition on your property record card with what you know to be true. Find out what a sale does to any tax relief you receive. Finally, have the closing attorney order the payoff letter near the closing date so the number is still current on the day the deed is filed.

What a seller owes on the tax side at closing

The seller's proceeds pay off back and current bills. A payoff letter from the tax office gives the closing attorney a firm number.

Circuit breaker participants face one more charge: selling ends eligibility, and the last three years of deferred tax become due with interest.

Sellers also carry the state deed tax of $1.00 for every $500 of value or part of $500. It goes to the register before filing. A local recording resolution wants a return name and address, plus the buyer's permanent mailing address, printed on page one of every instrument.

An inherited title, tenants or deferred repairs change none of this. A lien payoff is identical whether the buyer finances or pays cash, and an as-is sale does not lift a lien before closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Bertie County tax office?

It works out of the county office building at 106 Dundee Street in Windsor. Phone (252) 794-5310 for bills and (252) 794-5311 for maps and parcel lookups.

What county tax rate does Bertie charge?

The state's 2024-25 schedule lists .9300 per $100. The rate for the current year is on your bill, and a town levy is added inside town limits.

When does Bertie County revalue next?

2028 on the state's schedule, which is eight years after the January 1, 2020 reappraisal. A county can reappraise sooner but never later.

What is the cutoff to challenge a Bertie County value?

You must file before the county board of equalization and review adjourns, or within 15 days of a late-mailed notice. Appeals to the Property Tax Commission follow within 30 days of the mailed ruling.

Can I buy a county-owned parcel in Bertie County?

Yes, by upset bid. Deliver a written offer and a 5% deposit to the county manager's office at 106 Dundee Street. A newspaper notice then starts a 10-day window for higher bids, and the board may turn down any offer.

Contacting Bladen County Tax Administration

Tax Administration is at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown. Walk-in hours are weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00. Mail goes to PO Box 385, Elizabethtown, NC 28337. You can phone 910-862-6730 or write to bctax@bladenco.org.

An online portal shows bills and takes payments, and the automated line at 1-877-369-0025 accepts payments by phone. For prior-year assessments, owners can use bladen.ustaxdata.com.

Starting with the 2026 tax year, the county collects for four towns: East Arcadia, Bladenboro, White Lake and Elizabethtown. If your house is inside one of them, ask Tax Administration how the town portion shows up on your bill.

Housing and population in Bladen County

Bladen is a Coastal Plain county in southeastern North Carolina, with the Cape Fear River running through it and White Lake as its main visitor draw. Population is 30,007 as of July 2025, up 1.3% from the 2020 base but well below the 35,190 of 2010. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $135,100, owners hold 69.2% of the housing, and median gross rent is $773. The county issued 97 building permits in 2025.

With values that modest, even a small back-tax or title problem can take a big bite out of a sale price, so clear those items early.

Did the 2026 revaluation change my 2026 bill?

No. The General Assembly postponed Bladen's new values by a year. Bills for 2026 still use the older 2025 values, and the reappraisal values first apply for the 2027 tax year.

The county finished a reappraisal as of January 1, 2026 with a contracted appraisal firm and mailed notices to all real property owners on March 9, 2026. The one before that dated from 2022. Session laws S.L. 2026-8 and S.L. 2026-47 then imposed a one-year moratorium that covers Bladen and eight other counties: Anson, Buncombe, Chowan, Davidson, Guilford, Onslow, Pamlico and Pender.

A county still has to list and appraise anything new it finds during the reappraisal, such as an unrecorded building, using the older schedule of values. New notices of the revised values should go out again in 2027. Because the 2027 value is the one that will drive your bill, call Tax Administration at 910-862-6730 before you list and ask where your parcel stands.

How to appeal your assessment

The session laws give taxpayers in the affected counties the right to appeal 2026 values during calendar year 2026, which runs through December 31, 2026. Call the office to confirm your status, since a fresh notice for 2027 values should open the next round.

Affordability is not a ground for appeal. What counts is an assessment out of line with similar properties, or a factual mistake on the record card. Get the card first, then collect a private appraisal, comparable sales, a survey or photos of structural damage.

Appeal paperwork can be delivered in three ways:

  • By mail to the revaluation team, PO Box 774, Elizabethtown, NC 28337
  • In the marked box in the lobby of the tax office on E King Street
  • In the drop box in the lot behind the county courthouse

Formal appeals go to the board of equalization and review, which sits from the first Monday of April to the first Monday of May and, in a reappraisal year, finishes by December 1. After the board mails its ruling, the owner has 30 days to take it to the Property Tax Commission.

Tax rate and why values alone do not set your bill

The county rate is $.7850 per $100 of value, and the same 0.7850 shows for fiscal year 2026-27. Appraisal and rate are separate decisions. Values come first, then the commissioners fix the rate in June from the budget. A higher value by itself does not raise a bill.

Due dates and penalties

Bladen follows the state calendar. The statutory listing period runs through January 31.

February 1 onwardThree-fourths of a percent more each month

Exemptions and relief programs

Tax Administration sets two application deadlines:

  • June 1 is the cutoff for new elderly, disabled, disabled veteran and circuit breaker applications.
  • January 31 is the cutoff for new applications on everything else, including religious, charitable and present-use valuation.

For 2026, the income limit is $38,800 for the elderly or disabled exclusion and the circuit breaker, with $58,200 as the higher circuit breaker ceiling. The disabled veteran exclusion takes $45,000 off appraised value with no age or income test. An owner can use only one of the three programs, and the circuit breaker needs a fresh application each year.

Steps to take before you list

Start with the record card for your parcel, which shows the value, acreage and any buildings the county has on file. Check it for factual errors, since a mistaken square footage or a building that no longer stands is the easiest kind of appeal to win.

Next, ask Tax Administration whether any bill is unpaid, and whether the town portion applies if you live in East Arcadia, Bladenboro, White Lake or Elizabethtown. Get the payoff in writing so your closing attorney can plan around it.

Then confirm which value will apply when the sale closes. A deal that closes in 2026 uses the 2025 values for the bill, while anything that carries into the 2027 tax year uses the new reappraisal numbers. Tell your buyer which one applies so there are no surprises at settlement.

Selling with taxes owed

Before a deed is recorded in Bladen, taxes have to be accounted for. Either the filer completes a certification form, or a closing attorney prepares the deed and it states that any delinquent taxes will be paid by the attorney to the county tax collector when closing proceeds are disbursed.

That second route lets a house with back taxes close. The attorney pays the delinquent bills out of the sale money, and the deed then goes to the register. The seller also pays the $1.00 per $500 excise tax before recording.

A parcel that fails to sell at a county tax foreclosure auction becomes county property, and the county keeps a public list of those parcels. State law allows a deposit of up to 20% at the auction and a 10-day window for higher bids after the report of sale. Before confirmation, paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs redeems the property. If you are behind, a sale that closes before confirmation is the cleanest way out.

Frequently asked questions

How do I call Bladen County Tax Administration?

Dial 910-862-6730. Visits are at 201 E King Street in Elizabethtown, weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Why does my 2026 Bladen bill not reflect the new reappraisal?

The General Assembly postponed the reappraisal by a year for Bladen and eight other counties. Bills for 2026 use the 2025 values, and the new values start with the 2027 tax year.

Can I still appeal my Bladen County value?

The session laws allow appeals of 2026 values through December 31, 2026. A fresh notice for 2027 values should open the next round, so call the office to confirm your status.

When do Bladen homeowners apply for elderly, disabled or veteran tax relief?

New applications for those programs and the circuit breaker are due June 1 each year. Other exemptions and deferments, such as present-use value, are due January 31.

Can a Bladen County house with unpaid taxes still be sold?

Yes. The closing attorney pays the delinquent taxes to the county tax collector from your proceeds, and the deed says so. The sale has to close before the court confirms any tax foreclosure sale.

Brunswick County Tax Office contact

One office handles appraisal, assessment, ownership records and tax collection. It sits in the David R. Sandifer Administration Building, 30 Government Center Drive, Bolivia, NC 28422. The main number is 910-253-2829. For relief programs call 910-253-2811 on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m.

The tax office page on the county website links to tax bills, property record cards, certifications, the foreclosure list and land records. If you cannot pay a bill in one payment, the collections division offers a payment plan. Ask before the balance is late.

Housing and growth in Brunswick County

Brunswick County has grown fast. Population is 174,702 as of July 2025, up 27.8% from 136,695 in the April 2020 base. There are 116,023 housing units, and 84.6% are owner-occupied. The median home value is $349,800 and median gross rent is $1,351. Builders took out 4,457 permits in 2025, and each new house or addition can change a parcel's value before the next reappraisal.

Nineteen towns and villages levy their own rates, including Bolivia, Northwest, Leland, Navassa, Shallotte, Southport, Oak Island, Holden Beach, Ocean Isle Beach, Sunset Beach, Caswell Beach and Bald Head Island. The town where your parcel sits decides which town rate is added to the county rate.

Property tax rates

The county levies 0.3420, or 34.20 cents per $100 of value, and that rate is the same for 2024, 2025 and 2026. It was 0.485 in 2022 and fell to 0.342 in 2023, the year of the last countywide revaluation.

A Smithville Township rate of 0.04 and a few special districts, including two Bald Head Island zones, apply on top in their areas. Rates are set in late spring or early summer, so look at the county Tax Rates page after each budget vote. The next reappraisal year is 2027 and the last was 2023.

The 2027 revaluation and how to appeal

All parcels will be valued at market and in their condition on January 1, 2027. A building that is unfinished on that date is appraised at its percentage of completion.

New value notices are scheduled for February and March 2027. Compare yours with the record card and look for mistakes in the property data. An appeal has two stages:

  • Informal review: from January until the board of equalization and review convenes, the tax assessor can adjust a value when the facts support it.
  • Formal appeal: after the board convenes, it holds the authority, and owners or their representatives normally present their case in person.

Once the board has convened, any new appeal is treated as formal. After adjournment it is untimely and generally waits for the next year, and a win does not reach back to earlier years. G.S. 105-322 puts the board's first meeting between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May, with a December 1 finish in a reappraisal year. Beyond that sits the Property Tax Commission, which hears appeals filed within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

Due dates and interest

The due date is September 1. Nothing accrues until after January 5, or the next business day when that date lands on a weekend. This year's bills went out in mid-August, and paying by January 5, 2027 avoids interest.

From January 6 to February 1 a late bill carries 2%. After that it grows by three-fourths of a percent every month or fraction of a month. Mailed checks count as on time by postmark. A prepayment discount is possible when the board sets a schedule by May 1, so ask whether this year has one.

The tax claim attaches as of the January 1 listing date, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure suit.

Exemptions and relief programs

The county lists four programs. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, can claim the elderly or disabled exclusion on their permanent home if income stays under $38,800 for 2026. The county subtracts $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is larger.

  • Disabled veteran exclusion: a flat $45,000 comes off the appraisal with no age or income test, and an unmarried surviving spouse may claim it too.
  • Homestead circuit breaker: yearly tax cannot exceed 4% of income, or 5% when income is over the limit but within 150% of it. The overage is deferred and carries a lien.
  • Present-use value: farm, horticultural or forest land that qualifies is taxed on what it produces rather than on market value.

If the owner dies, transfers the property or moves out, three years of deferred circuit breaker tax plus interest come due, so a sale triggers that bill. Use the state application form and file it with the county tax office, preferably in January. Filings are taken through June 1.

Taxes and a Brunswick County house sale

By county resolution, a deed must be stamped by the tax office before the Register of Deeds will record it. The stamp shows that taxes, fees and assessments are paid.

To learn what is owed, ask for a Tax Certification under G.S. 105-361. Owners, attorneys and other interested persons can request one. It lists local tax liens, any deferred taxes, fire fees and assessments the office must collect, so ask for it early.

The seller also sends the register the deed tax, $1.00 for every $500 of consideration, before the deed is filed.

Before you list a Brunswick County house

Get your property record card from the county site and read it line by line: square footage, bedroom count, outbuildings. Then order a Tax Certification so you know about liens, deferred taxes, fire fees and assessments before an offer comes in.

If you receive relief, ask the relief line at 910-253-2811 what will come due at closing. A buyer's attorney will see the stamp requirement, so have the tax office stamp ready ahead of the closing date.

If taxes go unpaid: the county auction

A parcel with unpaid taxes may be sold at auction on the courthouse steps in Bolivia, whatever the weather. The high bidder puts down 5% right away, by cash, certified or cashier's check or money order. The county offers no financing.

Then a 10-day upset period opens, and every raise must top the prior bid by 5% or $750, whichever is greater. The winner gets a week after notice to pay the balance and is issued a commissioner's deed. A homeowner can still sell and pay the taxes at closing while the process is pending, so call the collections division early if you are behind.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call at the Brunswick County Tax Office?

Call 910-253-2829 for the Tax Office or 910-253-2811 for relief programs. The office is at 30 Government Center Drive in Bolivia.

What is the county tax rate in Brunswick County?

The county rate is 0.3420 for 2024, 2025 and 2026, with town or district rates added where they apply.

When does the next Brunswick County revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2027, with notices scheduled between February and March 2027. The prior revaluation was effective January 1, 2023.

Is there a grace period on late Brunswick County tax bills?

Not after January 5. Interest begins the next day, and the collections division can arrange a payment plan if you call before the deadline.

Do sellers need a tax stamp before recording in Brunswick County?

Yes. By county resolution the tax office must stamp a deed before the Register of Deeds records it, which confirms taxes, fees and assessments are settled.

Which Buncombe County offices handle my tax bill?

One department, Tax Assessment, covers the whole cycle from its building at 182 College Street in Asheville. It is open weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. The assessor lists, appraises and assesses property, while the collector bills and collects.

Each desk has its own number, so dial the one that fits your question.

  • Real estate values and appeal forms: 828-250-4940
  • Payments, balances and payment plans: 828-250-4910
  • Senior, disability and veteran relief: 828-250-4915
  • Business and personal property: 828-250-4930
  • Land records: 828-250-4970

Typing an address into tax.buncombenc.gov brings up the property record card, the bill and the appeal request. Print the record card before you list, so you can compare its details with the house. If you plan to sell, ask the collections desk for the balance on your parcel before you choose a closing date.

Why 2026 Buncombe bills use 2021 values

A law passed by the General Assembly in July 2026 makes the county hold off on its new values until January 1, 2027. Bills for 2026 therefore rest on the schedule from the 2021 reappraisal, even though the county had finished a reappraisal as of January 1, 2026 and mailed owners their new numbers.

Two measures were involved. S.B. 889 (S.L. 2026-8) delayed the schedule for a short list of counties that includes Buncombe. S.B. 474 (S.L. 2026-47) offered a way out through a revenue-neutral rate, which the county said would round to 40 cents. Commissioners chose to stay on the old values and a higher rate so the budget approved on June 2, 2026 would stand.

For most owners nothing moved. Unless you built or altered something, your value matches last year's, and last year's value already carried any Tropical Storm Helene adjustment. Mailed bills ran late, with most residential bills posted online first.

Rates on a 2026 Buncombe County bill

The county levy is 61.54 cents on each $100 of value, and the districts below add their own. Your parcel's address decides which of them apply.

The county assigns values for every town and district inside it, so the delay reached those units too. The 40-cent option applied only to the county's own rate. City and town rates come from their own governing boards, so read the lines on your bill.

Payment dates and options

A bill is normally due September 1, and the county lets owners pay through the following January 5 without a penalty. For the 2026 bills, that final penalty-free day is January 5, 2027.

Once that date passes, state law charges 2% interest from January 6 through February 1, then three quarters of one percent per month or partial month. The postmark date is the payment date for anything mailed.

If you need more time, Tax Collections offers a Casual Payment Plan or a Preauthorized Debit Payment Plan. Enrolled owners are not subject to wage or bank account garnishment. Call 828-250-4910 and ask for a collection specialist.

How to contest your Buncombe County value

There are two routes: an informal review by Property Assessment, or a formal hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review. An appeal of the value on the current bill can be filed through December 31, 2026.

To start online, enter your address at tax.buncombenc.gov, pick View Parcel, then Tax Appeal Request. A mailed form is available from 828-250-4940. Over 16,000 appeals came in on the 2026 reappraisal values, and the county is holding the unresolved ones for the 2027 reappraisal, so nobody has to refile unless a decision came back and they disagree.

  • Under G.S. 105-322 the board may lower, raise or confirm a value after hearing evidence.
  • Ask for the hearing before the board adjourns; a decision notice mailed late gives you 15 days from its mailing.
  • The board mails its ruling within a month of adjourning.
  • Beyond that, notify the Property Tax Commission in writing within 30 days of the mailed ruling.

Relief programs for owners

Buncombe administers the three programs set up by state law. Applications are open from January 1 through June 1, and a household can use only one program at a time.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: for owners aged 65 and up, or totally and permanently disabled, whose income is at or below the cap ($38,800 for 2026). It protects $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, whichever is larger.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value is removed, and no age or income test applies.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is limited to 4% of income, or 5% when income is over the cap but no higher than $58,200 for 2026. Whatever exceeds the limit is deferred, liened, and due when the owner sells or leaves.

The county warns that online videos describe a federal senior property tax exemption that does not exist, and it asks older owners to use only its official applications. Its General Assistance Program, described at buncombenc.gov/gap, offers short-term help with housing and utility costs.

Selling with taxes owed

The debt follows the parcel, so it is paid from the proceeds at or before closing. By state law the lien attaches on the date property is listed each year, with penalties, interest and costs added. The county can enforce it by filing a foreclosure suit where the land is located.

Call Tax Collections at 828-250-4910 for the payoff figure before fixing a closing date, and share it with your closing attorney so it is built into the settlement statement. If you hold a circuit breaker deferral, expect that balance to come due on the sale. A buyer's attorney will also want proof that the account is paid before the deed goes to the register of deeds at 205 College Street.

Owners with an open appeal should keep the paperwork handy, since the outcome applies to the 2027 value that the next buyer will see.

Housing context for Buncombe sellers

Buncombe's July 2025 population estimate was 277,417 in 142,799 housing units. The median owner-occupied home is $391,800, and 66.2% of homes are owned. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,785 a month, owners without one pay $505, and renters pay a median $1,362 in gross rent. Residents aged 65 or older make up 23.2%, and many in that group may qualify for the state relief programs above.

Frequently asked questions

What rate does Buncombe County charge on 2026 bills?

The county levy is 61.54 cents per $100 of value on the 2021 schedule. Unified Fire District property adds 17.38 cents, and Asheville City Schools adds 11.75 cents.

When do Buncombe bills have to be paid?

September 1 is the usual due date, and no penalty applies through January 5 of the next year. Interest begins January 6.

Can I still protest my Buncombe County value?

Appeals of the current bill can be filed through December 31, 2026, at tax.buncombenc.gov or through 828-250-4940. Appeals already made on the 2026 values stay on hold for 2027.

Why is my 2026 Buncombe value unchanged?

A state law pushed the new reappraisal to 2027, so bills use the 2021 values. A change only shows up if you added or altered improvements.

Which Buncombe homeowners qualify for tax relief?

People 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled within the income cap, plus owners with a permanent and total service-connected disability. Applications run January 1 through June 1, and the exemptions desk is at 828-250-4915.

Burke County Tax Office contact and divisions

The Tax Office works out of the Burke Services Building, 110 North Green Street, Morganton, NC 28655, from 8 am until 5 pm each weekday. The phone is (828) 764-9430, letters go to PO Box 219, Morganton, NC 28680, and Collections takes email at collections@burkenc.org.

Three divisions split the work. Real Property appraises land and buildings and answers questions on values, revaluation and appeals. Personal and Business Property takes listings and forms for taxable equipment and business assets. Collections issues bills and accepts payment for the county plus the towns and fire districts the office serves, so one bill can carry several levies.

The office also publishes its deed certification form and a tax website at burkenctax.com. If you are selling, start with Collections, the division that certifies the amount owed on a parcel before a deed moves on to recording.

Burke County tax rate

Burke's own levy is 55.5 cents per $100 of assessed value, and the budget for fiscal 2026-2027, about $120.7 million, kept it there. That budget began July 1, 2026. The county has cut the rate twice since 2023.

Your bill may list more than the county line, because town and fire district charges go through the same office. Look at each rate line for the units covering your address. A rate multiplies a value, and values will shift once the 2027 revaluation project is done.

The 2027 revaluation

Burke County is carrying out a revaluation project for 2027. Commissioners hold a public hearing at the Burke Services Building on a proposed Schedule of Values and Present Use Schedule of Values, with copies posted online and at the tax office. Call the Tax Department at (828) 764-9430 with questions about the schedules.

State law (G.S. 105-286) sets an eight-year ceiling between reappraisals, each as of January 1. Larger counties, those with 75,000 residents or more, can be forced to reappraise early if their sales assessment ratio drops below .85 or climbs above 1.15. The review board gets until December 1 in a revaluation year, a longer runway than usual.

When your new notice comes, set it beside recent sales of comparable homes nearby before deciding whether to appeal.

Due dates and penalties

Bills fall due on September 1, with face-amount payment allowed until January 6.

Statutory dates in a Burke County tax year
EventDate or rule
Listing windowStarts on the first business day of January and ends January 31
Bill duePayable September 1 of the fiscal year

Each summer the county mails listing forms for owners to update, sign and send back. Returning them within the January window avoids a late listing penalty.

How to challenge your value

Talk to the Tax Office first. Anything unresolved goes to the review board, which is the commissioners unless the county has formed a special panel. Your request must be in hand before the panel adjourns.

  • A written request or a personal appearance both count.
  • If the board's own notice was mailed less than 15 days before adjourning, the clock gives you 15 days from that mailing.
  • The ruling arrives by mail within 30 days after adjournment.
  • Past that sits the Property Tax Commission, which takes a written notice listing your grounds, with a copy to the assessor.

If your house has unrepaired storm damage, tell the Tax Office. Ask what relief is open to your parcel now.

Certification required before a deed is recorded

Burke uses a Delinquent Tax Certification form built on G.S. 161-31, which lets commissioners instruct the register of deeds to turn away a transfer deed until the collector certifies there are no delinquent taxes. The form was revised April 22, 2026.

You supply the parcel number, the seller and buyer names, the buyer's mailing address, the site address, the price and the acreage. The form also asks if a mobile home or personal property, such as vehicles, boats or farm equipment, goes with the sale, and whether land in Present Use Value will stay enrolled. Staff then complete a ten-year grid of deferred and due taxes.

Send it to the Office of the Tax Administrator, PO Box 219, Morganton, or to collections@burkenc.org. A closing attorney often files it, though asking Collections for a figure before you list can save days.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Burke County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property tax breaks

The state's three programs apply here, filed on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, and applications must be accepted through June 1. An owner may draw on one program only.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes whichever is greater, $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent residence, for an owner at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled whose prior-year income stays within the 2026 cap of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4% of income, or 5% where income runs up to $58,200, once the owner has lived in the home five years.

Circuit breaker savings are deferred, and the tax deferred over the three prior years falls due on a transfer, an owner's death or a move out. Mention any such deferral to your closing attorney.

Selling a Burke County home: tax steps

Begin by calling Collections at (828) 764-9430 for the amount owed on the parcel, including any town or fire district levy. Next, decide who will file the Delinquent Tax Certification. Your closing attorney usually does, but you can send it yourself to PO Box 219 or collections@burkenc.org with the parcel number, the buyer and seller names, the price and the acreage.

If land is in Present Use Value, say whether the buyer will keep it enrolled, since the form asks. If you have a circuit breaker deferral, expect the deferred tax from the three prior years to come due at the sale. Once the collector certifies that nothing delinquent remains, the register of deeds can accept the deed.

Housing in Burke County

Growth is slow. The mid-2025 population is 88,655, up just 1.2% from the 2020 base and below the 90,912 counted in 2010. The county has 41,669 housing units, and 74.5% of homes are owner-occupied with a median value of $185,400. Median gross rent is $884, and 588 building permits were issued in 2025. At that price level, back taxes or a certification delay can hold up a closing, so ask Collections for your balance early.

Frequently asked questions

What is Burke County's rate per $100?

It is 55.5 cents, unchanged for 2026-2027, plus any town or fire district charges that reach your parcel.

Where can I pay a Burke County bill?

Go to 110 North Green Street in Morganton during weekday office hours, call (828) 764-9430, or email collections@burkenc.org.

When does interest start on Burke County bills?

Interest starts January 6, since payment before that date is at face amount. It is 2% through February 1 and 3/4 of 1% a month after.

Is Burke County revaluing property?

Yes, a 2027 revaluation is under way, and state law demands reappraisal at least every eighth year. Call the Tax Department at (828) 764-9430 about the proposed schedules.

Do I need tax certification to sell in Burke County?

Yes, the county's Delinquent Tax Certification lets the collector confirm nothing delinquent remains before the deed goes on record. Request it at collections@burkenc.org or (828) 764-9430.

How Cabarrus County values and bills a house

Cabarrus appraises each parcel at market value on January 1. One bill then goes to the owner, combining the county rate with any city, town and fire district rates for the address. Current values date from January 1, 2024, and no flat percentage was applied to earlier assessments.

A parcel's value is built from the land, the building (type, age and physical traits) and extras such as garages, sheds, pools, fences and driveways. A structure still going up is valued by how complete it is on January 1, and that figure goes into the bill.

The ceiling in G.S. 105-286 is eight years between reappraisals. Cabarrus halved that interval, so values track the market more closely.

Who to contact about assessments and appeals

The Tax Administration department handles assessment and appeals, and the Revaluation office answers value questions at 704-920-2126 or revalinfo@cabarruscounty.us. Visit 65 Church Street S in Concord, NC 28025, any weekday between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.

Collections bills on behalf of the county, seven cities or towns and 16 fire districts. The Equalization and Review Board takes appeals; the County Commissioners appoint its members from residents who know the local market.

  • Values and property cards: search online by owner name, address or parcel
  • Comparable sales: use the map tool on the Tax Revaluation page
  • Relief: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker, along with present use value and wildlife conservation
  • Payment plans: ask Collections

How to appeal your Cabarrus County value

Begin with a written request for informal review. You do not need a special form, but attached evidence strengthens the case. The appraiser covering your area reviews what you send and replies with an Informal Review notice that also explains how to move to the formal level.

From the date of that notice you have 30 days to carry the appeal forward. To ask for a hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review, write to Cabarrus County Tax Revaluation, PO Box 707, Concord, NC 28026-0707, or file through the county's online system. The assessor's office must receive it within 30 days of the date printed on your Notice of Real Estate Assessed Value, or at any point before the Board adjourns. Adjournment usually comes in late April, and the local newspaper carries the date.

Once you submit, you and the county appraiser get one more look at the case, and you fill out an Application for Hearing. The board listens to both sides, and its decision letter follows by mail within a month of the hearing. A disagreement that survives the board goes to the NC Property Tax Commission. G.S. 105-290 requires a written notice of appeal with your grounds, filed 30 days or less after the ruling was mailed.

The county does not accept a large increase from one revaluation to the next as grounds. Build your case from comparable sales.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Cabarrus County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and penalties

Payment is due September 1. Once January 5 of the next year goes by, an unpaid bill is delinquent. Mailing happens once a year, in late July or the first days of August, for real estate, business and personal property alike.

A year on the Cabarrus County tax calendar
WhenWhat happens
January 1Parcels are valued, and the owner on this date gets the bill
JanuaryListing form for personal property opens, and real estate changes go on it
Late AprilReview board usually wraps up
By June 30Rates fixed through the budget
Late July to early AugustBills mailed
September 1Taxes due
After January 5Delinquent, so collection or foreclosure can follow

The interest rule in G.S. 105-360 adds 2 percent from January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for every month that follows. A delinquent bill can lead to collection actions or tax foreclosure. A payment plan is available from Collections if you ask for it, ideally early in the year, yet the whole bill must still be paid by the delinquent date.

Cabarrus County tax rates

For 2026 the county charges $0.576 per $100 of assessed value. Cities, towns and fire districts layer their own rates over that, and an address inside Kannapolis, for instance, picks up another $0.5595.

Budget season produces the rates: the Board of Commissioners and each municipality finish theirs by June 30. A new assessed value does not by itself tell you what the bill will do, because that depends on the rates. For your own estimate, take the assessed value from the real estate search, add up the rates for every district covering the parcel, and have Collections check the result.

Tax breaks for Cabarrus County homeowners

Cabarrus has three relief programs on the county's list: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker. You pick only one, and the application form, AV-9, goes to the county assessor by June 1 ahead of the tax year. Present use value for farm, forest and wildlife land is handled separately with its own applications.

  • Homestead (G.S. 105-277.1): open to an owner at least 65, or totally and permanently disabled, whose income is below $38,800 for 2026. The county leaves out $25,000 of value or half the appraisal, whichever is more.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of value drops out of the bill. The state form sets no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: after five years in the home, your tax is held to 4.0% of income, or to 5.0% if income lands above the cap but no higher than $58,200 for 2026. Savings are deferred and secured by a lien.

Who pays the bill when you sell

Settle this year's bill out of your sale proceeds, which is what G.S. 105-355 contemplates. Billing follows ownership on the first of January, so a seller who closes mid-year should forward the bill to the buyer.

Owner-occupied homes in the county have a median value of $354,800, and 71.2 percent are lived in by their owners. The real estate search shows values set as of January 1, 2024, so look at recent neighborhood sales before you list. Your closing attorney should get a payoff for all taxes due, fire district amounts included. Ask Collections whether any earlier year is delinquent.

A seller's tax checklist

Pull your property card from the real estate search and check the land, building and extras the county has on file. Look at the comparable sales tool to see how nearby homes sold. Ask Collections for the current year's balance and any prior-year delinquency. If you receive homestead or circuit breaker relief, tell your closing attorney, since a deferral can come due. Last, confirm which bill goes to the buyer after closing, because the county issues it to whoever owned the parcel on January 1.

Frequently asked questions

When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?

September 1. A bill is past due if not paid before the following January 5, and state law starts interest on January 6. Bills are mailed in late July or the first days of August.

How often does Cabarrus County revalue real estate?

Every four years by local choice, although state law only requires every eight. The current values are as of January 1, 2024. The Revaluation office at 704-920-2126 can confirm the next cycle.

How do I appeal my Cabarrus County property value?

Submit a written request for an informal review, then appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review within 30 days of your value notice or before the board adjourns, usually in late April. The decision letter arrives within 30 days of the hearing.

Does Cabarrus County allow installments on a tax bill?

Yes. The Collections office works with taxpayers on payment plans, but you must request one and the bill still has to be paid in full by the delinquent date. Contacting them early in the year is preferred.

Who gets the bill if my Cabarrus County house sells before year end?

The bill still goes out in the name of the owner on January 1, so forward it to the buyer if you receive it after closing. Settle the current year's tax through closing so it does not turn into a lien problem for the new owner.

Caldwell County at a glance

Caldwell County is foothills country in the state's northwest, with Lenoir as its seat. Population was estimated at 81,105 on July 1, 2025, living in 38,057 housing units. Owners occupy 73.5% of the homes, and the 2020-2024 middle value for an owned home is $192,200.

Nine municipalities touch the county: Lenoir, Hudson, Granite Falls, Cedar Rock, Cajahs Mountain, Gamewell, Sawmills, and parts of Blowing Rock and Rhodhiss. The town your parcel falls in changes the bill, since each one sets its own rate and a couple set none.

Tax Office location and hours

The Tax Office is at 905 West Avenue NW, Lenoir, NC 28645. Hours run 8 to 5 on weekdays, with weekends and federal holidays off. By mail, write to PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645. The main number is 828-757-1340, and listing questions can go to 828-757-1320.

The office lists personal property and business property, bills and collects the tax, and runs revaluation. For a home sale you care about three things: the assessed value of the real estate, whether any year's bill is delinquent, and whether the owner is enrolled in a relief program. The county advertises tax liens on real property once bills go unpaid, and the commissioners authorized advertising of 2024 liens at their February 2025 meeting.

Payment deadline and interest

Bills are due September 1. After that, a bill still unpaid on January 6 of the next year picks up 2 percent interest, and three-fourths of a percent more for every month it stays open. Timeliness is judged by the U.S. Postal Service postmark, and postage-meter dates are refused.

Practical points on paying:

  • You may pay part of the bill any time between its arrival and January 6.
  • Online payment takes American Express, Discover, Mastercard, Visa or a PayPal account, and PayPal's processing fees are not kept by the county.
  • Escrow does not redirect the bill away from you. If your lender should be paying it, ask the lender.
  • Personal property bills such as boats and unlicensed vehicles are mailed in July.

The 2026 rate chart also shows a discount of 2.00 for July and 1.00 for August. G.S. 105-360 lets a county adopt a prepayment discount schedule approved by the Department of Revenue, so ask the Tax Office how the discount is applied before you count on it.

2026 tax rates

The county rate for 2026 is 0.4666, and a town or district adds its own line. Rates are quoted per $100 of assessed value. Lenoir is 0.4600, with a separate downtown district at 0.1800, and fire and rescue districts add further lines for rural parcels.

Selected 2026 rates, per $100 of assessed value

A household solid waste fee of 22.75 applies, or 17.75 for city households. Rural fire districts run from 0.0430 for Bethlehem to 0.1415 for South Caldwell, so the district your house sits in changes the bill. The Tax Office can tell you which fire and rescue districts include your parcel.

The 2025 revaluation

Caldwell County reappraised all real property for 2025, after its sales-assessment ratio fell below the 0.85 level that triggers a reappraisal under state law. The prior revaluation took effect January 1, 2021. The point of a reappraisal is to give every taxpayer equal, uniform values.

County staff appraised residential property, and a third party handled commercial and industrial property. Many owners saw large jumps in assessed value, and commissioners talked about cutting the rate toward revenue neutral. If you plan to sell, compare the assessed value on your bill with what buyers are offering.

State law sets an eight-year outer limit under G.S. 105-286. A county of 75,000 residents or more must move up its reappraisal if the sales ratio slips under .85 or climbs over 1.15, which is what happened here.

How to appeal your assessment

Begin with the informal review. The Board of Equalization and Review hears a case only after that step. Return the Informal Review Form, and back it with a recent fee appraisal tied to local sales, or a comparison of similar homes by year built, size, construction and acreage. The county advises against paying for an independent appraisal unless you truly need one.

The Board of Equalization and Review is the formal body, and anyone still unhappy after it can go to the NC Property Tax Commission. Under G.S. 105-322, the board first meets between early April and early May, and your hearing request has to reach it before it adjourns. The Caldwell board has five members and four alternates, who must have lived in the county at least two years.

Personal property is separate. Appeals of individual or business personal property values go in writing to the Caldwell County Assessor's Office, PO Box 2200, Lenoir, NC 28645, within 30 days of the tax bill date. Business listings that miss the January 31 deadline without an approved extension carry a 10 percent penalty on the total tax.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Caldwell County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exclusions and relief programs

Caldwell County follows the state's three programs, and the county tax site has a relief brochure and an application. Elderly or disabled owners can use the exclusion in G.S. 105-277.1 which shelters the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of a home's appraised value. The 2026 income cap is $38,800.

A separate disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of appraised value. The circuit breaker caps tax at 4.0 or 5.0 percent of income, with a 2026 upper threshold of $58,200. Form AV-9 is the application, filed with the county assessor. The county must accept it through June 1 ahead of the tax year. Owners cannot combine the three programs.

If you own improvements, report new buildings and additions during January, with your cost and the percent complete on January 1. Report demolished improvements too.

Selling with the tax bill still open

The bill goes to whoever owned the property on January 1. If you closed after that date, pass the bill to the buyer. The lien attaches as of January 1 under G.S. 105-355, so the closing attorney should settle the current year and any open prior years.

Get a written payoff from the Tax Office, and look at which town or fire district appears on the bill, since the combined charge differs from parcel to parcel. If the house was inherited or has back years unpaid, get the full list of open years before you accept an offer. Delinquent taxes are collected through foreclosure. A cash sale has no lender payoff to coordinate, though the tax lien still gets cleared at the closing table.

Frequently asked questions

When are Caldwell County property taxes due?

September 1 of the tax year. Interest begins January 6 of the following year at 2 percent, then three-fourths of one percent a month until paid, and the county uses the U.S. Postal postmark, not a meter date.

Where do I pay or ask about my Caldwell County tax bill?

Go to 905 West Avenue NW in Lenoir any weekday from 8 to 5, or phone 828-757-1340. Online payment works by credit card or PayPal, and the processing fees go to PayPal rather than the county.

When did Caldwell County last revalue property?

The county reappraised real property for 2025, and before that a revaluation took effect on January 1, 2021. State law caps the gap at eight years, and a low sales ratio of under .85 can force it sooner.

How do I appeal a Caldwell County real estate value?

Return the informal review form with comparable sales or an appraisal. If you disagree with the result, request a hearing from the Board of Equalization and Review before it adjourns. From there the NC Property Tax Commission takes appeals filed within 30 days of the mailed board decision.

If I sold my Caldwell County house after January 1, who gets the bill?

The January 1 owner is billed, so forward a copy to the buyer. The county tries to notify the new owner but asks sellers to help.

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Carteret County, NC Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Carteret County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Which Carteret County office handles property tax?

Assessing and collecting both run through one Tax Administration office under an appointed Tax Administrator. The commissioners make the appointment. Office staff also serve the review board that hears value appeals.

Walk-in service is on the first floor of the Administration Building, 302 Courthouse Square in Beaufort, and at a Western Office at 701 Cedar Point Blvd., Cedar Point, NC 28584. The phone is 252-728-8485. Hours at both are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, holidays excepted.

The office handles appraisal, assessment, billing and collection on real, business and personal property. Before listing, ask it what is owed on your parcel and whether a relief claim is on file.

Due dates and interest

September 1 is the due date. Interest waits until January 6 of the following year. It starts at 2% for January and adds 0.75% each month after.

Key dates and rules
EventDate or rule
Taxes dueSeptember 1
Last day without interestJanuary 5
Interest starts2% for January, then 0.75% a month
Personal property value appealOne month from the date on the bill
Delinquent lien advertisementPublished between March 1 and June 30

Carteret's fiscal year 2026-27 rate is 22.5 cents for every $100 of assessed value. Real and personal property get separate bills. Property in Beaufort, Bogue, Cape Carteret, Cedar Point, Emerald Isle, Morehead City or Peletier gets one bill with county and town tax combined. Mailed checks are credited by postmark.

How to appeal your assessed value

Send the Real Property Appeal Form to the Tax Administration Office within the window on your value notice. A reappraisal notice gives you 30 days from the date it carries. The appeal covers assessed value alone; the rate and the bill itself are off the table.

The last general reappraisal used a January 1, 2025 market value. Compare your property's characteristics and nearby sales against what the county used. The assessor is presumed to have acted in good faith, so the burden is yours. Useful evidence includes sales of similar nearby homes, damage photos and repair quotes.

  • First level: the Board of Equalization and Review, nine local residents counting two alternates, which mails its Notice of Decision within a month of meeting.
  • Second level: the state Property Tax Commission. File within 30 days after that notice. Hearings are typically in Raleigh, and a lawyer may be needed.
  • Third level: the North Carolina Court of Appeals, only on a question of law, and then the state Supreme Court.

Boats, aircraft, mobile homes and business equipment take a different path. Your clock is 30 days from the annual bill's date. The county then sets a conference and rules afterward. The result can go down, up or stay put, and it applies only from that year onward. G.S. 105-290 sets the 30-day window to reach the Property Tax Commission.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Carteret County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Property tax relief for owners

North Carolina offers three ways to cut a home's bill, and an owner can take only one. Apply at the county tax office.

  • Age or disability: you need to be 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, with 2026 income of $38,800 or less. The reduction is $25,000 or one half of value, whichever is greater.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: a disabled veteran who qualifies, or an unmarried surviving spouse, has $45,000 of the home's appraised value excluded, whatever the age or income.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is held to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% when income is above $38,800 and no more than $58,200. Qualifying takes five years of owning and living in the house. Tax above the cap is deferred rather than erased.

The application is Form AV-9. File it during the January listing period if you can, because the assessor must accept it until June 1. Renew a circuit breaker claim every year. If you sell, die or move out, three years of deferred tax come due. Read the full rules at G.S. 105-277.1, 105-277.1B and 105-277.1C.

How can I pay a Carteret County tax bill?

Payment options are the web portal, the phone line, the mail and the counter. The portal accepts cards, eCheck and PayPal. The line at 1-888-544-9433 takes card payments if you have the bill in hand.

  • Mail: a check payable to County of Carteret, sent to PO Box 96264, Charlotte, NC 28296-6264.
  • Counter: at the Beaufort or Cedar Point office, with cash, check, money order or card.
  • Drop box: at the courthouse entrance, no cash, processed the next business day.

Card fees apply: a $1.50 flat charge for an eCheck and 2.50% plus $0.30 a transaction on credit cards. Partial payments in any amount are allowed online, but the full balance must be in before delinquency, and the phone line does not take partial amounts. If a full payment is out of reach, a hardship payment arrangement is available by application. Interest keeps running under it, but it may lower the odds of garnishment or foreclosure.

What happens when taxes go unpaid?

The lien stays on the parcel, interest keeps growing, and the county can use enforcement tools. G.S. 105-355 creates the parcel lien as of the listing date, and the penalties, interest and costs stick to it.

Tools include wage and bank garnishment, state income tax refund setoff, setoff against lottery winnings, attachment of rent, seizure and sale of personal property, and foreclosure on real property. Foreclosure under G.S. 105-374 resembles a mortgage foreclosure and ends at an auction on the courthouse steps, followed by a commissioner's report and a ten-day window for higher bids. An owner can still redeem before confirmation by paying the full amount.

A sale ahead of that is usually the cleaner exit. Once a delinquent account is advertised, the foreclosure process moves forward. If you are behind, call 252-728-8485 before the March 1 to June 30 publication period.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Carteret County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a Carteret County home with taxes owed

A tax balance follows the parcel as a lien, so it is normally cleared at closing. Get a current payoff number from the Tax Administration Office. Then work out with the closing attorney how this year's bill is split.

Recording the deed is its own errand at the register of deeds, described on the Carteret County register of deeds page. A circuit breaker deferral on the property comes due on a transfer, covering the three prior years.

A practical order for a sale: phone 252-728-8485 or stop at the Beaufort counter, ask for the balance on each bill tied to the parcel, and learn whether the town added its share to a combined bill. Then tell your closing attorney about any appeal still open or any relief claim on file, because those change the number. In a cash sale the buyer skips a lender's escrow setup, so the tax figure is simply paid out of your proceeds on the closing date. Keep the receipts and the closing statement with your records.

The county had 70,469 residents on July 1, 2025, in 54,293 housing units. The 2020-2024 median for an owned home is $333,300, with owners living in 74.7% of units.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Carteret County property tax rate?

The 2026-27 county rate is 22.5 cents per $100. Parcels inside a town add the town rate and arrive on one combined bill.

When do Carteret County taxes become delinquent?

On January 6, after the September 1 due date. Pay by January 5 and no interest is owed. After that, 2% applies for January and 0.75% for each month beyond.

What is the deadline to contest a Carteret County assessment?

Thirty days, counted from the value change notice for real property and from the bill date for personal property. Only value can be challenged.

Where do I pay my Carteret County tax bill in person?

Walk in at Beaufort or at the Western Office in Cedar Point. Both keep weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. A drop box at the courthouse entrance accepts checks.

Can Carteret County set up a payment plan?

Yes, in limited cases. The county offers a hardship payment arrangement by application and lets owners pay in partial amounts before delinquency. Interest still accrues under a plan.

Tax Office and related contacts

The Caswell County Tax Office takes listings, exemption forms and bill payments from the courthouse at 139 E. Church Street, Yanceyville. Write to PO Box 204, Yanceyville, NC 27379, or call (336) 694-4194 ext. 5116. It keeps weekday hours of eight to five.

Cards can be used through an outside payment service, with a fee that rises along with the tax amount. Bill numbers begin with R for real estate or P for personal property, and you leave off the zero that follows the letter when you type the number in. The county home page has a Pay A Tax Bill link to an online bill search.

Two other offices matter when you sell. The Register of Deeds is downstairs in the same courthouse complex at (336) 694-4197. The county GIS office, at (336) 694-4194 ext. 115, matches parcels to maps. Before anything else, phone the tax office for a payoff on any open bill.

Rates and revaluation schedule

For property listed as of January 1, 2025, Caswell levies 62.7 cents per $100 of value. Values were reset by the reappraisal that took effect January 1, 2024, and 2028 is the next one on the state schedule.

Caswell County rates, fees and schedule
Charge or dateAmount
County rate, 2025-26.6270 per $100 (62.7 cents)
