Solid waste disposal fee$75 where no town or private collection proof is furnished

Ten fire districts exist: Anderson, Casville, Cherry Grove, Leasburg, Milton, Pelham, Prospect Hill, Providence, Semora and Yanceyville. Your address falls in one of them, and the tax office can give you the combined charge for it.

For the current year's rate, call the tax office or open the budget ordinance on the county home page.

How to appeal an assessment

A disagreement over value is heard by the county's board of equalization and review. Get its meeting dates and the appeal form from the tax office before the spring session starts. The calendar comes from state law:

  • The board's opening session lands somewhere from the first April Monday to the first May Monday.
  • Outside a reappraisal year the board wraps up about three Mondays after opening and generally stops by July 1. In a reappraisal year it has until December 1.
  • Request a hearing before adjournment, in writing or by showing up. A decision notice mailed late in the session extends your window by 15 days from the mailing.
  • Its written decision is mailed within 30 days after it adjourns.
  • Still unhappy? The next step is a written notice of appeal to the Property Tax Commission, copied to the county assessor and mailed within 30 days of the board's decision date.

Because the 2024 reappraisal is the latest, the next large wave of appeals is tied to 2028. In between, a value usually moves only after a physical change to the property, a clerical error or a change in permitted use, so a quiet-year appeal should name one of those.

The state's January 1, 2025 sales ratio study showed a median ratio of 104.97 for the county. A value that looks high calls for evidence: recent nearby sales of comparable houses, plus dated photos of any defects that existed on January 1.

Homestead exclusions and deferment

Pick one of three state homestead programs; they cannot be combined. The application is Form AV-9, filed at the county tax office, which must accept it until June 1 before the tax year.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes $25,000 or half of the appraised value from the taxable amount, whichever is more. Qualifying owners are 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, and had income under the cap last year. The 2026 cap is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: waives $45,000 of appraised value whatever the applicant's age or income. Form NCDVA-9 is filled out with a county veteran service officer first.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: owners under the income cap pay no more than 4 percent of income, and those earning up to 150 percent of the cap ($58,200 for 2026) pay no more than 5 percent. A fresh application is due every year.

One catch for sellers: deferred tax is a lien, and transferring the property makes the deferrals of the previous three fiscal years payable. A house that used the deferment carries an extra payoff on the closing statement.

The tax office page links the state's exemption, exclusion and present-use value forms, as well as business personal property listing forms.

Taxes owed at closing

Tax follows the land, which is why an unpaid balance is cleared out of the sale proceeds. A year's lien attaches by statute on the January 1 listing date, with penalties, interest and costs added later.

Bills are due September 1 and cost face value until January 6. Then the charge is 2 percent through the end of January and three-fourths of a percent per month, or part of a month, after that. A seller with an open prior-year bill takes those charges to the closing table.

The deed adds its own charges. The register collects the state conveyance excise tax from the seller before recording: $1.00 for each $500 of price or fraction. Statute fixes the recording fees at $26 for an ordinary instrument's first 15 pages and $64 for a deed of trust's first 35.

What to bring or ask for: the bill number for each parcel, written payoff figures for every open year, and the fire district shown on the bill. If you used the circuit breaker, ask for the deferred balance as a separate number. Your closing attorney puts each amount on the settlement statement, and the deed is recorded once the excise tax is paid. A cash sale skips a lender's payoff letter, though the order is the same: tax first, then the deed.

If a bill sits unpaid long enough, the county can file a foreclosure suit like a lender's, ending with an auction at the courthouse door. Redemption stays open until confirmation, on payment of what is owed. Selling first is the cleaner route.

Caswell County at a glance

Few people live here: 53.5 per square mile in 2020. Yanceyville is the seat, with Milton the other town on the county website. The county had an estimated 22,563 residents on July 1, 2025, which is 0.8 percent fewer than in 2020.

Homes are inexpensive here. The median owned home was worth $164,500 across 2020-2024, and 75.2 percent of homes are occupied by owners. Residents 65 or older make up 25.4 percent, the group the elderly exclusion is built for.

County Environmental Health handles private septic permits, so a seller with a septic system can ask that office for the records on file.

Frequently asked questions

Which number reaches the Caswell County tax office?

Call (336) 694-4194 ext. 5116. The office is at 139 E. Church Street in Yanceyville, open Monday through Friday, eight to five. Keep your bill number handy and drop the zero after the R or P.

What is the Caswell County property tax rate?

Property listed as of January 1, 2025 is taxed at 62.7 cents on each $100. Fire district tax adds 3.3 cents in the Casville and County Fire Service districts, and solid waste fees are $55 and $75. The tax office has the current figure.

When is the next Caswell County revaluation?

The schedule shows 2028, following the reappraisal effective January 1, 2024. Counties must reappraise at least every eighth year and may choose shorter cycles. Confirm the date with the tax office, since schedules can move.

When are Caswell County property taxes due?

September 1. Pay before January 6 of the next year and you owe face value only. Later payments carry 2 percent interest at first, then three-fourths of a percent a month. Mailed payments are dated by postmark.

Is a sale possible with Caswell County tax still owed?

Yes. The full open amount, interest included, is deducted from your proceeds at closing. Pick your closing date only after you have a payoff figure, and find out whether a circuit breaker deferral means a second balance.

The Catawba County Tax Office

In Catawba County one office does the listing, appraising, assessing and collecting for all real and personal property. Call (828) 465-8414 with general questions and (828) 465-8436 to book a tax relief appointment. Relief applications can be mailed to Assessor's Office, Attn: Tax Relief, Box 368, Newton, NC 28658-0368.

If you are selling, this is where you get a written statement of what a parcel owes, find out whether a relief claim or deferment is on file, and learn which fire district or town your address belongs to. Have the parcel number or your bill ready, and have staff list each open year separately so nothing slips past closing.

The office has earned the Certificate of Excellence in Assessment Administration from the International Association of Assessing Officers. Your own bill depends on the parcel's value, the county rate, and the fire district or town where the parcel sits.

County, town and fire district rates

The county rate is .3985 per $100 of assessed value, and every parcel also pays either a fire district tax or a municipal tax. The county tax page prints the full list. Main figures are below.

A parcel inside a town or city pays that municipality's rate. A parcel outside pays the fire district rate that covers it. Check your bill or ask the tax office which applies, then add it to the county rate for the combined figure.

Revaluation and appeals

Catawba County revalues every four years. Values now in use date from January 1, 2023. The following countywide revaluation is effective January 1, 2027. State law requires one only every eight years, so the county moves twice as fast. Staff are studying sales and market trends for the 2027 round.

New appeals open after the 2027 notices go out, in January 2027. The path starts with an informal review and moves up only if that fails:

  • Once value notices go out, ask the tax office how to start an informal review, using the form enclosed with the notice.
  • When that fails, the county board of equalization and review is next. Ask for a hearing in writing or in person before adjournment.
  • After the board, the state Property Tax Commission hears appeals made by written notice within 30 days of the mailed ruling.

Revaluation updates values, not rates. The rate is set in the annual budget ordinance, usually finalized in June. An appeal can lower your value but cannot change the rate.

Property tax relief programs

Four programs are offered: the elderly or disabled homestead exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment, and AV-10 applications for other exclusions. An owner may pick only one of the first three.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: for owners who were 65 or disabled on January 1, own the home, live in the county and report income under the printed limit. The reduction is the greater of $25,000 or half the appraised value. A 65-plus applicant skips the disability certificate, and approval carries forward until you move, sell, rent, change the deed or go over the income limit.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: up to $45,000 of a permanent residence's assessed value is removed, and income is not tested. The county wants discharge papers plus VA certification of permanent, total, service-connected disability, or proof of specially adapted housing benefits.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: the bill is limited to 4 or 5 percent of income for owners with five or more years of living in and owning the home. The deferred part is a lien, repayable with interest for the current year and three earlier ones once the property transfers.

June 1 is the yearly cutoff for all three, and the circuit breaker needs a new application every year. The AV-10 for religious, charitable, historic and similar exclusions is filed in January. The 2026 income limit is $38,800, with $58,200 as the 150 percent mark for the circuit breaker.

Selling with taxes owed

Sale proceeds clear whatever tax is open. Each year's lien attaches on the January 1 listing date, and the bill is due September 1. Every parcel pays county tax plus a fire or town levy, so a Hickory payoff will not match one for a house in a rural fire district.

No interest is charged through January 5. From January 6 interest is 2 percent through January, and three-fourths of a percent for each month after.

Circuit breaker owners get the surprise: transferring the property is a disqualifying event, so the deferred amounts become payable at the sale. Ask the tax office for a statement showing the current bill and any deferred balance.

Deed charges belong to the Register of Deeds, a separate office, and the seller pays the state excise tax there before recording. Get the written tax statement first and hand it to your closing attorney, who builds the payoff into the settlement statement. A cash sale has no lender payoff to line up, yet the tax balance is still paid at closing.

Catawba County at a glance

Before listing, read your latest value notice and compare the assessed value with recent sales nearby. Buyers will study the new figures after the 2027 revaluation, so raise a value that looks too high through the informal review. Selling sooner? Expect a buyer's agent to ask about your current bill and the combined rate for your town or fire district.

The county seat uses Newton addresses, and Hickory, Conover, Claremont, Maiden, Long View, Catawba and Brookford are the other municipalities on the tax page. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 170,172 residents, in 77,827 housing units.

Of all homes, 72.2 percent are owner-occupied, and the 2020-2024 median home value is $241,600.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Catawba County property tax rate?

The county rate is .3985 per $100. Each parcel adds either a fire district rate or a town or city rate (.46 in Hickory, .45 in Newton, for instance), and the two together make the combined rate.

When do Catawba County property values change next?

January 1, 2027 is the date of the next countywide revaluation, following the one effective January 1, 2023. Catawba County revalues every four years, and appeals open once notices are mailed.

Which phone line handles Catawba County tax relief?

Call (828) 465-8436 to book a tax relief appointment, or (828) 465-8414 for general questions. Applications can be mailed to Assessor's Office, Attn: Tax Relief, Box 368, Newton, NC 28658-0368. The homestead deadline is June 1.

Do I have to pay off deferred circuit breaker taxes when I sell?

Yes. A sale ends the deferment, and this year's deferred tax plus the previous three years' becomes payable with interest. Ask the tax office for the balance ahead of closing so the proceeds can cover it.

Is a disabled veteran exclusion available in Catawba County?

Yes, with no income limit. Up to $45,000 of a permanent residence's assessed value is excluded. The applicant needs discharge proof and VA certification of permanent, total service-connected disability, and June 1 is the deadline.

Selling in Chatham County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Chatham County?

Which Chatham County office does what on property tax?

Tax Administration is split into a Listing Division, an Appraisal Division and a Collections Division. The Listing Division is at 12 East Street in Pittsboro, on the ground floor of the government annex facing the Pittsboro traffic circle. Its public counter operates on weekdays, eight to five. Mail goes to PO Box 908, Pittsboro, NC 27312, and the listing line is 919-542-8250.

Questions about what your house is worth on the tax roll go to the Appraisal Division at 919-542-8211. Bills, payments and returned-check issues go through Collections.

The county had an estimated 85,111 people in mid-2025, 11.6% more than in 2020. Pittsboro, Siler City and Goldston levy their own town taxes, and slices of Chatham near Cary and Apex are billed for those towns too. That mix is why two Chatham neighbors can have different bills on similar houses.

How often Chatham County reappraises

The county reappraises every four years, well inside the eight-year ceiling that G.S. 105-286 sets for every North Carolina county. Values now on the roll date from January 1, 2025, and before that from 2021. If the county keeps that rhythm, the next value date lands in 2029. The Appraisal Division can confirm it.

For the 2025 round, county appraisers studied recorded sales, building cost data and income and expense figures from commercial property to estimate values for more than 48,000 parcels. Many parts of the county went up in value from 2021, a few went down and some stayed about the same.

The tax rate is a separate step, set from each taxing body's budget. The county rate stays at 60 cents per $100 of valuation in the 2026-27 budget year.

2026 tax rates by district

The county-only rate is 0.60, and every other district adds its own piece on top. The county rate sheet prints a district rate and a combined rate for each area, and the combined figure is the one that matches a bill.

Fire and sanitary districts such as Bonlee, Moncure, North Chatham and Northview are also listed, plus solid waste fees for Pittsboro and Goldston and vehicle fees for Pittsboro, Siler City, Cary and Apex. The county budget year begins July 1, which is also when commissioners and the towns fix rates. Phone the tax office to learn which district covers your street address.

How to appeal a Chatham County value

Begin with the county's comparison tool, file with the Appraisal Division next, and take the matter to the county's equalization board only if the staff review leaves you unsatisfied. The county encourages owners to test a notice against nearby sales on its Comper website. An online appeal form lives on the appraisal page, and a printable paper form is available too.

  • Comparable sales, from your own research, the county's site or a real estate professional.
  • Photos of the inside and outside of the property, showing condition and upgrades.
  • A recent fee appraisal, such as one done for a purchase or refinance.

After an appeal is received, a tax office representative contacts the owner to go over the value. Still unresolved? Request a hearing, and the board mails its written finding. The Board of Equalization and Review sits each spring and takes no new appeals once it adjourns, so file early.

Two statutes set the outer frame. G.S. 105-322 puts the board's first sitting in April or early May, and G.S. 105-290 gives a 30-day clock for taking a loss to the Property Tax Commission.

Relief programs that reduce a tax bill

Chatham runs three state programs plus one local grant. For the state programs, the Tax Listing Office must receive your application before June 1 of the year you qualify.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: a resident aged 65 or more, or totally and permanently disabled, whose income is $38,800 or below, gets the larger of $25,000 or half the home's appraised value excluded.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: a disabled veteran resident or unmarried surviving spouse has $45,000 taken off appraised value. The NCDVA-9 form comes from the state division that handles veteran benefits.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: the bill is limited to a share of income if you are 65-plus or totally disabled, earn at most $58,200, and have owned and lived in the house for five calendar years. Anything above the cap remains a lien. If a disqualifying event happens, the latest three years of deferred tax become payable with interest. A new application is needed each year.
  • Low Income Tax Relief Program: a grant of up to $500, capped at 50% of the current bill, for residents who have owned and lived in the home five years and have household income at or below 60% of area median income. Food and Nutrition Services households skip the income paperwork.

To claim disability, supply a certificate signed by a North Carolina physician or issued by a government agency. Heirs or executors must tell the office when a recipient dies, and a surviving spouse reapplies for the following year. Failing to report a disqualifying event means recovery of the exclusion plus penalties and interest.

Due dates, and tax owed at closing

Each September 1 is the due date, and G.S. 105-360 allows payment without interest through January 5. Interest runs 2% from January 6. Beginning February 1, each month or fraction adds three-fourths of one percent. A check or electronic payment that bounces draws a penalty of $25 or 10% of the payment, whichever is greater, up to $1,000.

A tax lien attaches on the listing date under G.S. 105-355, so the bill follows the house, not the seller. As a rule the closing office pays this year's tax out of the seller's money, and the buyer takes over from there. Owners who let a bill go unpaid can face a tax foreclosure sale held at the courthouse door, with the sale price applied to taxes, penalties, interest and costs under G.S. 105-374.

Sellers can speed things up with a short checklist: ask Collections for the balance on every open bill, confirm the district on your bill so the combined rate is right, find out from the Listing Division whether a relief program is on the property, and give your closing attorney each figure in writing. In a cash sale there is no lender payoff to coordinate, but the tax is still settled from proceeds at closing.

For 2020 to 2024 owner-occupancy was 80.6% and the median home value was $446,200. Anyone receiving a program benefit should ask the Listing Division what a sale does to it. Collections can give you the open balance, which your closing attorney needs before the contract date.

What recording a Chatham County deed costs

Excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of consideration is paid by the seller at the register of deeds office, as G.S. 105-228.30 provides. At the Chatham County Register of Deeds a deed of up to 15 pages is $26.00 to record, and each added page is $4.00. Loan documents cost more, with a deed of trust at $64 for up to 35 pages.

These recording amounts mirror the uniform schedule in G.S. 161-10. Your closing office will supply exact settlement figures, because they turn on the price and the number of pages.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay or question my Chatham County property tax bill?

Call the Tax Administration offices in Pittsboro. The Listing Division answers at 919-542-8250 and the Appraisal Division at 919-542-8211. Payments go through Collections. Visit the Listing Division at 12 East Street, weekdays 8:00 to 5:00.

What is the Chatham County county-only tax rate?

For 2026 it is 0.60, which equals the 60 cents per $100 of valuation for fiscal year 2026-27. Your full rate depends on where the parcel sits, because towns and fire districts add their own.

When can I appeal my Chatham County value?

The Board of Equalization and Review meets each spring, and once it adjourns no new appeals are heard. Owners can still talk to the Appraisal Division about errors, and the next reappraisal brings a new notice and a new window.

Can a Chatham County senior get a lower assessment?

Yes, if age and income fit. At 65 or older with income of $38,800 or less, a greater-of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value is excluded. The application is due before June 1 at the Tax Listing Office.

Who pays the deed excise tax in Chatham County?

The seller does. The transferor owes $1.00 per $500, paid to the register of deeds before recording. The closing office usually deducts it from proceeds.

Until the next revaluation, the tax value on your parcel stays tied to that January 1, 2025 date.

Tax rates

The County Manager's recommended 2026-2027 budget keeps the county rate at 40.5 cents per $100 of valuation. With a public school rate and a fire tax rate added, the combined figure is 61.5 cents per $100.

Rates in the recommended 2026-2027 budget

County property tax40.5 cents
Public school tax14 cents
Fire tax7 cents
Total61.5 cents

Check final figures, and any city or town rate, with the tax office. The school, fire and municipal rates that hit your bill depend on your parcel's location.

How to appeal your assessment

Four routes exist: a written appeal filed online, one sent by mail or email, or an in-person meeting. A phone call does not count as an appeal.

  • Online: the appeal form is on the county tax site, and each parcel needs its own.
  • Mail: a photocopy of the form goes to the Cleveland County Tax Assessor, P.O. Box 370, Shelby, NC 28151.
  • Email: send it to tax.assessor@clevelandcountync.gov.
  • In person: complete the request form that came with your notice, then phone 704-484-4911 to book a time.

Expect a mailed answer in eight weeks or longer. A review can end with the same value, a lower one or a higher one. Only two arguments count: the value is far above its likely selling price, or it was appraised unfairly against similar properties. Arguing about how big the jump was, citing an insurance value, or pleading hardship will not work.

Still unhappy after the informal review? Write to the Board of Equalization and Review to request a hearing before the board adjourns; the county announces that date on its site and in the local paper. Beyond the board sits the Property Tax Commission, and you have 30 days from the day the board mails its decision to go there.

Does a higher appraisal mean a higher bill?

Not always. The bill is tax value times rate, and every taxing jurisdiction picks its own rate, so after a revaluation some bills climb, others drop and a few barely move.

Appraisers can act on value alone. Concerns about services or affordability belong with the elected boards that set the rates. Before you appeal, open the county's assessment records map and turn on the Improved Sales and Vacant Sales layers, which the county suggests for finding recent comparable sales near your parcel. Vehicles, trailers and boats are valued every year, while land and buildings are valued only at a countywide revaluation.

Paying and tracking your bill

The tax office website includes an online payment search and a record lookup, so you can see what is owed on a parcel before you list it. An address change request keeps notices from going to the wrong place after a move, and the tax estimator offers a rough preview of a bill. Tax Administration answers questions at 704-484-4843.

Sellers should check the balance early. The closing agent can only pay what the collector reports, and an old year turning up at the table is the kind of surprise to avoid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cleveland County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax relief programs

The county tax assessor takes applications for three state programs. Applications usually close June 1, and only one program can be used at a time.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is greater, is taken off what is taxed. For 2026 the household income ceiling is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 of appraised value is exempt, and the state form applies no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: your bill is held to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent if income sits between the limit and $58,200 in 2026. It takes five years of owning and living in the home, plus a fresh application each year.

Tax put off under the circuit breaker for the last three years is due when the home changes hands. A sale therefore ends the deferral, and the sum is added to your closing statement. Farm and forest land can also qualify for a present-use deferral, taxed at use value with the difference carried on the books.

Due dates and penalties

September 1 is the due date; January 5 is the last day before interest starts. Bills are figured and mailed in July after the rate-setting boards act.

Interest begins at 2 percent on January 6, and three-fourths of 1 percent more is added every month from February 1. The lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, so any unpaid year stays with the house.

For unpaid tax, the county can foreclose; its tax foreclosure page walks through it. Auctions happen in the Commissioners' Room, second floor, with 5 percent down from the high bidder. A challenger has to beat the bid by $750 or 5 percent, whichever is more, filing in person at the courthouse, and every upset bid opens a new ten-day period. The owner can still redeem until confirmation by the court.

Selling with taxes owed

Request a payoff figure from the collector. The settlement agent pays it out of your proceeds, so the buyer takes on nothing. Any back years are paid off at closing, interest included.

For a parcel already in foreclosure, the liens are listed in the complaint in the clerk's file. Pull it at the courthouse, 100 Justice Place in Shelby, using the CV file number. If repairs or back taxes are making an ordinary sale difficult, our North Carolina page explains a cash option.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When must a Cleveland County bill be paid?

By September 1. Paying after January 5 adds 2 percent, then three-fourths of 1 percent for each month that follows, starting in February.

How do I challenge my Cleveland County appraisal?

File a written appeal online, by mail to P.O. Box 370, Shelby, or by email, or ask for an in-person appointment at 704-484-4911. Phone appeals are not accepted, and a mailed decision can take at least eight weeks.

Is Cleveland County on the standard eight-year cycle?

No. State law caps the gap at eight years, but the county revalues every four. Its latest revaluation took effect January 1, 2025.

By when must relief paperwork reach the county?

June 1 is the usual deadline for the tax year. The elderly or disabled exclusion, disabled veteran exclusion and circuit breaker are all filed with the county, not the Department of Revenue.

May I close on a sale while taxes are owed?

Yes. Get the balance from the collector and have it paid from your proceeds. If foreclosure has started, you can still redeem until the court confirms the sale.

Where to pay your bill

The Columbus County Tax Office is at 810 Pinckney Street, Whiteville, with a public lobby open from half past eight to five. Call 910-640-6635, or write to P.O. Box 1468, Whiteville, NC 28472.

You can pay by mail, phone, online, dropbox or in person, with cash, check or credit card. The collections page has the details. Online payments go through columbus.webtaxpay.com, and the phone line is 877-768-4775.

The office collects for more than the county. It also bills for the City of Whiteville and the towns of Fair Bluff, Sandyfield, Boardman, Brunswick, Cerro Gordo, Bolton, Chadbourn, Tabor City and Lake Waccamaw. If you cannot find an old balance for one of those towns, call town hall.

Property tax rate and fire districts

The county rate is $0.805 per $100 of assessed valuation for fiscal year 2026-2027, and all of it goes to the General Fund. Commissioners adopted the budget ordinance on June 1, 2026. It rests on an estimated total valuation of $4,010,748,958 and a collection rate of 97.72 percent, and it allows discounts for early payment. Two school systems, Columbus County Schools and Whiteville City Schools, serve the county. A special fire tax by district is added on top of the county rate.

RateFire districts

Ask the tax office which fire district your parcel is in and whether a city or town levy also applies.

Revaluation: last in 2021, next in 2029

Columbus County last revalued in 2021, and the next revaluation is set for 2029. Property tax revenue stays relatively flat outside revaluation years, at roughly $30 million a year for the county.

If you sell before 2029, expect the assessed value to date from 2021. Median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 was $146,000. If your own figure looks far from that, ask the appraisal staff how your parcel was valued.

The county has about 50,487 residents and 23,724 housing units, and owners live in 71.1 percent of homes.

Due dates and late charges

Taxes are due September 1, and January 5 is the last day before delinquency. Amounts quoted are good through the last day of the month, and interest of three-fourths of 1 percent accrues on the first day of each month on delinquent taxes. State law adds a 2 percent charge from January 6 to February 1 under G.S. 105-360. Mailed payments count as received on the USPS postmark date.

After a parcel has been advertised for sale, only certified funds are accepted to redeem it. Once the court confirms a sale, North Carolina allows no redemption. To learn whether a property is in tax foreclosure, ask the tax collector's office directly.

How a tax foreclosure sale works

Sales take place outside the main entrance of the Columbus County Courthouse unless the weather is bad. The notice posted at the courthouse and printed in the newspaper controls; the foreclosures page is only an informal list of answers.

  • The high bidder pays a deposit of 20 percent of the bid or $750, whichever is greater. On sales over $5,000, a $1,000 cash deposit is due at once, with the rest within two business days.
  • Every bid is open to a 10-day upset period. Upset bids are filed through the Clerk of Court with a 5 percent or $750 deposit, whichever is greater.
  • After the upset period ends and the sale is confirmed, the last high bidder has three days to pay the balance to the commissioner.
  • The owner keeps the property until a new deed is recorded and may redeem until the court confirms the sale.

Upset bid amounts are found through the NC eCourts portal using the full file number, and the bid form is AOC-CV-414. The clerk will not answer upset bid questions by phone or fill out the form for you.

Property tax relief

The county posts an application for the elderly and disabled exclusion, and the state also offers a disabled-veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferral. Filing runs from January 1 to June 1, and each owner may use one program.

  • County application (2025 tax year): household income at or under $37,900, age 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled on January 1, and a permanent residence titled in the applicant's exact name.
  • 2026 tax year: the income ceiling rises to $38,800, and the excluded amount is the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value.
  • Owners with a disabled-veteran designation: $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, with no age or income test, on Form NCDVA-9.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is limited to 4 percent of income up to the limit and 5 percent above it, up to 150 percent of the limit.

The county asks for the prior year's income tax statement, an SSA-1099, a doctor's certification for applicants under 65, and a death certificate where a spouse has died and the deed was not corrected. Applications are denied if they are incomplete, if the name on the deed differs from the application, or if they miss the deadline. An approved elderly or disabled application does not have to be repeated each year unless household circumstances or income change. A circuit breaker application is filed anew every year.

How to appeal your assessment

Start with the appraisal staff. If that fails, the next forum is the county's equalization board, which by state law is the board of commissioners unless a special board is created. Ask who sits on Columbus County's.

The board opens its session between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May. In an ordinary year it finishes by the third Monday after its first meeting and generally cannot sit past July 1. A hearing request, in writing or in person, must arrive before adjournment, or within 15 days of a late-mailed notice. Rulings are mailed within 30 days.

Beyond the board is the Property Tax Commission, with a 30-day filing window that runs from the board's mailing date. Vehicles, equipment and other personal property are handled by separate staff at the tax office.

Farm notice on title searches

State law (Session Law 2018-113 and G.S. 106-741) requires land records to carry a notice for anyone researching title. It flags a tract within one-half mile of a poultry, swine or dairy qualifying farm or a voluntary agricultural district, or within 600 feet of any other qualifying farm. The county has about 54 people per square mile on 938.12 square miles of land, so farm and rural parcels are common and the notice is worth reading.

The tax office page also lists staff for the solid waste trash user fee and for senior citizen exemptions. Before closing, ask whether any trash fee is attached to your parcel.

If a farm house, an inherited tract or a back-tax parcel is hard to sell the usual way, our North Carolina page explains a cash sale.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Columbus County property tax rate?

The fiscal year 2026-2027 county rate is $0.805 per $100 of assessed value. Fire district taxes range from 0.06 to 0.12 per $100, and city or town taxes are billed separately.

When are Columbus County property taxes due?

September 1. January 5 is the last day to pay before interest begins, which then builds at three-fourths of 1 percent a month after the initial January 6 charge.

Where do I pay Columbus County property taxes in person?

At the Columbus County Tax Office, 810 Pinckney Street, Whiteville, from half past eight until five. You can also pay by mail, by phone at 877-768-4775, online or at the dropbox.

When is the next Columbus County revaluation?

2029. The previous revaluation was in 2021.

Can I stop a Columbus County tax foreclosure?

An owner can redeem until the court confirms the sale, by paying the taxes, interest and costs. After advertising, the county takes certified funds only.

Tax Administration offices and contacts

Craven County Tax Administration, at 226 Pollock Street in New Bern, both appraises real estate and collects the bills. Weekday counter hours are eight to five. Call the real estate appraisal division at 252-636-6640 with value questions, and the tax collection division at 252-636-6605 about bills.

Business personal property and non-business personal property each have their own division. Vehicles are taxed through the state's tag-and-tax system, which a house seller can generally skip unless a closing statement lists a vehicle gap bill.

Eight municipalities sit in the county: Bridgeton, Cove City, Dover, Havelock, New Bern, River Bend, Trent Woods and Vanceboro. About 105,025 people live here, in 50,334 housing units. Owners live in 68.4% of homes, and the typical owner-occupied house was worth $231,600 in 2020 to 2024.

Tax rate and exclusions

The commissioners kept the 2026-2027 county rate at 44.48 cents per $100 of assessed value. This is only the county levy. A town or district charge may sit on top, and the 2026 tax rates document on the county site shows it.

The rate applies to assessed value after any exclusion you hold. Three state programs exist.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or 50% of a permanent residence's appraised value, whichever is greater, is removed from taxation, provided income is within $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 of appraised value is excluded. Age and income do not matter.
  • Circuit breaker: your bill is capped at 4.0% of income, or 5.0% when income exceeds the limit but stays within 150% of it, which is $58,200 for 2026.

Apply on Form AV-9 with the assessor. Applications are taken until June 1 of the preceding year, and each program has its own page on the county tax menu.

Value and rate are separate decisions. Revaluation fixes market value; the commissioners fix the rate to cover the budget. So a higher assessment is not itself a higher rate, though an unchanged rate still yields a bigger bill if your value rises.

Due dates and penalties

The tax menu also lists pre-payments and a delinquent payment assistance page. For delinquent bills, the county refers owners to NCHomeownerAssistance.gov and the state hotline 1-855-696-2423.

Ahead of a sale, get a payoff figure covering the current year and any earlier unpaid ones. The real property tax lien attaches as of the listing date (G.S. 105-355), so a payoff letter protects buyer and seller alike.

Revaluation: 2023 and 2028

Tax year 2023 carried the most recent revaluation, and tax year 2028 is next. The 2028 values will be market value as of January 1 of that year. A Revaluation 2028 page is already online, with a comparable-sales search tool marked "coming February 2028."

Under G.S. 105-286 no more than eight years may separate revaluations, and a county of 75,000 or more can be required to revalue sooner if sales assessment ratios fall below .85 or rise above 1.15. Craven has run a shorter cycle than the statute requires, and Hurricane Florence in 2018 pushed the planned 2020 revaluation to 2023.

If you sell before 2028, your parcel's value will date from that 2023 revaluation.

How to appeal your assessment

Send a signed appeal form to the county assessor before the date printed on your value notice, which in a revaluation year is the board's adjournment date.

  • Include comparable sales from on or before January 1 of the revaluation year, photos showing the property's condition, and any recent appraisal or market analysis.
  • The owner, an attorney or an agent under power of attorney can sign. A close family member may also appear when the owner cannot, such as during unexpected military duty or a hospital stay.
  • An appraiser reviews the file and mails a result: higher, lower or unchanged.
  • Still in disagreement? The Board of Equalization and Review hears the case and sends a hearing letter at least 15 days ahead.
  • Bring a copy of your evidence for each of the seven board members.

After the board comes the Property Tax Commission. File written notice within 30 days of the date the board mails its decision, with a copy to the assessor (G.S. 105-290).

  • Historic Properties, Builders Exclusion, Religious Uses Exemption and Antique Airplane and Automobile Exclusion pages.
  • A gross receipts rental tax report and an occupancy and tourism development tax form, which matter to anyone selling a rental.
  • Change of mailing address forms, so a seller's final bill reaches the right place after closing.

What to ask before you list

A few calls early on save trouble later. Ask the appraisal division at 252-636-6640 how your parcel was valued in 2023 and when the next revaluation will arrive. Ask tax collection at 252-636-6605 whether anything is open from an earlier year. If you rent the property, ask whether the gross receipts rental tax report or the occupancy and tourism development tax form still needs filing. Finally, file a change of mailing address so your last bill finds you.

Having those answers in hand makes the payoff figure and the settlement statement easy to check.

Tax year 2028. The last one took effect in 2023.

Who handles property tax in Cumberland County

Cumberland County Tax Administration assesses real estate and sends the bills. The office is on the fifth floor of the county courthouse in downtown Fayetteville, Room 530, 117 Dick Street. The phone number is 910-678-7507, and it is the same number you call to set up a payment plan.

About 338,473 people live in the county, in 146,623 housing units. Owners occupy 55.0% of homes, so close to half the housing is rental, and the middle owner-occupied home is valued at $199,200. Rates differ from one town to the next, so the address matters when you estimate what a buyer will pay each year.

2026 property tax rates

On 2026 bills (fiscal year 2027) the county's general rate is 49.9 cents per $100 of valuation, with a 5.0-cent special recreation rate beside it. Towns add their own rates, so the total depends on where the parcel sits.

Flat fees on the tax bill

Service charges appear on the same bill and sit outside the rate. The county prints these amounts:

  • Solid waste fee of $285 a year for Fayetteville residences with seven or fewer units.
  • Solid waste fee of $130 a year for unincorporated areas and every municipality except Spring Lake.
  • Refuse tax of $342.72 a year in Hope Mills and $396.00 in Spring Lake, the latter including a $12 residential litter control fee.
  • Fayetteville residential storm water by impervious surface: $84.00 below 2,500 square feet, $168.00 for 2,501 to 4,800, $252.00 beyond that.
  • Residential storm water of $60 a year in Spring Lake and in Hope Mills.
  • Vehicle fees: $25 vehicle fee plus a $5 transit tax in Fayetteville, $10 in Hope Mills, and $5 each in Stedman and Spring Lake.

Buyers weigh the full bill, not only the rate, so read yours line by line. A house just over a town line can carry very different charges.

Due dates and penalties

The due date is September 1. Paying by January 5 avoids interest, penalties and collection.

Past that date, G.S. 105-360 applies: 2% from January 6, plus three-fourths of one percent for each month or part of a month starting February 1. MyCCNCPay takes credit, debit or electronic draft payments. A payment plan goes through the phone number above.

The yearly listing period ends January 31 (G.S. 105-307), and changes to your parcel, new construction for one, are reported by then.

Bills left unpaid may end in a tax foreclosure sale, which an outside attorney conducts for the tax office. The foreclosure page on the county site names that attorney and shows parcels in an upset bid period. Redeeming remains possible until the court confirms the sale: pay the taxes, penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-374).

Revaluation in Cumberland County

Real property was reappraised countywide for 2025, eight years after the January 1, 2017 revaluation. The county follows an eight-year cycle under G.S. 105-286, so expect the next one on that schedule.

A revaluation year runs in a set order. Notices go to owners in February, and the notice carries an informal appeal form on its back. Informal appeals are due in March, the Board of Equalization and Review convenes in April, and formal appeals close in May when the board adjourns. New rates using the updated values take effect July 1, and bills follow that August.

If you agree with the new value, there is nothing to file. Assessed values are posted online, and a Revaluation Call Center at 910-678-7800 books appointments with appraisers. The county also points owners to three state relief programs: present use deferment, the elderly or disabled exclusion and the disabled veteran exclusion.

How to appeal your assessment

Ask for an informal review first. If that fails, file a formal request with the Board of Equalization and Review before the board adjourns, by hand at Room 543 of the courthouse, by mail to PO Box 449 in Fayetteville (ZIP 28302), or in the secure drop box on the courthouse's rear lot.

Put the request in writing. Every appealing taxpayer hears from an appraiser, and if the case reaches the board a letter gives the hearing date and time. Bring appraisals, comparable properties, income and expense statements, repair estimates and photos of unusual conditions.

The regular board opens its first session between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May. In a non-revaluation year it finishes within three Mondays unless it needs longer, and it cannot meet after July 1. The 2026 board convened April 22 and accepted real property appeals until May 20.

Corrections, including clerical errors, go to a special board that sits at 3:30 p.m. on the second Wednesday of every month but July. Unhappy with a board ruling? You can take it to the state Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the notice's mailing (G.S. 105-290).

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Cumberland County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exclusions that can lower the bill

For a disabled veteran, the first $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, whatever the age or income. A service officer completes Form NCDVA-9 first, and the form then goes to the assessor.

Elderly or disabled relief and the circuit breaker go through Form AV-9 at the assessor, accepted up to June 1. If you qualify, mention it when you list the house, because a lower annual bill is a selling point for the next owner.

Selling with taxes owed

Because taxes are a lien on the property, an unpaid bill survives the closing. The closing attorney normally pays what is owed out of your proceeds and gets a payoff figure from Tax Administration first. Call 910-678-7507 for the amount, since interest grows each month after January 5.

If the house is already in the foreclosure process, you still have the right to redeem until the court confirms the sale. A buyer paying cash can close quickly enough to clear the taxes before that point, and a cash sale skips the lender appraisal and loan approval steps that slow a financed one.

Take your latest tax bill, exemption approvals and payment records along when you first sit down with your attorney. Mid-year sales are common, so ask Tax Administration how the current bill is split between you and the buyer.

Frequently asked questions

When are Cumberland County property taxes due?

Every September 1. January 5 is the last day to pay before interest, and the 2% charge starts January 6.

What is the combined rate inside Fayetteville city limits?

The City of Fayetteville rate is 0.4495 and the county rate is 0.499, for a combined 0.9485 per $100 on 2026 bills.

Where does a formal appeal go?

Take it to Room 543 of the courthouse, mail it to PO Box 449, or use the secure drop box. It must be in writing and in hand before the board adjourns.

When was the last Cumberland County revaluation?

The 2025 revaluation is the latest. The one before it took effect January 1, 2017, and the county revalues every eight years.

Who runs Cumberland County tax foreclosure sales?

An outside attorney conducts them for the Tax Office. Call the attorney's office listed on the county's foreclosure page for sale dates and upset bid status.

Davidson County tax offices

Two sides share the work: an assessor lists and values property, and a collector bills and collects. Both sit at 913 Greensboro Street, 3rd Floor, Suite 303, Lexington (NC 27292), open weekdays 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. A second counter in Denton opens at 8:30 AM on weekdays.

  • Tax office and appeals line: 336-242-2160.
  • Collections line: 336-242-2180.
  • Assessor mailing address: P.O. Box 1617, Lexington, NC 27293.
  • Payment mailing address: Davidson County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1577, Lexington, NC 27293.

The assessor's side answers questions on listing, billing and assessed values. The collector's job stops at collecting.

About 180,182 people live in the county, in 69,846 households, and 74.4 percent of those households own. The median owned home is valued at $219,100, and the median household income is $64,172 (2024 dollars).

2026 tax rates

The county's own rate is 0.5400 on the 2026 sheet. A parcel inside a city, school district or fire district picks up that jurisdiction's rate as well. Call the tax office to confirm the final numbers for your parcel.

Davidson County 2026 rates by jurisdiction

Fire districts are listed separately and run from 0.0965 for Reeds Fire to 0.1624 for Healing Springs Fire. City motor vehicle fees are $30.00 in Lexington and High Point, $20.00 in Thomasville and $5.00 in Denton. Discounts do not apply to the city and municipal service district lines.

Due dates, discounts and penalties

Each July the county mails bills for land, buildings and business or personal property. September 1 is the due date, and interest waits until after January 5. A January 5 that falls on a weekend rolls to the next business day.

Early payers save: 1 1/2 percent off in July, 1 percent off in August. A postmark of January 5 is on time, but the county advises sending it a week ahead. Once an account is past due, 2 percent is added for January and 3/4 percent more for every month after. If you need a payment plan, arrange it when the annual bill lands and finish it by the delinquent date. The office takes cards.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Davidson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Revaluation postponed to 2027

Values last reset on January 1, 2021. The reappraisal once planned for 2026 now falls in 2027 under new legislation. State law requires counties to reappraise at least once every eight years, and a revaluation here covers more than 97,000 parcels.

The aim is to equalize values, not to raise revenue, and elected officials set the rates in June. If you appealed a 2026 or 2027 value on time, you do not need to refile, and any change from those appeals applies to the 2027 tax year. The county's appeal page has separate forms for the current 2026 value and the 2027 revaluation value, and questions can go to revalhelp@davidsoncountync.gov.

How to contest your value

Appeals run on three levels. You begin with an informal review, where a county appraiser reads your property record and looks at whatever evidence you bring. A mistake found there is corrected with no formal appeal.

Next is a formal hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review. By law the commissioners sit as that board unless a special one is created, and Davidson County describes its board as local residents with real estate knowledge, appointed by the commissioners. After an unwelcome board decision, you can give written notice to the state Property Tax Commission, and the 30 days run from the date the board's notice is mailed.

The county lists reasons that are not grounds for a reduction:

  • The size of the percentage increase or decrease.
  • A market value above the insurance value.
  • A feeling that the value is simply too high.
  • An owner's inability to pay the tax.

Homestead and relief programs

North Carolina sets up three relief programs, and you may claim just one of them. Older or permanently disabled owners with income of $38,800 or less (2026) can exclude $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is larger.

Under the circuit breaker, a household at or below that income limit pays no more than 4.0 percent of income, and one up to 150 percent of the limit ($58,200 for 2026) pays no more than 5.0 percent. Five years as owner and occupant come first. The disabled veteran exclusion is the third: $45,000 off the value, whatever the owner's age or income.

Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, and the homestead application is linked from the property information page on the county site. Any tax deferred by the circuit breaker turns into a lien that must be paid when title transfers, so a sale triggers it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Davidson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Unpaid property tax

Interest starts after the January 5 deadline, and the bill then becomes subject to collection. The collector can use wage garnishment, attachment of bank accounts or rents, levy on personal property and, for real estate, foreclosure by sale at public auction.

  • Unpaid real estate accounts can be advertised in local newspapers from March 1 to June 30, at added cost to the taxpayer.
  • Sheriff's warrants, in rem foreclosures and attachment of the state tax refund are also used.
  • The lien date is the listing date under state law, so the lien exists before the bill is due.

The county posts a PDF list of 2025 delinquent taxpayers and a tax foreclosure list. Davidson County also requires a tax certificate before the Register of Deeds takes a deed, so a delinquent balance has to be cleared first.

Selling a Davidson County house

A mid-year sale leaves the January 1 owner on the hook for that year's bill. Find out whether the closing will prorate it. The tidiest route is for the closing attorney to pay the collector directly out of your proceeds.

With no attorney closing, ask for the tax certificate well ahead of time, because the deed will be turned away at the Register of Deeds without it. Check any open 2026 or 2027 appeal as well, since a changed value takes effect for 2027.

Before listing, pull together your latest bill, proof of any exclusion and a payoff figure from the collections line, 336-242-2180. A cash buyer does not wait on a lender, which helps when a delinquent balance or newspaper advertising is running. Whatever the buyer's financing, the taxes come out of the sale money first.

Frequently asked questions

When do Davidson County property taxes come due?

September 1, and no interest accrues through January 5. Paying in July saves 1 1/2 percent, and paying in August saves 1 percent.

What rate applies to a Davidson County home?

The county's 2026 rate is 0.5400, plus any city, school and fire district rates. Lexington is 0.6500 and Thomasville is 0.6200. The tax office can confirm the final rate for your address.

Did Davidson County delay its revaluation?

Yes, the 2026 revaluation moved to 2027 under new legislation. Timely appeals of 2026 or 2027 values still get reviewed, and a change applies for the 2027 tax year.

How do I challenge my Davidson County assessment?

Submit the county's form for an informal sit-down with an appraiser. If that does not settle it, a formal hearing follows, and a further appeal to the state Property Tax Commission is due within 30 days of the board's mailing.

How much interest do late Davidson County taxes carry?

Past-due real estate is charged 2 percent for January and 3/4 percent per month afterward. Send payments by mail at least five business days before January 5.

Selling in Davie County? Get a Cash Offer

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Davie County?

Davie County property tax offices

Davie County Tax Administration has three divisions: real property appraisal (which also covers mapping and land records), personal property appraisal, and tax collection. Billing and payment belong to the collector, while listings and assessed values belong to the assessor.

The Administration Building, 123 South Main Street in Mocksville, takes listings Monday to Friday from 8 AM to 5 PM, whether you come in, file online or mail them. Reach the assessor at 336 753-6120 and revaluation staff at 336-753-6140. Appeals on real property are sent to that same address.

Thinking of selling?

Mostly rural, Davie is gaining suburban residents: 45,855 people in July 2025, a 7.3% rise over the 42,719 of April 2020. Owner-occupied homes make up 82.2% of housing, valued at a median of $253,900 (2020-2024), and median household income is $75,057. With owners so common, the exclusions below apply to many sellers.

2026-27 tax rates

Davie levies $0.6486 per $100 of valuation countywide for fiscal 2026-2027, and your parcel's location adds more. Multiply the tax value by the combined rate to get the bill.

Davie County rates for the 2026-27 fiscal year
AreaRate
Davie County$0.6486 per $100 valuation

Town of Mocksville$0.29 per $100 valuation
Town of Cooleemee$0.42 per $100 valuation, plus a $75.00 solid waste fee per residence

The county's budget guide for the same year keeps the countywide rate at 64.86 cents and the fire tax at 4 cents. On a tax bill, the countywide fire levy shows up as ADVL followed by a number. Ask the collector which fire district covers your parcel before you work out a payoff.

Due dates and penalties

Expect your bill shortly after July 1. It is due September 1, but payment is taken through January 5 (the next business day when that is a Saturday, Sunday or holiday). No bill by September 15? Phone the collector.

  • Payments must arrive or be postmarked by the deadline. With no postmark, the delivery day counts, so mail at least 5 business days ahead.
  • Real estate accounts that go past due are charged 2% for January and 3/4% for each month beyond.
  • Partial payments are welcome, and a mailed one needs a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt.
  • Paying online by card adds a convenience fee and requires the bill year, account number and bill number.

Between March 1 and June 30, current-year delinquent real property liens must be advertised in a newspaper, with the cost added to what the owner owes. Wage, bank account and rent garnishment, foreclosure and tax warrants are all in the collection toolkit. By statute the lien on a parcel arises on the listing date, January 1.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Davie County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Values were last reset effective January 1, 2025, with notices to owners in February 2025. Before that came 2021. Davie has recently revalued every four years, though state law only requires one every eight.

County staff did the work in house. Appraisers sorted the county into roughly 215 appraisal neighborhoods, compared recent sales and applied one schedule of values. The revaluation covers near 24,000 parcels, and the schedule stays in use until a new one is needed or 8 years pass.

To contest a value:

  • Fill out the appeal form completely, sign and date it, and return it within thirty days of receiving it.
  • Send it to the Revaluation Office at 123 South Main Street, Mocksville, NC 27028, email it with supporting documents, or use the online form on the Revaluation/Land Records page.
  • State your basis for the appeal. Some appeals get a site visit.
  • Watch for a letter saying whether the value changed. It can go up, stay the same or go down.

Some sales do not count as qualified comparisons: a conveyance of two or more parcels, transactions between relatives or related businesses, undivided or fractional interests, sales involving governments, utilities, lenders or relocation firms, and forced or auction sales. Pick comparables outside those categories. Lose before the county board and you can go to the Property Tax Commission, within 30 days of the date the board's notice was mailed. Call 336-753-6140 to find out when the next appeal window opens.

Exclusions and the circuit breaker

Three state programs exist, and each owner picks only one:

  • Elderly and disabled exclusion: income of $39,900 or less, and a cut of $25,000 or 50% of the value of the house and one acre.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: honorable discharge and a 100% service-related disability, with no income cap, for $45,000 off the home and one acre.
  • Circuit breaker: income of $59,850 or below, North Carolina residency, and five years owning and living in the home.

Income ceilings shift from year to year, so ask the assessor for the current figures. If you already receive an exclusion you need not reapply, but the circuit breaker requires a fresh application annually. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, who must take it up to June 1 ahead of the tax year.

The circuit breaker defers any tax above the cap and records it as a lien. A sale makes up to three prior years of deferred tax payable, so find that figure before you list.

Listing property each January

The listing window is the month of January. Forms must arrive or be postmarked by January 31, and a late listing draws a 10% penalty. Owners also report new buildings and improvements and list unregistered vehicles, mobile homes, boats and business assets.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Davie County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

At closing the seller usually pays the year's tax, with proration as a courtesy between the two sides. The legal duty rests with the January 1 owner of record, yet collection can follow the property to the next owner, so settle the split with your attorney.

  • Ask the collector for a payoff covering every open year and any advertised delinquency.
  • The grantor purchases the state deed stamp at the register of deeds before recording, at one dollar per five hundred dollars of price.
  • On the circuit breaker, expect the deferred amount to come due on transfer.
  • Any lien for unpaid tax must be cleared through closing, no matter who buys.

A fast cash closing can pay off delinquent taxes before newspaper advertising adds cost, and it skips the lender's appraisal, which leaves the payoff figure as the main number to settle. Give the closing attorney your latest bill and any exclusion paperwork.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Davie County property tax?

Pay the Tax Collector by mail, in person at the Administration Building, in the dropbox, or online with a card. Mailed payments can go to the lockbox, and the office has a teller window. Online card payments carry a convenience fee.

How do I appeal my Davie County value?

Return the appeal form within thirty days of receiving it, with your basis and any documents. Call 336-753-6140 to ask when the next appeal window opens.

What is the Davie County tax rate in Mocksville?

A Mocksville parcel is charged the county rate of $0.6486 per $100, the countywide fire rate of $0.04 and the town rate of $0.29 for 2026-27. Other towns and fire districts have their own figures in the table above.

Must I renew a Davie County elderly exclusion each year?

No. An owner already receiving an exclusion does not need to reapply. The circuit breaker is different, because the state requires a new application each year.

Who covers the deed stamp on a Davie County sale?

The seller. The register of deeds collects one dollar per five hundred dollars of price (a leftover fraction counts as another five hundred) at recording, and the proceeds are split between the county and the state.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Duplin County?

Duplin County tax offices

Three offices make up the Tax Department: Assessing, Collections and Land Records. They share the Hardison Building at 117 Beasley Street, Kenansville, and keep weekday hours of 8 am to 5 pm.

Duplin County tax offices
OfficeWhat it doesPhone
AssessingSets values on real and personal property and takes exclusion and present-use applications910-296-2110
CollectionsCollects county and town taxes, runs delinquent collection and foreclosures, issues mobile home moving permits910-296-2112
Land RecordsMaintains parcel maps and who owns what910-296-2110 (general tax questions)

Mail goes to Box 968, Kenansville, NC 28349. Collections handles town levies along with county bills for Calypso, Greenevers, Kenansville, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace and Warsaw. Walk in with cash, a check or a card, call, or use the online portal. Cards cost extra every time.

The housing market for a seller

Rural Duplin had about 51,571 residents in July 2025, after falling from 58,505 (2010) to 48,715 (2020). Of its 24,235 housing units, 70.3% are owner-occupied, with a median value of $137,400. Median gross rent is $865 and median household income is $55,148.

Ahead of listing, get a payoff figure from the collector and learn from the assessor whether an exclusion is on file.

Property tax rate

The county's recommended budget for 2026-27 keeps the rate at 58 cents for every $100 of assessed value. That matches the year before, which was a 15.5-cent cut from the 73.5 cents budgeted for 2024-25 after the January 2025 revaluation.

  • Revaluation in 2025 lifted the tax base by about 25% and brought assessments to roughly 98 percent of market value.
  • The revenue-neutral rate it produced was $0.5667 per $100.
  • Billed value for 2026 is $6,143,053,057 of real and personal property, spread over 42,374 nonexempt parcels as of January 2026.
  • Fire districts add their own rate to the county's. The 2025-26 recommended budget runs from 4.5 cents per $100 (Calypso department) up to 10 cents (Harrells department).

The fire district and town for a parcel decide its full rate, and the assessing office can tell you both. With values near market, a buyer's lender will see a tax load that matches the real price.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Duplin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

When Duplin County revalues

Current values date from a January 1, 2025 revaluation. The next is planned for January 1, 2030. The state minimum is every eight years, yet commissioners chose in 2023 to reappraise countywide every five.

Between cycles, assessing staff go through building permits for new construction and additions and talk with owners about value. The next reappraisal will be carried out by state-certified appraisers. Anything you built, added or tore down since the last one has probably already reached the appraisers by way of the permit.

How to appeal your value

Begin with the county's informal review form. It asks for the owner, appellant, parcel number, address and your opinion of value. You circle the basis of the appeal: appraisal, asking price, purchase price or comparable sales.

  • Attach photos or documents that back up your number. Missing evidence can delay the review.
  • Commercial or income property owners include their three latest years of income and expenses.
  • Mail the form to Duplin County Revaluation, PO Box 968, Kenansville, NC 28349. The current form lists April 15 as the submission date.
  • A separate form handles personal property appeals and requests a Board of Equalization and Review hearing.

State law has the county board meet for the first time between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May. If the ruling goes against you, send the Property Tax Commission written notice of your grounds within 30 days of the mailing date, and copy the assessor.

Due dates, penalties and foreclosure

September 1 is the due date, and anything paid before January 6 is free of interest. After that, 2% applies through the start of February, and 3/4% is added for each later month or fraction of a month.

The collector can use:

  • Wage garnishment.
  • Seizure of grower payments.
  • Bank account attachment.
  • State income tax refund attachment.
  • Foreclosure on the property.

A tax foreclosure runs like a mortgage foreclosure. The county attorney receives the delinquent file, the court picks a sale date, and a sign goes up on the property while notices run in local papers. Bidding takes place at the Kenansville courthouse steps and starts at the county's bid. Whoever bids highest puts down 20% that day in cash or certified check. Once the commissioner files the sale report, anyone has 10 days to raise the bid or file exceptions. Until confirmation, the owner may redeem by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Duplin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exclusions and relief programs

Assessing processes the senior, disability and disabled veteran exclusions plus present-use value applications for farmland. Its forms include an application for property tax relief, a certification of disability and a certification for the disabled veteran exclusion.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the larger of $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, for owners 65 and up or totally and permanently disabled whose income is under the cap ($38,800 for tax year 2026).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off the home's appraised value, at any age and income.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is held to 4% of income (5% for incomes between the cap and 150% of it), and anything above is deferred.

File with the county assessor, who must take applications until June 1 before the tax year. If you own a mobile home, note that no moving permit comes from the collector until the taxes are paid or shown not to be at risk.

Selling with taxes owed

Request a payoff from collections, find out which fire district and town taxes apply, and let your attorney settle the year's tax at closing. The seller also buys the deed stamp, a different charge, at the register of deeds.

If you inherited a house with back taxes, ask whether Collections has already sent it to the county attorney, because that shortens your time. A cash buyer may close before a sale date is set, and cash skips the lender's appraisal and approval steps. In both cases the payoff is paid from the proceeds. Call Collections at 910-296-2112 for the number.

On sale day, expect to bring the latest bill, any exclusion approvals and a list of every open year. The closing attorney then asks Collections for a final payoff that includes the town levy if the parcel is inside Calypso, Greenevers, Kenansville, Magnolia, Rose Hill, Teachey, Wallace or Warsaw. Paying the whole balance at closing keeps the buyer's title free of tax claims and avoids a delay when the deed is recorded.

Frequently asked questions

When is the next Duplin County revaluation?

January 1, 2030. The latest took effect January 1, 2025, and commissioners voted in 2023 to revalue every five years.

How do I pay Duplin County property tax?

Go to the Tax Office at 117 Beasley Street in Kenansville, call 910-296-2112, or use the online tax portal. In person you can use cash, check or card, and cards carry a fee.

What rate does Duplin County charge?

The recommended 2026-27 budget uses 58 cents per $100 of assessed value. Fire districts and towns collected by the county add more, so ask the assessing office for your parcel's full rate.

How do I appeal a Duplin County assessment?

Mail the informal real property review form with evidence to Duplin County Revaluation, PO Box 968, Kenansville. It lists April 15 as the submission date, and commercial owners add three years of income and expense figures.

What happens if Duplin County taxes go unpaid?

The county can garnish wages, attach bank accounts, grower payments and state refunds, or foreclose. Foreclosure sales are on the courthouse steps in Kenansville, with a 20% deposit from the winning bidder.

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Durham County?

Durham County Tax Administration

Tax Administration is on the third floor at 201 East Main Street, Durham, and answers at 919-560-0300. Appeals, bills and relief applications all start there, and the Land Records team works from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM.

An online Tax Help portal lets owners file an appeal, message staff and follow the status of a case. To pay, go to pay.dconc.gov, mail a check to the Tax Collector at P.O. Box 580240, Charlotte, NC 28258-0240, pay at the counter, or pay by phone (a convenience fee applies). E-check adds a $3.25 processing fee.

Inside the city you pay both a county and a city tax, so look at both bills when you plan a sale.

The Durham housing market

Durham County had an estimated 347,240 residents in July 2025, 6.9% above the 2020 estimates base, with 164,222 housing units. Owners occupy just 55.5% of homes, which leaves a large rental segment. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $389,400, median gross rent is $1,508, and median household income is $82,316. Builders pulled 4,772 permits in 2025.

2026-27 tax rates

The Board of County Commissioners approved a countywide rate of 57.92 cents per $100 of property value in the 2026-2027 budget ordinance. The City of Durham kept its rate at 43.71 cents per $100 for the same year.

  • Durham County: 57.92 cents per $100 for 2026-27.
  • City of Durham: 43.71 cents per $100 for 2026-27.
  • Owners of residential property in unincorporated Durham County get a solid waste decal with the mailed bill.

The 2025 reappraisal reshaped the rate history. Total taxable value grew from $43 billion in 2019 to more than $70 billion. The county rate fell from 0.7987 to a revenue-neutral 0.5192, and the rate set for 2025-26 was 0.5542. For 2026-27 it is 57.92 cents.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Durham County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and penalties

Bills come due September 1, and you have until January 5 to pay without penalty. Until then you can also make partial payments on real property with no interest or added cost.

Pay as soon as the bill arrives, or send it to the escrow department if your lender pays it. Under the state schedule, January 6 begins a 2% charge, and each month or fraction after February 1 adds three-fourths of a percent.

The statutory lien on a parcel dates from January 1, the listing date, and carries any penalties, interest and costs. A sale later in the year does not remove it. Only payment does.

If you are selling in the fall, remember that the bill follows the parcel and the closing attorney will want the amount owed in writing. Call 919-560-0300 for it, and check whether the e-check fee of $3.25 or the phone convenience fee matters to you when you pick how to pay. A check by mail to the Charlotte P.O. box is the plain option, but allow time for it to arrive before January 5.

How to appeal your value

The tax office can look only at appraised value. Tax rates, affordability and services are outside an appeal. If you believe the value is well above or below what the property would have sold for on January 1, 2025, you can appeal.

The Board of Equalization and Review can still allow a late application until December 31, and owners who miss a deadline are advised to apply in future years. Appeals on personal property and vehicles generally run on a 30 day clock from the bill, or from a separate value notice if one was sent.

Useful evidence:

  • An independent appraisal based on comparable sales near the reappraisal date.
  • The deed and related appraisal information.
  • A list of comparable sales from the same period.
  • Surveys, plat maps and photographs, especially of condition problems.

The path has three levels. An informal review with a staff appraiser typically takes 30 to 120 days, and any agreed value is only a recommendation. The Board of Equalization and Review, appointed by the commissioners, makes it final, and attendance is optional. Proof is the taxpayer's job. Beyond that, a petition to the NC Property Tax Commission must go in within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

Tax relief programs

Durham publishes three state homestead programs plus one local program. The state programs share a June 1 filing date. The elderly and disabled exclusion takes a single application, while the circuit breaker is renewed every year.

Homeowner tax relief programs in Durham County
ProgramWhat it doesMain requirement
Elderly/Disabled Homestead ExemptionRemoves $25,000 or half of assessed value, whichever is greater, for the home and up to 1 acreAge 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with 2025 income of $38,800 or less
Circuit Breaker defermentLimits tax to 4% of income, or 5% in the higher tier; the excess is deferredSame age and disability rules, income up to $58,250, and five years of ownership and residence
Disabled Veteran ExclusionRemoves the first $45,000 of appraised valueTotal and permanent service-connected disability; open regardless of age or income
DSS Low Income Homeowner ReliefHelp toward the current bill through a three-tier income modelHousehold at or below 80% of area median income, five or more years in the home, apply through DSS

DSS applications open each September 1, and that program cannot be combined with the homestead exclusion. A circuit breaker owner who sells owes the deferred taxes for the most recent 3 years at transfer, with interest.
