Selling a Durham County house

Ask Tax Administration for a payoff figure before closing so the year's bill is settled at the table. A sale can also bring an appraiser to the property, and a structure built after 2025 is valued using January 1, 2025 market rates.

  • The seller buys the state deed stamp at the register of deeds, a dollar for each five hundred dollars of price, before recording.
  • Assessed value stays tied to the January 1, 2025 market, so a newer sale price can differ from it.
  • Owners with a deferred circuit breaker balance should request the figure early.

An inherited or tenant-occupied house with a long tax history needs the same payoff request. The relief team can say whether an exclusion should have been on the account.

A cash buyer can close quickly, which helps when a bill is close to January 5 and penalties are coming. A cash sale also skips a lender's appraisal and underwriting. The tax payoff, the deed stamp and recording costs are still due at the closing table.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Durham County property tax rate?

The countywide rate for 2026-27 is 57.92 cents per $100 of property value. Owners inside the city also pay the City of Durham rate of 43.71 cents per $100.

When are Durham County property taxes due?

Each September 1, with no penalty until after January 5. Partial payments on real property are allowed until then.

Can I still appeal my Durham County property value?

The Board of Equalization and Review can allow a late application until December 31, and you can apply again in future years. Call 919-560-0300 to find out what the board will accept.

How do I apply for Durham County tax relief?

Apply to the county assessor by June 1 on Form AV-9 for the elderly or disabled exclusion or the circuit breaker, adding the NCDVA-9 form for the disabled veteran exclusion. Call 919-560-0300 for help with the form.

Who buys the deed stamp on a Durham County sale?

The seller. The state rate is a dollar per five hundred dollars of price, paid to the register of deeds before recording.

Who values and who bills property

Edgecombe County's Tax Administration department splits the work between two desks. The assessor appraises property and takes exemption, exclusion and deferment applications. The collector mails bills and goes after unpaid ones. Anyone may look through listing and valuation files from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

  • Taxes paid or owed: the Tax Collector at (252) 641-7810.
  • Value and bill basis questions: the Tax Assessor at (252) 641-7855.
  • Mail for appeals: Edgecombe County Tax Assessor's Office, Attention: Tax Assessor, PO Box 10, Tarboro, NC 27886.

The collector bills for the county itself, 14 fire districts, one drainage district and eight towns: Conetoe, Leggett, Macclesfield, Pinetops, Princeville, Speed, Sharpsburg and Whitakers. Owners in other municipalities get a separate bill from that town or city.

Edgecombe County tax rates by town

The county bills the fire districts and the eight small towns itself, so a Pinetops address shows county and town levies on one statement.

The January listing rule

Listing opens on the first business day of January and closes January 31. A form that arrives late costs a 10% penalty for each year it was late. Forms for people who have listed before go out by mail in late December.

Houses and land sit in a permanent listing system, so you report only when a building was added, altered or removed. Pulling a building permit is not a substitute for that report. Mobile homes, campers, boats, untagged vehicles, business equipment and appliances in rentals do have to be listed each year.

The person who owned the property on January 1 answers for the whole year, even after a spring sale. Commissioners may stretch the listing season, and someone with good cause can ask in writing for a personal extension before the regular period ends.

When do Edgecombe County tax bills come due?

The due date is September 1, and interest holds off until January 6 under G.S. 105-360. Interest is 2% through the end of January, then three quarters of one percent for every later month or part of a month.

A county or town can set up early payment discounts by resolution before May 1 of the due year, so ask the collector whether one applies when you pay. A payment sent by mail counts as received on its postmark date.

How to challenge your real estate value

Start by calling the assessor at 252-641-7855 or sending in the informal review form. The informal review is open only when your value changed from last year's bill and you are seeing the new number for the first time. A new owner faces the same test.

If the informal result disappoints you, or you did not qualify, you take a formal appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review. The commissioners appoint that panel from residents who know local real estate. It meets in the Administration Building, 201 Saint Andrew Street, Tarboro, and the county publishes a notice each year with the meeting and hearing request dates. Watch the Rocky Mount Telegram for it, or call the assessor.

  • The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2024, and its values stay until the next one.
  • Later swings in the market cannot be weighed in a review.
  • An owner who got word of a change after adjournment has until December 31.
  • Vehicle, business and personal property appeals are due 30 days from the bill date.
  • The next level is the state Property Tax Commission, reached by notice within 30 days of the board's mailed decision (G.S. 105-290).

Homestead and use value programs

Exemption, exclusion and deferment applications all go through the assessor. State law offers three homestead paths: an exclusion for elderly or disabled owners, a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferment. Send Form AV-9 to the county assessor. The state takes it through June 1 ahead of the tax year, and the 2026 income limit is $38,800.

Farm and forest owners have a separate path called Present Use Value. It taxes qualifying land at a use schedule and defers the difference. If the land drops out, the county rolls back the year of the change plus three earlier years.

Unpaid property tax and foreclosure

The collector can use foreclosure, sheriff executions, and garnishment of wages, bank accounts and rents. The county keeps a public Tax Foreclosure List that tags each parcel as complaint filed, settlement pending, private sale pending, upset bid period or a posted sale date.

Buyers at these sales leave a 5% deposit, take the property as is, and cannot undo the purchase. For upset bid details, call the Clerk of Court at 252-824-3200 Ext. 2 with the file number. State law gives ten days after a sale report for an upset bid, and an owner can redeem before confirmation by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs (G.S. 105-374). If your parcel shows up on the list, phone the collector before the sale date.

Selling with taxes owed

The collector prepares statements of taxes due for attorneys and real estate professionals. Ask for one before you set the closing date. Deeds need a tax certification before recording unless the attorney preparer statement appears on the instrument, so line that up with your closing attorney too.

  1. Request the statement of taxes due.
  2. Have your closing attorney work out the proration, since January 1 ownership fixes responsibility for the whole year.
  3. Pay any balance from your proceeds at closing.
  4. If the land is in use value, remind the buyer that a new application is needed within 60 days of transfer.

A cash sale skips the lender's payoff and appraisal timing, but the tax statement and deed certification still apply. Our Edgecombe County register of deeds page covers recording fees.

Edgecombe County at a glance

Edgecombe is a rural county with 96.7 residents per square mile over 505.44 square miles of land at the 2020 count. Typical monthly owner costs run $1,252 with a mortgage and $511 without one. Population grew 0.5% from April 2020 to July 2025, and the county has 19,652 households of about 2.44 people each. Those numbers point to a slow, steady market.

What is the Edgecombe County tax rate?

The county rate is 0.89 per $100 of value on its 2025 sheet. Towns and fire districts add their own rates, and a $150.00 solid waste fee applies.

What is the last day to list property in Edgecombe County?

January 31. A form must reach the office or carry a postmark by then, and a late form draws a 10% penalty per year. If the 31st falls on a weekend, the period runs to the next business day.

Where do I start if I think my Edgecombe County value is wrong?

Begin with an informal review: call 252-641-7855 or send the review form. If that does not settle it, file a hearing request with the Board of Equalization and Review before it adjourns.

Is Edgecombe County property revalued each year?

No. State law requires a revaluation at least every eight years, and the last one here took effect January 1, 2024. Between revaluations a house is relisted only when its buildings change.

How can I see whether an Edgecombe County parcel is facing tax foreclosure?

Open the county's Tax Foreclosure List. It shows each parcel's description, township, number, status and file number. For upset bid details, call the Clerk of Court at 252-824-3200 Ext. 2.

Where to pay and who to call

Forsyth County Tax Administration values real and personal property and collects the county levy. Visit the Government Center at 201 North Chestnut Street, Winston-Salem, any weekday from 8 in the morning until 5 in the afternoon, or call 336-703-2300.

Send mail to Forsyth County Tax Collector, PO Box 82, Winston-Salem, NC 27102. There is a drop box by the parking deck entrance that accepts payments at any hour, and phone and online payment are available too. Credit cards add 2.25 percent with a $2.00 minimum, debit cards add $2.85 and an e-check adds $.20 up to $9,999.99.

Forsyth County tax rates

For fiscal year 2027 the county charges 55.40 cents on every $100 of assessed value, an increase of 1.88 cents over the prior year. Towns and fire districts layer their own levy over that figure. Property tax covers 61 percent of county revenue, so the budget drives the rate.

The rate sheet names ten places in all: Winston-Salem, High Point, Kernersville, King, Clemmons, Lewisville, Rural Hall, Walkertown, Tobaccoville and Bethania. Clemmons, Lewisville, Bethania and Tobaccoville carry extra fire district and local columns, so the total depends on the parcel's fire district. Winston-Salem also has a business improvement district with an extra levy.

What happens after January 5

Bills are due September 1 and can be paid without penalty through January 5. After that, interest starts at 2 percent for January and goes up by three-fourths of one percent each month.

A bill is delinquent once January 5 arrives with the September 1 charge still open. Garnishment of wages and levy on personal property may start immediately. The office can also intercept state income tax refunds and lottery winnings through debt setoff. A mailed payment counts on its USPS postmark date, and a date from a private postage meter does not substitute.

Electronic payments count when the money reaches the collector, not when you click submit. E-checks take several days, and a wrong account number gets the payment rejected, which can push you past due. Owners who have fallen behind can ask a revenue collector for a payment agreement, and current owners can start a prepayment plan in January.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Forsyth County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The 2025 reappraisal

Every real property value was reset as of January 1, 2025. In the county's words the figure is its estimate of what the parcel would likely sell for on that day.

Eight years is the legal maximum between reappraisals, yet Forsyth has generally moved every four years since 1988 to soften swings. Notices went out in the first two weeks of February 2025. One property can rise or fall independently of its neighbors, and the change in a bill depends on the new value, any personal property you own and the rate. The rate is set separately, usually in May or June.

How to contest your assessment

Start with an informal appeal to Tax Administration. When that leaves the question open, put a written request in front of the Board of Equalization and Review.

  • Formal window: January 1 through June 30 unless the county advertises another period, or 15 days after the latest value notice if that falls later.
  • Form: print the board's appeal form from the parcel's detail page, or call 336-703-2300 and the office will send one.
  • Personal property: a written appeal is due 30 days after the first notice or bill.
  • Next level: the North Carolina Property Tax Commission hears a board decision when notice is filed inside the 30 days set by G.S. 105-290. The state courts sit above it.

Reappraisal appraisers are often out of the office, so call first and leave a number for a callback, or book an appointment. Informal appeals can also be filed online through the county's eNotices portal.

Homestead and relief programs

The office takes applications for three state programs, each due by June 1, and an owner may use only one.

  • Owners who are elderly or disabled and earn $38,800 or less for 2026 can exclude $25,000 of value, or half the value if that is bigger.
  • A disabled veteran excludes $45,000 on a residence, using Form AV-9 and VA certification of a permanent and total service-connected disability.
  • The circuit breaker caps the bill at 4 percent of income (5 percent when income is up to $58,200) and defers what is left.

Once you hold the senior exclusion you reapply only if you move to a new permanent residence. The circuit breaker is different and must be renewed every year. Disabled applicants attach a certificate from a North Carolina physician or a government agency. If the recipient dies, the person required to list the property tells the office.

Selling a Forsyth County house

The bill goes to whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and the county calls payment at closing the cleanest way to avoid trouble.

  1. Ask the Tax Office for the current balance before you sign a contract.
  2. If this year's tax is not yet due, the office accepts a prepayment based on the prior year's bill.
  3. Agree with the buyer on proration. That is a private deal, and the Tax Office does not calculate it.
  4. Have the closing attorney pay what is owed from your proceeds.

Under Session Law 2006-106 a seller is released from liability for tax assessed on property that was transferred before the bill went past due. The collector can still pursue whoever owns the parcel on the past-due date, so settle it at closing anyway. A cash sale skips lender payoff steps, but the tax still has to be settled.

A title search can turn up two more things. Unpaid demolition assessments from Winston-Salem, Kernersville or the county are billed through the tax office, and if they stay unpaid the parcel can head toward foreclosure. Tax foreclosures are run by an outside attorney, with sales at noon at 175 N. Chestnut Street and upset bids of at least 5 percent more and no less than $750 (G.S. 45-21.27).

Timeline for a seller

Plan around three dates. September 1 is when the bill is due. January 5 is the last day to pay without interest. June 1 is the cutoff for relief applications. If you list in spring, your bill for the year is probably still open, and the buyer's lender will want to see it settled or prepaid.

Bring your parcel number and the most recent bill when you call 336-703-2300. The staff can tell you the balance, whether a payment agreement is in place and whether any demolition assessment is attached to the parcel. If an outside foreclosure attorney already has the file, the same line connects you to the foreclosure liaison.

County snapshot

Forsyth County has 401,718 residents as of July 1, 2025, and 184,703 housing units across 407.85 square miles of land.

The county rate is 55.40 cents per $100 of assessed value. Town and fire district levies are added, and the rate sheet prints 1.143 as the Winston-Salem total.

Where is the Forsyth County Tax Office?

At 201 North Chestnut Street in Winston-Salem, open weekdays from 8 a.m. until 5 p.m. The main line is 336-703-2300. Mail payments to PO Box 82, Winston-Salem, NC 27102.

When does a Forsyth County bill turn delinquent?

After January 5 following the September 1 due date. Interest of 2 percent applies for January, then three-fourths of one percent for each later month.

Can a tax foreclosure in Forsyth County be stopped?

Yes, by paying all taxes, interest and fees. Ask for the foreclosure liaison at 336-703-2300 to get the balance, since an outside attorney runs the case.

Must I renew the senior exclusion each year in Forsyth County?

No, unless your permanent residence changes. Tell the office if income climbs above $38,800 or the disability ends. The circuit breaker is the exception and needs a new application every year.

Who runs property tax in Franklin County

Three units make up the Franklin County Tax Office: Assessor's Office, Collections Department and GIS/Mapping. Phone 919-496-2172 for any of them, and expect voicemail at busy times.

  • Assessor: this desk lists and values land, buildings, business and personal property, and registered vehicles. Value questions go to Tax Assessor's Office, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549.
  • Collections: enforces the Machinery Act on current and past due accounts. Mail payments and certification requests to Tax Collector, P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549.
  • GIS/Mapping: keeps the parcel layer for the county.

Due dates and discounts

September 1 is the due date. Bills for 2026 go delinquent on January 6, 2027.

The county prints statements around late July or early August. A payment that arrives before September 1 earns a discount, and prepaying before the bill run is allowed. Once a bill is delinquent, collection becomes forceful, and G.S. 105-360 adds interest of 2 percent through February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for every later month or fraction of a month.

BIS Online Services, a third party, handles cards and charges a non-refundable convenience fee. Its phone line is 877-768-4775. Keep the tax year, bill number, local zip code and amount in front of you, and ring the county office at 919-496-2172 to get the amount. Mail can cross a past-due notice, so pay early and add interest if you are late.

Sellers: before you pick a closing date, get a current balance from the Collections Department.

If your lender escrows the tax

Escrow does not stop the mailing. Every bill still goes to the owner of record, and lenders take the ones they owe from a file the county supplies.

You can check that your lender paid by searching the county collection site during the second week of September or by calling 919-496-2172 and pressing option 2. It also helps to send the mortgage company a copy of the bill with your next payment. Already sold? Pass the bill to the new owner unless you plan to pay it. Deals between buyers, sellers and attorneys are not the county's business, but the tax is a lien, so a buyer will want every bill cleared at closing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Franklin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The tax certification step

Franklin County's Register of Deeds has turned away transfer deeds since April 1, 2015, unless the Tax Collector has first certified that no delinquent tax lien sits on the parcel.

There is no charge. Collections offers the service on weekdays in business hours and shuts for county holidays. Your closing attorney or you can drop in before recording. By mail, address the envelope to the Tax Collector at P.O. Box 503, Louisburg, NC 27549, and add Attention: Tax Certification. Electronic filings go through the step on their own.

Any open bill can stall the sale. Pay it yourself, or have the closing agent pay from your proceeds so the certificate gets issued.

How to dispute your assessment

Real estate appeals can be filed from January 1 until the county board of review adjourns, which is usually in May. If you receive a notice of changed value, a separate 30-day clock begins.

The January 1, 2024 revaluation sets current values. The county asks that you send the finished appeal form plus every supporting paper to Franklin County Revaluation, P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549, ahead of April. Staff look at it first. Whatever they cannot resolve gets a board hearing and a mailed decision. A filing that misses adjournment waits for the next tax year. Beyond the board sits the state Property Tax Commission, which needs notice within 30 days, and the owner must show a substantial overstatement.

Which appeal reasons the county accepts
Reason offeredCounty position
Bill is higher than before, or income is fixed in retirementNo legal basis
Prices fell or you paid less after January 1, 2024No legal basis under G.S. 105-287
Similar homes carry lower assessed valuesHas a legal basis
Highly similar sales before January 1, 2024 at far lower pricesHas a legal basis
Fire, wind or water damage still unrepaired on January 1Has a legal basis, with proof and photos
Septic permit denied, with a Health Department letterHas a legal basis

Relief for owners on a fixed income

The state offers three programs, but you may use just one: the senior or disability exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion or the circuit breaker cap.

  • An owner who is elderly or disabled and earns no more than the 2026 ceiling of $38,800 excludes $25,000 of value, or half the value where that is greater.
  • A veteran with a qualifying disability excludes $45,000 of value, and age and income do not matter.
  • The circuit breaker requires five or more years of ownership. Tax is capped at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent where income is $38,800 up to $58,200, with the excess deferred.

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor instead of the state revenue department. Income does not reduce the value itself, so a retiree with relief questions should phone the Tax Assessor's Office. Selling the home makes any circuit breaker deferral payable.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Franklin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Solid waste fee and tax liens

A solid waste availability fee rides on bills for any dwelling or business with an electrical hookup, and the tax is a lien on the parcel.

Money from the fee pays for trash pickup and disposal at twelve convenience centers. Each electrical connection is charged, even when nobody lives in the house full time, which means an empty house with power still owes it. The commissioners set a new amount every year in the budget ordinance, so call the Tax Office for your parcel's figure.

When a bill stays unpaid, the lien dates back to the listing date under G.S. 105-355. The county may then foreclose in court under G.S. 105-374, with a sale at the courthouse door and a 10-day period for higher bids. Someone in bankruptcy still receives bills, but the collector cannot chase delinquent tax while the case is open.

Selling with back taxes or an inherited house

An inherited house carries the same lien. The tax collector can tell you which years are open. Before the court confirms a foreclosure sale, a person redeeming under G.S. 105-374 pays taxes, penalties, interest and costs to clear the debt.

  1. Call Collections for the unpaid years and a payoff figure.
  2. Get the certification stamped before the deed is taken to the Register of Deeds.
  3. Let the closing agent settle the balance out of what you receive.

Selling for cash does not remove any of this. Every transfer needs the lien cleared and the certificate issued.

Franklin County growth

Growth defines the county. Population reached 82,037 by mid-2025, compared with 68,625 in 2020, spread over 491.80 square miles of land. Homeowners live in 78.6 percent of occupied housing, and the median owner-occupied value is $284,300.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

On what date do 2026 Franklin County bills go delinquent?

January 6, 2027, after the September 1 due date.

Will Franklin County record my deed without a tax certification?

No, a real property transfer needs the Tax Collector to certify first that no delinquent lien exists. The stamp is free during weekday office hours.

Where does a Franklin County value appeal go?

Send the form and your papers to P.O. Box 504, Louisburg, NC 27549. You can file from January 1 until the board adjourns, or for 30 days after a changed value notice.

Does a larger bill justify a lower Franklin County value?

No. A bigger bill or a fixed income is not a legal reason. Better evidence is lower values on similar properties, sales from before 2024 or documented damage.

What number do I use to check or pay a Franklin County bill?

To check payments, dial 919-496-2172 and press option 2. To pay by card over the phone, call BIS Online Services at 877-768-4775 and expect a convenience fee.

Who runs property tax in Gaston County

The work is split in two. Valuing property and hearing appeals belong to the Tax Office, while billing and collecting belong to the Tax Collector. Walk-ins go to 128 West Main Avenue, Gastonia, NC 28052, and mail goes to P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. Weekday hours are 8:30 am to 5 pm.

Call 704-866-3158. Extension 1 reaches the Tax Collector's Office at 100 East Garrison Boulevard in Gastonia, and extension 2 reaches the Real Estate Appraisal Department. Relief program questions go to option 6, and exemptions for religious, charitable and similar property go to option 2. Under North Carolina law the assessor lists, appraises and assesses real estate, and the collector uses the remedies in the Machinery Act to collect what is billed.

2026 tax rates by district

Your bill adds the county rate to the rate for the city or town you live in, or to a fire district rate if you live outside a municipality.

Due dates and penalties

Gaston bills come due September 1, with a grace period through January 5. Taxes become delinquent on January 6.

  • Interest of 2% starts on January 6.
  • Each month after that adds three-quarters of one percent until the balance is paid.
  • Delinquent accounts face levy, wage garnishment, attachment of rent or bank accounts, in rem foreclosure and mortgage style foreclosure.
  • Business personal property is listed during January.

How to pay your Gaston County bill

You can pay online with your Property Key or parcel ID, name or address, by phone at 980-303-2276, by mail or in person.

Mailed payments go to Gaston County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. The county takes checks and money orders by mail and wants no cash in the envelope. The 100 E Garrison Boulevard site has a drive-through for cash, check or money order, and a 2.2% fee applies to cards used inside. Drop boxes sit at both tax office locations, 128 W Main Ave and 100 E Garrison Blvd. Credit card payments by web or phone carry a nominal fee and post within 48 hours. For prepayment plans call 704-866-3030 or 704-866-3037.

Appealing a Gaston County value

File one form per parcel, signed by the owner or an attorney or attorney in fact, with the Tax Office. Gaston's board hears real estate cases in spring.

The board typically adjourns in the last week of April, and the county advertises exact dates in the Gaston Gazette in March. A Notice of Value Change gives you whichever is later, adjournment or 30 days after the notice. Personal property can be appealed within 30 days of the bill. Five sworn members chosen by the commissioners sit on the board. A ruling comes within 30 days, with a letter that explains how to reach the state Property Tax Commission. Gaston presumes its value is right, so your evidence must show the value is well above market as of the last reappraisal date.

  • Bring appraisals, comparable sales, photos and, for rentals, income and expense statements.
  • Evidence must speak to January 1 of the latest reappraisal year.
  • Trouble paying is not a ground for appeal.

When is the next reappraisal?

The next countywide reappraisal is scheduled for 2027. Gaston has used a four-year cycle, with the last two reappraisals effective January 1, 2019 and January 1, 2023.

North Carolina sets eight years as the longest gap, so Gaston's four-year cycle is a local choice. In a reappraisal year an informal review comes first. You can use the online form, schedule an appointment with an appraiser or return the form that comes with the reappraisal notice. You get a decision letter, and the value may go up, go down or hold. An answer you dispute goes on to the board. Sellers listing in 2027 should read the notice carefully, because a new value changes what a buyer expects the tax to be.

Property tax relief for homeowners

Three programs for homeowners apply to a permanent residence, and an owner can receive benefit from only one.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion (G.S. 105-277.1): removes $25,000 or half the assessed value, whichever is larger, from a home and up to an acre. Age 65 or a total and permanent disability, plus income under the yearly limit, is required.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion (G.S. 105-277.1C): up to $45,000 off assessed value for a permanently and totally disabled veteran or an unmarried surviving spouse, with no age or income test. Form NCDVA-9 goes with the application.
  • Circuit breaker (G.S. 105-277.1B): tax capped at 4% of income in the lower bracket and 5% in the next, after five years of owning and living in the home, with a fresh application every year.

Apply between January 1 and June 1. Later applications need approval from the Board of Equalization and Review. Income thresholds adjust yearly, so ask the Tax Office on option 6 for the current limit. Present use value for farm and forest land needs 10 acres of agriculture, 5 of horticulture or 20 of forestry, and applications are due in January.

Selling with relief or unpaid tax

Your personal relief does not pass to the buyer, and a sale can bring a deferred tax bill. Sell the residence (or lose the owner) from January 1 to July 1 and the elderly or disabled exclusion comes off for that year. After July 1 it holds for the current year and ends the following January 1.

Selling ends circuit breaker status, and three years of deferred tax then become payable with interest. Farm and forest land that leaves present use value is billed the difference for the current and three prior years, and a buyer has 60 days to file for continued use. Because unpaid tax is a lien, a title company will want the bill cleared at closing. Our Gaston County Register of Deeds guide shows where the deed is filed once the tax is settled.

  1. Call the Tax Collector at extension 1 for a payoff.
  2. Call option 6 to find out whether relief or a deferral is attached.
  3. Have the closing attorney pay the balance at the table.

A cash buyer still needs the lien cleared, so a cash sale does not skip this.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Gaston County property tax rate for 2026?

The county rate is 0.5990. Add your city or fire district rate, such as 0.4700 for Gastonia or 0.1150 for most fire districts. Ask the Tax Office which district your parcel is in.

When do Gaston County property taxes become delinquent?

On January 6. Bills are due September 1, and 2% interest starts January 6, followed by three-quarters of one percent monthly.

Where do I file a challenge to my Gaston County assessment?

With the Tax Office, before the board adjourns, which is usually in the last week of April. A Notice of Value Change gives you the later of adjournment or 30 days.

Can I pay Gaston County property tax by phone?

Yes. Call 980-303-2276 and have your property key number from the top right corner of the tax bill. A nominal card fee applies.

When is the next Gaston County reappraisal?

The next countywide reappraisal is scheduled for 2027, after reappraisals effective January 1, 2019 and January 1, 2023.

Who handles your Granville County tax bill

Granville County Tax Administration, at 919-693-4181, is the one number for valuation, relief programs and billing. Almost every question routes there.

A contracted appraiser stands in for the assessor on informal real estate appeals. The next step up, the Board of Equalization and Review, is made up of the county commissioners. The county has five municipalities: Butner, Creedmoor, Oxford, Stem and Stovall. Each town's levy appears on the county bill beside its own line.

Owners outside every municipal boundary, and owners inside Stovall, also pay a fire district tax. That money is restricted to fire protection.

Tax rates by jurisdiction

The county rate is 0.631 per $100 of value. A town or fire district rate is added on top, depending on where the parcel sits. Inside a town, add the town rate. In the countryside, or in Stovall, add the fire district rate.

Granville County rates per $100 of value

County rate0.631

City of Oxford0.57
Town of Butner0.42

Town of Stovall0.355

The county's formula is value times the combined rate, divided by 100. Call the tax office to confirm which districts touch your address, since the boundaries decide which rows apply.

Due dates, discount and penalties

Pay a current-year bill during the window of July 1 to August 15 and the county trims 1.5% from it. Past that window the bill is due September 1, and interest does not start until January 5 passes.

  • July 1 to August 15: 1.5% off for early payment.
  • September 1: regular due date, G.S. 105-360.
  • January 5: the final day to pay face amount.
  • Afterward: 2% through February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or fraction.

Options include the website, a mailed check, the counter, your bank's bill pay and the phone. The county's card vendor also runs e-billing that sends an alert whenever a balance, an owner or a due date changes. A mailed check is judged by postmark, which means the last day is a risky day to drop it in the mail.

When is the next revaluation?

The next countywide revaluation is set for 2030. Until then, assessed real estate values reflect market conditions on January 1, 2024.

Granville finished a reappraisal in 2018 and first ran on the state's eight-year schedule. In 2020 the Department of Revenue warned that tax values and sale prices were drifting apart, so the commissioners moved to a six-year cycle. Average home sale prices in the county are up 27% since 2021.

A frozen valuation date works two ways. A later market swing, up or down, is not grounds for a different value. A factual error on the parcel record is fair game at any point in the appeal window: wrong acreage, a demolished building still listed, or a structure that was never there.

In a revaluation year the sequence runs like this: notices in January or February, informal appeals February through April, board hearings starting in April, board adjournment in June and a new rate on July 1.

How to appeal your assessment

Appeals climb three rungs: the assessor's informal review, then the commissioners acting as the equalization board, then the state Property Tax Commission.

  • Fill out the county's Assessor's Appeal Form early. The appraiser replies in writing, and if you accept the reply, you are done.
  • Still unhappy? Call 919-693-4181 and request a board hearing. Hearings start near the end of April and continue into early June.
  • The last rung is written notice to the Property Tax Commission, due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290).

When there is no revaluation that year, appeals open January 1 and close on the day the board adjourns, which is never later than early June. An owner whose value was changed by a notice mailed after adjournment gets extra time.

Personal property has its own clock. Contest within 30 days of the first notice, attend a conference, and send the board a written request within 30 days after the final answer. Vehicles are handled on a separate county page. A review might leave the figure alone, drop it or raise it, so weigh that before you file.

Relief programs that could lower a bill

North Carolina offers three ways to cut a homestead bill, and Granville's tax office (919-693-4181) can tell you which suits you. You can take just one.

  • Age 65 and up, or disabled: a slice of your home's appraised value is exempt, whichever is bigger between $25,000 and half. Income has to stay under the 2026 limit of $38,800. Statute: G.S. 105-277.1.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of value is exempt regardless of age or income. Statute: G.S. 105-277.1C.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is limited to 4.0% or 5.0% of your income, and whatever is shaved off sits as a deferred lien. Statute: G.S. 105-277.1B.

Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, who has to accept it through June 1. Sell a circuit breaker home and three fiscal years of deferred tax come due, so raise it with your closing agent early.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Granville County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Taxes you owe become a lien on the parcel dating to the January 1 listing date (G.S. 105-355), and penalties, interest and costs ride along.

Write to Granville County Tax Administration and ask for the amount due on the current bill, plus any deferred amount tied to a relief program. Give both numbers to the person running your closing.

Ignored long enough, a balance can lead to a sale on the courthouse steps (G.S. 105-374). You can still redeem before the sale is confirmed, and paying in full ends the matter. Your buyer's deed is recorded in Oxford, where the seller pays the state excise tax of $1.00 per $500, or fractional part, before the clerk accepts the filing.

A cash sale skips a lender's payoff and appraisal steps. The tax lien still has to be cleared at or before closing, so ask for the figures early and keep the receipt for your file.

Granville County housing at a glance

The county has 61,421 residents and 25,685 housing units. About 77.1% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, and the middle value of an owner's home is $247,700. A household averages 2.52 people.

About one resident in five is 65 or older (20.0%), so the age-based exclusion is worth asking about. These are countywide midpoints, and a specific parcel can sit well away from them. Before you list, pull your own bill and compare the town and fire district lines to the rate table above.

Frequently asked questions

What is Granville County's county tax rate?

The county rate is 0.631 per $100 of value. Your town or the fire district adds its own rate on top.

Does paying early save money in Granville County?

Yes. Current-year bills paid from July 1 through August 15 get 1.5% off. The regular due date is September 1.

By when must a Granville County value be challenged?

In a year without revaluation, the deadline is the day the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, no later than early June. Begin with the assessor's form.

Who can claim the $25,000 or half-value exclusion?

A homeowner age 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, who lives in the home and keeps income under the limit, which is $38,800 for 2026. Apply on Form AV-9.

Where is a Granville County deed recorded?

At the Register of Deeds in the courthouse at 101 Main Street, Oxford, phone 919-693-6314. The seller pays the excise tax to that office before recording.

Where to get help and how to pay

Guilford County's Tax Department sets values and mails bills. Walk-in help is available at 400 W. Market St. in Greensboro and 325 E. Russell Ave. in High Point, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Mailed payments are timed by postmark. With no Postal Service postmark, the day the office receives the envelope counts, and you must prove it was on time.

The 2026 reappraisal and the moratorium

Bills for 2026 carried 2025 values, so the reappraisal numbers debut on the 2027 bill. Senate Bill 889 put a one-year hold on the reappraisal that began January 1, 2026, and Guilford is covered.

Staff appraisers did the reappraisal work themselves, and owners received notices in February 2026. The next reappraisal year is 2032.

If you already appealed the 2026 value, that appeal stays alive and carries to the next bill. Commissioners set the fiscal year 2026-27 rate at 78.95 cents per $100, which is 5.9 cents higher than before. The rate rose in 2026 while the new values arrive in 2027, so the two changes land in different years.

Due dates, discount and interest

September 1 is the day a bill is payable, and a payment on or before January 5 owes no interest. Bills go out in the first half of July.

A prepayment discount rewards owners who pay by August 31. The percentage has been quoted two ways, so ask the Tax Department which figure applies to your bill.

After the cutoff, interest starts at 2% for month one and 0.75% per month beyond that. Collection steps begin immediately: garnishment of wages and bank accounts, levies on personal property, attachment of state refunds and lottery prizes, and eventually foreclosure. Guilford never runs tax lien sales.

How to appeal your assessment

Put the appeal in writing and send it to the Board of Equalization and Review any time from January 1 to May 15. The 5 p.m. cutoff moves to the next working day when May 15 lands on a weekend or holiday. Online filing is accepted, and the paper form is available from 336-641-4814.

Under the moratorium law, 2026 appeals stay open through December 31, 2026, and 2027 appeals run to May 17, 2027. The online portal reopens January 1, 2027, and taxreval@guilfordcountync.gov can mail you a form earlier.

A county appraiser reviews the file and makes a recommendation. Accept it and the matter closes. Reject it and you get a hearing date before the five-member board, where the county value starts out presumed correct and you must bring proof. Useful proof includes:

  • Closed sales of similar homes near the reappraisal date, an appraisal from the year before, or a contractor quote that attaches a dollar figure to a defect.
  • Wrong square footage on the property record card, and outside influences like a flood zone.

The board will not act on the size of an increase or on hardship paying, and it excludes forced sales from its comparables. Further review sits with the state Property Tax Commission, which takes a notice filed within 30 days after the board mails its ruling.

Relief programs

Guilford administers three programs, and an owner can collect from only one. June 1 is the filing deadline. A late packet goes to the review board if the Tax Department has it a full week ahead of the board's final December session.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters $25,000 or 50% of the home's value from tax, whichever is greater. You must be 65, or totally and permanently disabled, on January 1, with gross income under $38,800. It needs one application.
  • Circuit breaker: caps the yearly bill at 4% of income, or 5% when income falls between $38,800 and $58,200. Five years of owning and living in the home are required, and you reapply annually.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: shelters the first $45,000 of value with no age or income test. It serves a veteran whose service-connected disability is total and permanent, and that veteran's unmarried surviving spouse.

If you plan to sell, look hardest at the circuit breaker. Tax above the cap is postponed and stays on the parcel as a lien. Once the home changes hands, three years of postponed tax come due with interest. The exclusions carry no repayment. Mail applications to PO Box 3138 in Greensboro (27402) or hand them in at either tax office. Relief help lines are 336-641-3320 and 336-641-7911.

Selling with a tax balance

Pay it off no later than closing. The lien attaches to the parcel as of its January 1 listing date, with interest and penalties riding along, so a buyer's title search will turn it up.

If a lender escrows your taxes, the servicer requests the bill from the county, and a notice reaches you around mid to late July. The legal duty stays with you, so confirm the amount was paid. Without escrow, pay directly before interest starts.

Unpaid taxes can lead to a court foreclosure modeled on a mortgage foreclosure. It ends in a sale at the courthouse door, followed by ten days in which a higher bid may be filed once the commissioner reports. Selling first keeps the price with you. The Tax Department's bill search shows what is owed, and our register of deeds guide explains how the deed records afterward.

Check these before listing a Guilford house:

  • A circuit breaker deferral that comes due on transfer.
  • A parcel record that no longer matches the house after an addition. An online Property Verification form fixes this, and the record card updates in about 48 hours.
  • Vehicle gap bills, which arrive separately from the real estate bill.

A cash buyer expects clear title just as a lender does, so the tax balance gets settled the same way.

Guilford County housing

Guilford has 246,403 housing units and 562,234 residents. About 59.9% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, and the middle owned home is worth $259,900. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,536 a month, those without pay $515, and renters pay a median $1,163. Seniors make up 18.0% of the population, the group the relief programs target.

Frequently asked questions

Were Guilford's 2026 tax bills based on the new reappraisal?

No, they used 2025 values because Senate Bill 889 paused the reappraisal for a year. The new values apply to the 2027 bill, appeals filed against them are still processed, and 2032 is the next reappraisal.

When must a Guilford property owner file a value appeal?

In an ordinary year the cutoff is 5 p.m. on May 15, and the appeal has to be in hand or postmarked by then. The moratorium law extended 2026 appeals to December 31, 2026 and set May 17, 2027 for 2027 appeals.

Is there a property tax break for seniors or a disabled veteran in Guilford County?

Yes. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and under the income cap can shelter $25,000 or half the home's value, whichever is larger. A qualifying disabled veteran can shelter $45,000. File with the Tax Department by June 1.

What becomes due if a circuit breaker owner sells?

Three years of deferred tax, plus interest, come due on the transfer date, because a sale ends eligibility. Ask the Tax Department for a payoff figure before closing.

How can I pay the Guilford County tax bill?

Use the Pay It portal online or by phone, mail a check, or visit the Greensboro or High Point office. Cards add a fee, and gift cards are refused.

Halifax County, NC Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Halifax County, NC Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Halifax County? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Halifax County?

Halifax County Tax Administration

One department, Tax Administration, does the work many counties split between an assessor and a collector. The staff appraise houses and business equipment, mail the bills, accept payments, review relief and exemption requests, and maintain ownership records, tax maps and GIS layers.

The office is at 357 Ferrell Lane in the town of Halifax (zip 27839). Mail goes to P.O. Box 68. Call 252-583-2121. The counter runs half past eight to five, Monday to Friday, and the county's pay page links to online property tax payment.

Halifax County has about 46,534 residents, 25,078 homes and apartments, and a middle owned-home value of $106,200. Owners occupy 62.9% of occupied homes, and only 75 permits for new building were issued in 2025.

Taxes must be settled before a deed can record

A county rule dated January 1, 2016 tells the Register of Deeds to refuse any deed that moves title to real property until the Tax Collector certifies that the described parcel carries no lien for delinquent property tax or any other tax the collector enforces.

For a seller, that is a gate in front of closing. Staff need time to research the parcel, so the deed has to reach the collector's office between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Before recording is scheduled, ask your closing attorney to confirm the certification is done.

The county also handles town taxes through a tax agency fund. Request a payoff figure well ahead of closing and ask whether a municipal balance shows on the parcel.

Property tax rates

The ordinance for the year beginning July 1, 2026 levies $0.70 on every $100 of property listed as of January 1, 2026. Five cents of that is reserved to repay the installment contract dated May 26, 2016 that financed the school replacing Manning Elementary.

More layers may sit on top, depending on location. The ordinance also covers school supplements, fire districts and town collections for Enfield, Halifax, Hobgood, Littleton, Roanoke Rapids, Scotland Neck and Weldon.

Halifax County levies, fiscal year 2026-27

School supplement, Weldon-Halifax Administrative Unit$0.20
School supplement, Halifax County Schools Administrative Unit$0.10

Separate rates apply in eleven fire districts: Arcola, Darlington, Davie, Enfield, Halifax, Hobgood, Littleton, Rheasville, Scotland Neck, Tillery and Weldon. Phone the tax office to learn your district and whether a town rate applies to you.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Halifax County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and interest

The bill is payable September 1, and a payment made through January 5 carries no interest. Interest then runs at 2% for the rest of January and at three-fourths of a percent for each month or part month afterward.

Listing happens in January and closes January 31, though commissioners can add 30 days in an ordinary year or 60 in a revaluation year. A prepayment discount exists only when the governing board sets a schedule before the due date, so ask Tax Administration whether Halifax offers one. The postmark governs mailed checks.

The county budget moves $100,000 into a revaluation fund for 2026-27. State law requires reappraisal of real property at least every eight years. The tax office can tell you the year your current values took effect.

How to contest a valuation

Start with the county's equalization board, formally the Board of Equalization and Review. Commissioners fill that role unless a separate board has been created, and the board starts meeting in April or early May. Your request for a hearing must reach it before it adjourns.

In years without a revaluation the board finishes in a few weeks and stops by July 1. In a revaluation year it can work until December 1. A decision follows within a month of adjournment. The next level is the state Property Tax Commission, where a written notice stating your grounds is due thirty days after the board's mailing, with a copy for the assessor.

Boards respond to evidence tied to the revaluation date, such as sales of similar homes, an independent appraisal or repair quotes. Tax Administration can give you that date for Halifax.

Which relief programs can a homeowner claim?

Three state programs exist, and each owner may use just one. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor. January is the intended window, yet the assessor must accept applications through June 1 before the tax year begins.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: excludes $25,000 or 50% of the home's appraised value, whichever is more. The owner is a North Carolina resident who, as of January 1, is at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled and whose income falls below $38,800 for 2026.
  • Circuit breaker: holds the bill to 4% of income, or 5% for income between that limit and $58,200. The owner needs five years of owning and living in the home. Postponed tax stays as a lien and falls due when the home transfers.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: excludes $45,000 of value, and no age or income test applies. Form NCDVA-9 is completed first with a veteran service officer and then filed with the assessor.

Seniors make up 25.2% of Halifax's population, and 16.3% of people under 65 report a disability, so these programs reach a large share of owners.

If the tax goes unpaid

Unpaid tax becomes a lien from the January 1 listing date. To collect, the county files a foreclosure suit locally, and notice goes to the record owner, the spouse and other lienholders.

Halifax advertises each scheduled tax foreclosure on its website. The sale rules are:

  • Bidding happens in the courthouse's lower lobby in the town of Halifax.
  • Every bid stays open to upset for 10 days.
  • Property sells as is, and neither the county nor the commissioner warrants title or condition.
  • Bidders should consider a title examination, and skipping one does not release a bid.

Before confirmation, an owner can redeem by paying the tax bill together with penalties, interest and court costs. Any money left after the taxes is held by the court for those entitled to it. Selling beforehand leaves the equity in your hands. Call the county Legal Department at 252-583-3612 about a scheduled sale.

Steps for a seller

Get a payoff figure from Tax Administration and clear the balance first, which lets the collector certify the parcel. Then give your attorney the vesting deed and payoff letters. Recording follows the certification, and the register will not take the deed without it. A cash sale skips a lender's review, but the tax certification still applies. Recording after a sale is covered in our Halifax County register of deeds guide.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I find Halifax County Tax Administration?

At 357 Ferrell Lane in Halifax, with P.O. Box 68 for mail and 252-583-2121 for calls. One department handles both valuation and collection, and service runs half past eight to five on weekdays.

Which tax rate does Halifax County charge?

The 2026-27 ordinance sets $0.70 per $100 for the county. Two school administrative units add $0.20 or $0.10, and fire districts and towns add rates that vary by parcel location.

Must a seller clear delinquent taxes before a Halifax County closing?

Yes. A county rule in force since January 1, 2016 bars the register from taking a deed until the Tax Collector certifies the parcel has no delinquent tax lien. Pay any balance first so the certification can issue.

Is it possible to challenge a Halifax County assessment?

Yes. Request a hearing from the county's equalization board before it adjourns in spring. If the board's decision disappoints you, the Property Tax Commission accepts an appeal filed thirty days after the mailing at the latest.

What is a Halifax County tax foreclosure sale like?

It is a public auction in the courthouse lobby. Each bid stays open to a higher offer for 10 days, the house sells as is with no title warranty, and the county posts each notice on its website.

Who to call about a Harnett County tax bill

The Harnett County Tax Department, based in Lillington, lists, appraises and bills every parcel in the county, and its Collection Division takes the payments. For a value, call the Real Property Division at 910-814-6920. For a bill or a payment, call 910-893-7520 or write to taxinfo@harnett.org.

Collections are at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 101, Lillington, NC 27546. The register of deeds uses the same street address at Suite 200, which is handy when a sale needs both a payoff figure and a recorded deed.

Real property is listed automatically every year, so owners do not receive an annual listing form. Owners are asked to report new structures and additions, and county appraisers work from building permits issued by the county or a municipal permit office.

Tax calendar

The Harnett payment clock starts September 1 and stays penalty-free through January 5. On January 6 the balance picks up 2%, then 3/4% for every further month, as in G.S. 105-360.

For the 2026 bills, January 5, 2027 is the final day before delinquency. Owners can pay in equal monthly amounts or in any amount they choose while the bill is open, and each payment is applied to the bill with an updated statement mailed back.

Payment options and fees

Bills can be settled through the online portal, the phone line at 1-866-580-9996, the mail, or the counter, and only the counter takes cash. Checks, certified checks and money orders work at the counter or through the mail.

  • Personal debit cards carry a $3.80 convenience fee per transaction.
  • Credit cards are charged 2.50% of the balance.
  • Business credit or debit cards on high-rewards programs carry 3.25%.
  • E-checks carry $2.00 per transaction.

The processor keeps those fees. A bounced check voids the payment, and the bill is charged the larger of 10% of the check or $25.00. The office makes no payment arrangements once a bill is delinquent, so installment payers should begin before January 6.

How Harnett County values a house

The Real Property Division sets fair market value for the county's 73,000-plus parcels with a CAMA system. Inputs include site visits, zoning and soil classes, deeds, market sales and aerial photos.

The reappraisal of January 1, 2022 was followed by a move to a four-year cycle on the revenue department's recommendation, which put the next reappraisal at January 1, 2026. State law sets the outer limit at eight years under G.S. 105-286.

A structure is valued by its percent complete on January 1. A garage finished in March adds nothing to that year's bill. If you have just built or renovated, the value on the bill may lag the real condition of the house.

Disputing your assessment

Start by asking the Real Property Division how it handles value reviews after the 2026 reappraisal, and go to the county's review board if that conversation leaves a gap. Commissioners usually sit as that board, and G.S. 105-322 sets its opening session between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May.

  • Request a hearing, by letter or by appearing, before the board adjourns.
  • A written decision follows within a month of adjournment.
  • A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, with notice due thirty days after that decision is mailed.

Bring comparable sales close to the house, contractor estimates and dated photos. A value tied to January 1 of the reappraisal year is easier to contest with evidence from that date.

Relief programs for homeowners

Harnett County also offers an exemptions page and a present-use value program for farm and forest land. Three state programs for a permanent residence run through the assessor on Form AV-9, and an owner may draw on just one of them.

  • An elderly or disabled owner can exclude the larger of $25,000 or half the assessed worth of the home, if 2025 income stayed under $38,800.
  • A disabled veteran's home gets a flat $45,000 cut in taxable value, with no age or income test.
  • The circuit breaker holds tax to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% for incomes between $38,800 and $58,200, and defers the remainder as a lien.

File during the January listing period; late forms are still taken until June 1. The deferral ends at transfer, and the deferred taxes for the three prior fiscal years are then payable, so a seller using it should expect that balance at closing.

What follows when a bill goes unpaid?

Liens on unpaid real estate tax are advertised each spring in The Daily Record, under the name of the owner on January 6, with an advertising fee added to the bill.

Harnett mostly uses the mortgage-style foreclosure method, a civil action ending in a courthouse-steps auction by a court-appointed commissioner. The sale calls for a 10% deposit, then a 10-day upset bid window, and each upset bid must top the last by 5% or $750, whichever is greater. The owner can redeem before confirmation by paying all taxes, fees and costs.

The state issues no tax lien certificates, so an outsider who pays someone else's delinquent bill gets no title. Foreclosure usually comes after the office has tried bank attachments, wage garnishment, rent attachment and a sheriff's levy.

Tax at closing

Whoever owns the parcel at closing settles its tax, and the payoff is taken out of sale money at the closing table. Get a written balance from the Collection Division, with interest and any advertising fee included, before closing is scheduled.

The register of deeds collects a separate deed tax before recording, and the seller carries it. A house with delinquent tax, a foreclosure filing or a deferred balance can still sell, provided the lender and tax office are paid in the right order. A cash buyer will want the same clear title, so the payoff works the same way.

Harnett County housing

Harnett County has about 150,137 residents, up 12.4% from the 2020 base, and 59,085 housing units, 71.0% of them owner-occupied. The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $246,200, and median household income is $71,287. Permits issued during 2025 numbered 2,205. These figures help set expectations for pricing and timing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Does Harnett County reward early payment?

No. The county offers no discount on ad valorem property tax. Owners can make prepayments from February through August, which spreads the cost but earns no reduction.

What is the final day to pay a Harnett bill without a penalty?

January 5, following the September 1 due date. For the 2026 bills that is January 5, 2027, and interest begins the next morning.

Is a sale possible while Harnett taxes are unpaid?

Yes. The title agent remits the tax, interest and any advertising fee out of the seller's funds, so request an up-to-date payoff figure from the Collection Division first. A filed foreclosure case adds court costs and attorney fees to that figure.

Does Harnett County reappraise property every year?

No. The county moved to a four-year cycle after its January 1, 2022 reappraisal. Between reappraisals, values change when a property changes, such as new construction or an addition.

Where do I pay or ask about a Harnett County tax bill?

Use the online portal, the phone line at 1-866-580-9996, the mail, or the counter at 305 W. Cornelius Harnett Blvd, Suite 101, Lillington. Questions about a bill go to 910-893-7520 or taxinfo@harnett.org.

Who to call about a Haywood County tax bill

Haywood's tax work is divided between two counters inside the Historic Haywood Courthouse, 215 N. Main Street, Waynesville. Values come from the assessor in Suite 220. Bills and payments run through Collections in Suite 224.

Collections, at 828-452-6643, handles partial payments and payoff figures for a parcel that is being sold. The assessor's reappraisal line is 828-452-6734.

The county rate is not the whole bill. The county collects for 22 fire districts, 10 road maintenance districts and one sanitation district. Owners of improved property, manufactured homes and campers included, also pay a landfill fee.

The July 2025 population estimate is about 63,369, a gain of 2.1% over 2020. Of 36,637 housing units, 74.9% are lived in by their owners, at a median value of $279,200.

Due dates and penalties

Haywood mails bills in late August or early September, and payment is expected in September. No interest builds through January 5. Past that date a 2% charge applies, and 3/4% is added each time a new month begins. Paying in September is the simplest way to avoid all of it, and an owner who already knows a sale is coming should pay early so the payoff figure is a clean zero.

A bill you cannot clear by January 5 may qualify for a fixed monthly payment, so ask Collections. State law on interest is G.S. 105-360.

Ways to pay

Options are the county website, the phone line at 1-877-729-8290, the mail, a dropbox outside the courthouse, and cash at the Collections counter. An outside processor adds 3% to card payments, online or by phone, and 2% to e-checks.

  • Put only checks and money orders in the dropbox, never cash.
  • Use the mailing address printed on your bill. The lockbox is now PO Box 96270, Charlotte. A returned payment can be resent to the Waynesville office in its original envelope, which keeps the first postmark.
  • Lenders and escrow companies get no bill from the county, so give your copy to the servicer if it pays your tax.

Why was the revaluation moved to 2027?

After Hurricane Helene, Haywood pushed its reappraisal back two years, from 2025 to January 1, 2027, after confirming with the state that the delay was allowed.

Until that date, most parcels keep the 2025 value. Exceptions are properties that changed through an addition, a remodel, new construction or flooding. The 2027 numbers will follow the market as it stands then, which could move a Waynesville or Maggie Valley assessment a long way.

The proposed 2027 schedule of values, standards and rules can be read at the assessor's second-floor office. Reappraisal must happen at least every eighth year under G.S. 105-286.

Storm damage and appeals

Use the county's Damage Report Form and deliver it to the assessor by hand, by post, or at personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov. A flooded house should be reported before listing, so the assessment fits the house as it is now.

Disagreements over real property value are heard by a review board of five appointed members and one alternate, each on a one-year term. The assessor schedules its meetings as the need arises.

  • Ask to be heard before adjournment, as G.S. 105-322 requires.
  • The written decision arrives within a month after adjournment.
  • An appeal to the Property Tax Commission is due thirty days after the board mails its notice.

Before you go, gather whatever shows the damage or the value problem: photos, any repair estimates, and the Damage Report Form you already sent. Keep a copy of everything you submit. The board meets only when the assessor schedules it, so call 828-452-6734 early to ask when the next session is likely, rather than waiting until a sale is under contract.

Homestead exemption and other relief

Haywood owners can look at three state programs for a permanent residence, but only one may be claimed. Since 28.2% of residents are 65 or over, the age-based programs reach many homeowners. The application is Form AV-9, filed with the assessor.

  • Age 65 or older, or disabled, with 2026 income no higher than $38,800: half the value or $25,000 is shielded, whichever is more.
  • A veteran with a permanent, total service-connected disability gets $45,000 of value excluded.
  • The circuit breaker limits tax to 4.0% or 5.0% of income once you have lived in the home five years, and defers the balance.

The normal window is the January listing period, with applications taken through June 1. Any deferral ends when the house is transferred, so it shows up at closing.

Unpaid tax, foreclosure and selling

A foreclosure can start the day after January 5 of the collection year, though the county says it acts only on owners who ignore notices or break a payment plan. First the collector can attach bank accounts, garnish wages or rents, or levy on personal property.

Two routes exist. In an in-rem foreclosure under G.S. 105-375, the Tax Department and County Attorney handle everything. In a mortgage-style case under G.S. 105-374, an outside attorney does. Sales are public auctions in front of the Haywood County Justice Center, as is and without warranty. The buyer puts down 20% and owes the balance at the end of the 10-day period and confirmation. Upset bids must exceed the last bid by 5%, at least $750, and are filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.

A sale does not wipe out the bill. The January 1 owner stays liable for that year, so the tax payoff is part of closing.

Steps for selling with taxes due

Start by phoning Collections for the clearing amount. Hand that number to the closing attorney, who will pay it from your proceeds. Anyone with a circuit breaker deferral should ask for that balance as well, since it comes due on transfer.

Storm-damaged sellers should file the damage form first, because buyers look at whether the assessment matches the house. A cash sale skips repairs and appraisals, yet the tax payoff is still settled at the table.

Closing date matters. Sell in October and the full year's bill still belongs to you, since ownership was fixed back on January 1. A fall closing can mean the bill arrives afterward, and it should go straight to the closing attorney. Leave it unpaid and interest begins after January 5, with the parcel advertised and a fee added by March.

Frequently asked questions

When does interest start on Haywood County property tax?

Once January 5 passes. A 2% charge is added, then three-quarters of one percent more every month until the bill is paid.

Does Haywood County sell tax lien certificates?

No. North Carolina does not sell tax liens or certificates over the counter, and covering another person's delinquent bill gives you no ownership.

When is the next Haywood County revaluation?

It takes effect January 1, 2027, delayed from 2025 because of Hurricane Helene. Most parcels keep 2025 values until then.

I sold my house, so why did I get the tax bill?

Real property is taxed to whoever owned it on January 1, and a mid-year transfer leaves the seller responsible. Pay that year's tax at closing.

Where do I send storm damage reports?

To the Tax Assessor's Office at 215 N. Main Street, Suite 220, Waynesville, NC 28786, or by email to personalproperty@haywoodcountync.gov, using the Damage Report Form.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who handles property tax in Henderson County

The work is split between an Assessor, who sets values, and a Tax Collector, who bills and collects. The collector's counter is Suite 66 on the ground floor at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville, NC 28792, open weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00.

Call 828-697-4667 for an appraisal or appeal and 828-697-5595 for payments. The Assessor does not choose rates. The commissioners and the governing boards of Hendersonville, Fletcher, Saluda, Mills River, Flat Rock and Laurel Park each set their own to match their budgets.

One collector bills for the county, thirteen fire districts, Hendersonville, Laurel Park and the Henderson County portion of Saluda. There are 22 tax districts in all, counting the general county district, and rates differ with the services each provides.

For context on pricing, the county had 122,375 people in July 2025, owner-occupied homes with a median value of $351,400, 75.0% owner occupancy and 1,093 building permits issued in 2025. About 29.1% of residents are 65 or over.

How the county values property

All taxable property is valued at 100% of market value under the uniform standards in G.S. 105-283. That covers about 71,500 parcels, some 4,500 businesses with personal property, over 10,000 manufactured homes and more than 100,000 registered vehicles billed monthly.

Henderson reappraises every four years instead of waiting for the eight-year state limit in G.S. 105-286. The last reappraisal was in 2023, and the next takes effect January 1, 2027. A building still under construction on January 1 is valued by its percent complete, and a farm or forest tract in the Present-Use Value Program is assessed below market.

Property tax is expected to pay for about 50% of county operating spending in fiscal year 2027.

2027 reappraisal timeline

Henderson's schedule runs from the January 1, 2027 effective date through tax bills in August 2027. Notices of assessed value should go out around February 1, 2027, so owners see new numbers before the appeal window closes.

Henderson County 2027 reappraisal schedule
DateStep
January 1, 2027Reappraisal effective date
About February 1, 2027Notices of assessed value mailed
January 1 to April 13, 2027Informal appeals to the Assessor
April 14, 2027County review board convenes
May 14, 2027Board adjourns, closing the appeal period
By June 30, 2027Commissioners set the 2027-2028 tax rate
August 2027Tax bills mailed

If you plan to list in 2027, expect the new value to be public before buyers start asking about taxes.

How to appeal your assessment

Start with an informal written appeal to the Assessor on the county's standard form. A formal appeal goes to the county review board only if that fails to settle the value, and it must be received before the board adjourns.

  • Once a formal appeal is in, an appraiser meets you to discuss the value and check the information you supplied.
  • If you still disagree, each side presents at a public hearing.
  • The board mails its decision within 30 days of that hearing.
  • The next step is the state Property Tax Commission. Notice is due 30 days from the board's letter, and most cases are heard in Raleigh.

The statewide rules are in G.S. 105-322. Strong exhibits for a seller include recent sales of similar homes nearby, an appraisal tied to a sale contract, and repair quotes for defects a mass appraisal cannot see.

Payment methods and due dates

You can mail a check, visit the counter, pay online or use the automated phone line. The counter takes cash, check, money order and cards. A drop box in the south parking lot is emptied daily, and it is no place for cash.

  • Card and e-check payers owe a convenience fee that goes to the payment vendor.
  • Prepayments taken January through July show up as a credit once the bill is issued.
  • If you expect to be late, call before the account is delinquent. Most owners are offered a plan.
  • Mail checks to Henderson County Tax Collector, 200 N Grove St, Ste 66, Hendersonville, NC 28792.

Under G.S. 105-360, taxes are due September 1, paid at par through January 6, and carry interest after that.

Homestead exemption and other relief

With 29.1% of the county 65 or over, the age-based programs reach many owners. The Assessor handles the elderly or permanently disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, present-use value and the circuit-breaker deferral.

  • Elderly or disabled: $25,000 or half the value of the permanent residence, whichever is greater, if 2026 income is within $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 off appraised value, with no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker: tax held to 4.0% of income, or 5.0% above the $38,800 mark up to $58,200, with the excess deferred.

An owner can use only one of the three. Apply on Form AV-9, which the county accepts through June 1 before the tax year. A circuit-breaker deferral is payable when the home transfers.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Henderson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Unpaid taxes, foreclosure and selling

The Tax Collector may foreclose on real property with delinquent taxes. Sales are held on the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street. The county lists each parcel with an estimated opening bid that leaves out interest and expenses accruing daily. Ask the Clerk of Court at 828-694-4100 for upset bid amounts, and call 828-698-3090 with sale questions.

A recent county sale listed 15 parcels with estimated opening bids from $739.08 up to $14,077.24.

A seller with a balance can clear it at closing instead. Get the payoff from the Tax Collector. The seller also pays the deed excise tax of $1.00 per $500 separately.

Here is how a sale with taxes owed usually goes. Request the payoff from the Tax Collector, give it to your closing attorney, and have it paid from your proceeds so the parcel is clear when the deed is recorded. A cash buyer can close on that timeline without waiting for a lender appraisal, though the tax payoff is still settled at closing. If you cannot sell fast enough, call the collector before delinquency to ask about a plan.

Preparing to list in a reappraisal year

Sellers listing around the 2027 reappraisal have a few things to line up. When the notice of assessed value arrives, compare it with recent sales of similar homes nearby. If it looks high, file the informal written appeal before April 14, 2027, since that is when the review board convenes. Hold on to any appraisal tied to a sale contract, and get repair quotes for defects the county could not see from the street.

Remember that the value and the rate are separate. Your appeal changes the value only. The commissioners and your town set the rate by June 30, 2027, and bills follow in August 2027. If a closing falls before then, ask the closing attorney how the year's tax will be prorated and paid.

Frequently asked questions

When is the Henderson County reappraisal effective?

January 1, 2027. The county follows a four-year cycle and last reappraised in 2023, so values reset to market as of that date.

By when must a 2027 value be contested?

The review board adjourns on May 14, 2027, which closes the 2027 appeal period. Informal appeals to the Assessor run from January 1 to April 13, 2027.

Can I pay Henderson County property tax in installments?

Yes. The Tax Collector encourages monthly installments, accepts prepayments from January through July, and usually offers a payment plan if you call before the bill is delinquent.

Where are tax foreclosure sales held?

On the courthouse steps at 200 North Grove Street, Hendersonville. The Tax Collector lists each parcel with an estimated opening bid, and the Clerk of Court gives current upset bid amounts.

Who sets the Henderson County tax rate?

The Board of Commissioners sets the county rate, and each municipality sets its own. The Assessor only determines value, so an appeal changes the value and not the rate.
