Tax offices in Winton

On Justice Drive in Winton, two adjoining offices divide the job. Each keeps weekday hours through 5 p.m.

Hertford County tax offices
OfficeAddressPhone
Tax Assessor115 Justice Drive, Suite 4, Winton252-358-7810
Tax Collector115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, Winton252-358-7815

The assessor finds, identifies and appraises every taxable parcel and personal property account. The collector sends one bill that covers the county and the towns of Ahoskie, Harrellsville, Cofield, Como, Murfreesboro and Winton, plus two drainage districts, three fire districts and solid waste fees. Expect several lines on a single parcel's bill.

Due dates and penalties

The due date is September 1. On January 6 a 2 percent charge begins, and 3/4 of 1 percent more is added monthly after that.

For mail, lateness is judged by the Postal Service postmark, never a meter stamp. You may make partial payments any time between receiving the bill and January 6. Escrow does not keep the bill from reaching you, since lenders are told electronically and decide which ones to pay, so phone your lender if it is meant to cover yours.

  • Pay online, at the Winton counter, or on the toll-free line at 1-888-520-8728.
  • Card payments online carry 2.5 percent, a processor fee the county never receives.
  • The counter takes cards too.
  • A returned check costs $25.00 or 10 percent of its amount, whichever is higher, up to $1,000 under G.S. 105-357(2).

The 2027 revaluation

Real estate values reset on January 1, 2027, the first reset since 2019. Under state rules, no more than eight years may pass between reappraisals.

Appraisers divide the county into market areas, also called neighborhoods, look at recent sales in each, and apply one schedule of values so comparable houses are measured alike. An outside appraisal firm with staff from North Carolina and Virginia is doing the work, and field measuring started in July 2025 to correct listing errors and record changes since the last round. A notice of assessed value comes soon after the effective date, with appeal steps printed on it. The tax office can pull the parcel's 2018 tax card if you want the old figures beside the new.

Values will not all move in step, because the aim is fairness between owners. Rates come from the commissioners and town boards, typically in June, and a bill equals value times rate, so request the rate sheet while planning a sale.

How to appeal your value

Your notice of assessed value explains how to appeal. Forms will also appear on the Assessor's page as the revaluation date nears.

Formal appeals go before the equalization and review board, which is usually the commissioners wearing a second hat. During a revaluation year it finishes by December 1. Your request to be heard has to be in before adjournment, and the assessor can tell you that date. See G.S. 105-322.

Tax relief programs

Only one of three state relief programs may be used by an owner: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion, or the circuit breaker (G.S. 105-277.1, 105-277.1C and 105-277.1B). Apply through the county assessor on Form AV-9. State form income limit for 2026: $38,800.

Phone the Tax Assessor at 252-358-7810 to find out which program suits you and whether your parcel already has a filing. June 1 before the tax year is the last day to file, and the circuit breaker must be renewed each year. Selling can end a deferral, so bring it up before listing. The form is NCDOR Form AV-9.

Selling with taxes owed

Property tax stays with the land. G.S. 105-355 places a lien on real property as of the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs ride along. The owner named on the January 1 listing gets the bill, even if that person conveys later.

Steps for a seller:

  • Ask the collector for a payoff covering the current year and prior ones.
  • Let the closing attorney pay taxes from proceeds, language the Register of Deeds expects to see on deeds.
  • Hand any late-arriving bill to the buyer.

If a bill goes unpaid, the county can garnish wages, attach bank accounts or state income tax refunds, levy property and foreclose. Delinquent accounts can get a three-month payment plan. Auctions happen at the courthouse door, advertised in the local newspaper, and winners pay in full with cash or certified funds.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Hertford County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Getting ready to list

Before a house goes on the market, make three calls. The Tax Collector, 252-358-7815, can quote what clears the parcel. The assessor, 252-358-7810, can say whether a relief filing or deferral is attached. The tax office can send the rate sheet.

A sale near the 2027 revaluation will meet the new assessed value soon after January 1, 2027. Buyers' attorneys will see it, so learn the number and the appeal deadline early. Cash sales skip the lender's appraisal, but taxes still come out of proceeds at closing.

Vehicles, county-owned land and auctions

The Tax Collector also handles more than house bills. Motor vehicles are billed within 90 days of tag renewal, owners get one month to pay before interest starts, and after four months a block goes on the tag. The county cannot prorate or reduce a vehicle bill without the FS20 receipt from NCDMV, which must reach the office within one year of surrender. The license plate agency in Ahoskie is at 907 E. Memorial Drive.

The office lists county-owned property open for bids and foreclosed parcels with their auction dates. An outside attorney schedules foreclosure sales, and parcels that fail to sell at auction are sold by the county. You do not register ahead of time for an auction. You or a representative just appear at the courthouse door.

Homes and owners in Hertford County

The county has 8,285 households of about 2.20 people each. Owners hold 67.4 percent of the homes, and the middle-priced owned home is worth $119,200. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,285 a month, against $523 for those without. Parcels range from town lots in Ahoskie, Murfreesboro and Winton to cropland and timber, which is why the fire district and solid waste lines vary from one parcel to the next. Bring the collector's total to the closing table so nothing is left owing.

Housing costs are modest here, so a surprise tax bill at closing stings more than in a pricier market. Settle the payoff before the closing date, and confirm with the collector that the figure is current, since penalties and interest keep building each month after January 6.

Frequently asked questions

How can I pay my Hertford County tax bill?

Pay online, in person at 115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, or by calling 1-888-520-8728. Online card payments add a 2.5 percent fee, and partial payments are accepted until January 6.

Which office sends the tax bill?

The Tax Collector bills for the county, six towns, fire and drainage districts, and solid waste fees. Call 252-358-7815 with questions.

When does the next revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2027. The last one was in 2019, and owners receive notices of their new assessed values shortly after that date, with appeal instructions on the notice.

I sold my house but still got the bill. Why?

Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 is the name on the bill, so one can still arrive after you sell. Send a copy to the new owner.

Can I pay Hertford County taxes over time?

Yes for delinquent accounts. The collector offers a three-month plan, and you can ask about it at 252-358-7815.

Hoke County Tax Office

The Tax Office has two departments, both at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. Property gets listed, appraised and assessed by the Assessor. Collections handles billing and payment for real estate, personal property and delinquent motor vehicles.

Write to PO Box 1557, Raeford, NC 28376, or call 910-875-8751. The county's roll covers about 28,000 parcels of land, 700 businesses and 40,000 motor vehicles across roughly 390 square miles of land.

For context on pricing, Population climbed from 52,082 in the 2020 count to an estimated 56,939 in July 2025, in 22,440 housing units. Roughly 73.0 percent of homes are owner occupied, with a midpoint value of $219,300. Builders took out 558 permits in 2025.

Rates and fees on the bill

Four pieces can make up a bill: the county rate, a city rate, a fire district rate and a solid waste fee. Each rate is charged per $100 of value. City properties skip the fire district tax and the solid waste fee.

Sample Hoke County bill lines
Line on the billRate or fee
Hoke County rate.73 per $100 of value
City of Raeford rate.48 per $100 of value
North Raeford fire district rate.10 per $100 of value
Solid waste fee$130.00 per unit in the sample bill

No two fire districts charge the same. The Tax Office has a sheet naming the district for your parcel, and it can confirm the current Raeford rate for a house inside city limits.

Revaluation schedule

The last countywide revaluation took effect January 1, 2022, with notices going to all taxpayers on February 3, 2022. The next is set for January 1, 2030, and work starts two years before.

Eight years is the longest gap allowed between reappraisals under G.S. 105-286. Meanwhile your real property value is pegged to the January 1, 2022 market unless you build something new or the parcel changes. The assessor can show how a sale price stacks up against your 2022 value.

An appraisal sets each owner's share of the taxes that support schools, roads, parks, public health, libraries, police and fire protection. What you pay depends on your value and the rates set each year by elected county and city or town officials.

How to appeal your assessment

Send the Notice of Appeal of Assessment to the Tax Assessor ahead of the equalization board's adjournment. Newspaper and web notices announce the date, and the assessor's office will confirm it by phone. Your appeal must be in before then, so mark the date once the notice appears.

  • Each parcel needs its own form, signed by the owner or a representative: an attorney, or an attorney in fact with a power of attorney if the owner is not a corporation.
  • Evidence can be an appraisal, sales of similar properties, income and expense statements or replacement cost. Send copies with the form.
  • You must prove the value was well above true market value on the January 1, 2022 valuation date.
  • The board sets a hearing date and tells you. You can attend or send counsel.

An appraisal already handed over in an informal appeal does not have to be resent. If the county board does not settle it, you can go on to the Property Tax Commission by giving written notice within 30 days of the mailed decision. See G.S. 105-290.

Due dates and penalties

Taxes fall due September 1. G.S. 105-360 sets face value for payment before January 6, a 2 percent charge from then through February 1, and three quarters of a percent for each month afterward.

Online payment is available, and Collections takes billing questions. Mailed payments count as of the USPS postmark, so hold on to the envelope. Counties may offer prepayment discounts, and Collections can tell you if Hoke does.

A lien attaches to the parcel under G.S. 105-355 as of the listing date, and the county may foreclose in the court where the land lies. Auctions take place at the courthouse door, and a person who redeems ahead of confirmation owes the tax with penalties, interest and costs. See G.S. 105-374.

Homestead exemption and other relief

The state's three programs are the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferral, and each owner picks one. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor.

For 2026 the base income limit is $38,800 and the circuit breaker's upper tier is $58,200. June 1 before the tax year is the filing cutoff. Selling triggers the deferred tax under the circuit breaker, which is worth raising with your attorney before listing. See NCDOR Form AV-9.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Hoke County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Handling the tax bill when you sell

Ask Collections for a payoff covering the current and prior years. The lien runs from the listing date, so a current-year bill left unpaid has to be cleared at closing.

  • Let the closing attorney pay taxes out of proceeds.
  • Outside Raeford, expect a fire district tax and a solid waste fee on the bill.
  • Confirm any exclusion filing is current before the sale.
  • Keep the 2022 value notice where you can find it.

Phone Collections at 910-875-8751 early, and refresh any payoff quoted weeks ahead, because the figure changes once penalties start in January. Even a quick cash closing pays the taxes from your proceeds, so line up the number first.

Reading your bill before you list

Take last year's bill and go line by line. Every parcel carries the county rate, but a Raeford rate appears only inside the city. Outside it, you will see a fire district rate and the solid waste fee. A line that seems off deserves a call to the Tax Office before a buyer's attorney notices.

Next, check the value. The 2022 revaluation fixed values at the January 1, 2022 market, so your assessment may differ from what a buyer will pay now. That gap alone is no basis for an appeal, which must show the value was too high on the 2022 date.

A seller's timeline

The tax year looks like this for a seller. Pay the September 1 bill by January 6 and nothing extra applies. Later, 2 percent and then three quarters of a percent monthly pile on. Since the lien dates from listing, a buyer's side will want the account paid or cleared at closing before a contract goes through.

Before the first showing, collect your parcel information, latest bill, any exclusion filing and 2022 value notice. With those in hand Collections can quote a payoff fast, and a tax question will not slow the closing.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Hoke County Tax Office?

Both the Assessor and Collections are at 227 N. Main Street in Raeford. Write to PO Box 1557, Raeford, NC 28376, or call 910-875-8751.

When is the next Hoke County revaluation?

Set for January 1, 2030, with work starting two years earlier. The previous revaluation was effective January 1, 2022, and notices went out February 3, 2022.

What is the Hoke County property tax rate?

The county's sample bill shows a county rate of .73 per $100, a Raeford rate of .48 and a North Raeford fire district rate of .10. A solid waste fee can apply outside city limits, so ask for the current rate sheet.

What do I file to contest a value?

File one Notice of Appeal of Assessment per parcel with the Tax Assessor, plus evidence like appraisals or comparable sales, before the equalization board adjourns. Newspaper and website notices give that date.

Does Hoke County have a fire district tax?

Yes, outside city limits. The rate depends on the district where the property sits and is added to the county rate.

Iredell County Tax Administration

One department runs the whole system from 135 E. Water Street in Statesville. It has three divisions: assessor, tax collector and land records mapping. The commissioners set policy, but you deal with staff for almost everything.

The office opens at 8 a.m. and closes at 5 p.m. on weekdays. The assessor answers at 704-878-3017 and the collector at 704-878-3020. Mail goes to PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687. More is on the county's Tax Administration page.

  • Assessor division: listing, values, exemptions and appeals.
  • Tax collector division: bills, payments, delinquent accounts and closing payoffs.
  • Land records mapping: parcel maps and the online GIS used to find an owner of record.

A bill question goes to the collector, and a value that looks off goes to the assessor.

Housing here is busy. Mid-2025 population was 211,798 across about 93,711 housing units. The midpoint owned home is $321,400, owners occupy 71.9 percent of occupied homes, and builders took out 1,835 permits in 2025.

Tax rates

The county charges 0.50 per $100 of assessed value for 2026, matching 2025 and 2024, and the 2026-2027 budget keeps it there.

Inside a town, a municipal rate is added, along with any fire or special district. The 2026 figures below come from the county's rate chart, all per $100 of value.

Taxing unit2026 rate

Downtown districts in Statesville (.10) and Mooresville (.14) add to the bill for properties inside them.

The county also bills a flat solid waste fee of $64 per household, mobile home or apartment for 2026, and half of that for an owner with the elderly or disabled exclusion. Davidson adds a $20 privilege charge on vehicles, and Mooresville has its own solid waste fee.

Due dates and penalties

Iredell mails statements in August. Payment is due September 1, and the collector adds nothing before January 5. On January 6 a 2 percent charge applies, and 0.75 percent more joins it each later month.

The statute on due dates and interest explains the January 6 trigger. Some towns and counties offer a discount for paying early. The collector can say if yours does.

Unpaid real estate taxes are advertised in the newspaper each March, with an advertising fee added to the bill. On a delinquent account the collector may use:

  • Attachment of bank accounts
  • Debt set-off against state income tax refunds
  • Garnishment of wages or rents
  • Levy on rents or other money owed to you
  • Seizure of a vehicle or other personal assets
  • Foreclosure

Vehicle tax is a separate matter. It comes with the state tag renewal notice, and you pay it to the DMV rather than the county.

How reappraisal works

A four-year cycle puts Iredell at double the state's pace, since the minimum is eight. Values last reset January 1, 2023 and reset again January 1, 2027, and the 2027 schedule of values is on the assessor pages. G.S. 105-286 is the outer limit, and a shorter cycle is the county's choice.

Neighborhood by neighborhood, appraisers study recent sales and bring values in line with the market. Sales that are not true market deals get set aside: family transfers, gifts, trades, and forced sales that drag a price down.

The figure on your notice is what bills are based on until the next reappraisal. Listing near a revaluation date? Look up the new appraisal card on the county taxweb site before settling on an asking price.

How to appeal your assessment

The process has three steps, taken in order, laid out on the county's appeals page.

  1. Informal review: mail the appeal form and documents to the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, or use the online portal. You have 30 days from the notice date. An appraiser replies with a new notice that may lower, raise or keep the value.
  2. Review board: write out the request, naming the property and your grounds, with a signature from the owner or an attorney. Plan to mail it, and check the method with the assessor at 704-878-3017. The board opens its session in the spring window set by G.S. 105-322.
  3. State commission: still unhappy with the board's written decision? File with the Property Tax Commission within 30 days.

Anyone filing for you who is not an owner or lawyer, such as a friend or tax consultant, must attach a power of attorney or risk rejection. The county's appraisal is presumed correct at the hearing, so you carry the proof. The county wants sales contracts, MLS data or private appraisals dated 2022, plus photos of damage and surveys.

  • Accepted reasons: value out of line with market on the reappraisal date, similar properties assessed differently, or errors on the record card.
  • Rejected reasons: a big increase, inability to pay, weak county services, high taxes, or a market shift after the effective date.

Homestead exemption and other relief

A permanent residence can qualify for one of three state programs. Apply to the assessor on form AV-9.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: owners 65 or older, or totally and lastingly disabled, with 2026 income under $38,800 can exclude $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is larger.
  • Veteran exclusion: $45,000 of value comes off for a permanent, total, service-connected disability, regardless of age or income.
  • Circuit breaker: after five years in the home, tax is capped at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for incomes up to $58,200.

The filing window runs through June 1 ahead of the tax year, as the AV-9 notice shows. The circuit breaker defers the savings under a lien, and selling or moving out triggers repayment of the prior three years. If you are in it, get a payoff from the assessor before listing. Iredell also halves its solid waste fee for owners who hold the elderly exemption.

The same division handles present-use value for farm and forest owners and inventory relief for builders.

Selling and who owes the tax

Ownership is fixed on January 1, so a seller who closes later still owes that year's bill. Splitting it with the buyer is a private deal made at closing.

The collector's position is simple: a transfer does not release the seller, the transfer year's bill goes to the seller, and proration is a matter of contract. Your realtor or closing attorney can explain how it was split. Asking for payment to the collector at closing ties up loose ends, and the office accepts a prepayment at last year's rate when the new bill is not yet out.

Back taxes are the bigger danger. Under G.S. 105-355 a lien reaches the parcel on the listing date, which is why a buyer's lawyer wants the account current. The county names the owner of record at the delinquency date in its advertisement, so get a payoff figure before signing a contract.

A quick cash closing follows the same steps. Call the collector at 704-878-3020 for the payoff and have the closing attorney pay it from your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Iredell County property tax rate?

For 2026 it is .50 per $100, with Statesville, Mooresville and other towns adding theirs. Look up your town and fire district on the county rates page.

When must Iredell County taxes be paid?

September 1 is the due date, with nothing added through January 5. After that, 2 percent applies, and then 0.75 percent more monthly.

Where do I file an appeal?

Begin with the assessor at PO Box 1027, Statesville, NC 28687, inside 30 days of your notice. A written appeal to the county review board comes next, then the state Property Tax Commission.

Who pays the property tax when I sell?

If you sell after January 1, the bill for that year stays yours. Any split with the buyer comes from the contract or closing, and you may ask to pay the collector at closing.

Does Iredell County offer relief for older homeowners?

Yes. The elderly or disabled exclusion is open to owners 65 and older, or disabled, within the income limit, with applications through June 1. Those owners also pay half the solid waste fee.

Who to call about your tax bill

Tax Administration is in the Smithfield courthouse at 207 East Johnston Street, second floor. Hours are weekdays from 8 to 5, and the office closes on county holidays.

Two phone lines divide the work, as the county contact page shows:

  • 919-989-5120 (Tax Collection): your bill, payment plans, wage garnishment, bank attachment and foreclosure policy. Mail goes to P.O. Box 451, Smithfield, NC 27577.
  • 919-989-5130 (Tax Administration): listing property, valuation and relief programs. Mail goes to P.O. Box 368, Smithfield, NC 27577.

An online portal shows bills, appraisal cards and sales. The county also posts a delinquent tax file and an accounts receivable file on its downloads page, which lenders use.

Johnston County property tax rates

The county rate is 0.510 per $100 of value for the 2026 tax year, down from 0.520 the year before. The county fire protection service district adds 0.115 on top. If you live inside a town, that town's rate is added too.

The county GIS decides which districts apply to a parcel. If the districts on your bill look wrong, call 919-989-5130.

Due dates and penalties

Statements are mailed in July and the bill is due September 1. You can pay without penalty through January 5. On January 6 the balance picks up 2 percent, and then three-quarters of a percent more every month.

Billing follows whoever owned the property on January 1, but the paper statement is mailed to the owner of record on June 30. If one shows up for a house you have already sold, hand it to the buyer. Lenders pull their own data from the tax office and usually pay late in the year, so a copy sent to you is just for your files.

Owners who want installments can sign a payment agreement for the current year, accepted until the bill turns delinquent. Older unpaid years are not eligible. Ways to pay:

  • Phone: 888-327-7344, with the year and bill number
  • Web: the county pay taxes page
  • Mail: Tax Collections, P.O. Box 451
  • In person: a locked drop box at the courthouse doors

Cars and trucks are billed separately. The state tag and tax system collects vehicle tax through the Division of Motor Vehicles.

What changed with the revaluation?

The previous countywide revaluation was in 2019, and the new values took effect January 1, 2025. They drive tax bills from the summer of 2025 until the next countywide revaluation, with exceptions such as new construction.

State law at G.S. 105-286 requires every county to reappraise at least every eight years. The county hired Pearson Appraisal Service, and its own certified appraisers reviewed the results. They used aerial images, street-level images, sales data and the tax database, and made field visits to more than 115,000 properties.

Appraised value and assessed value are the same as of the revaluation date. An online home estimate can differ from the tax office figure because automated models do not check whether a sale meets the statutory test, while the county screens sales by phone calls and visits. A foreclosure sale gets careful analysis before it counts as market evidence, and your own purchase price may differ from market value.

Report changes you make to a property, such as additions, demolished buildings, or fire and flood damage. Email taxoffice@johnstonnc.gov, call 919-989-5130, or note it on the January listing form.

How to appeal your assessment

Value appeals follow a yearly calendar. The next window for real property opens in February 2027, and the county's valuation appeal form must be in by the deadline on its appeals page.

Personal property follows a different clock: the form has to reach the tax office within thirty days of the bill date. Individual and business personal property share one form, and both are on the county forms page.

After that review the next body is the equalization and review board, which G.S. 105-322 assigns to the commissioners by default. A last appeal to the state Property Tax Commission is possible under G.S. 105-290, filed with a copy to the assessor.

Listing has its own deadline. January is the listing month, and a late list adds a 10 percent penalty to the levy. Last year's improvements, untagged vehicles, boats, aircraft and business assets all go on the form. A building permit does not count as listing.

Homestead and other relief programs

The county applies three state homestead programs for 2026, and an owner picks one. File Form AV-9, available from the county forms page, and ask for the relief specialist at 919-989-5130.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: owner is 65, or permanently and totally disabled, and the owner plus spouse have combined income of $38,800 or less.
  • Circuit breaker deferment: same age or disability test, income cap of $58,200, and five years of owning and occupying the home.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: service-connected total and permanent disability, or a specially adapted housing benefit. A surviving spouse who has not remarried can also qualify.

The county wants applications before June 1 of the tax year. Farm, forest and horticultural land can qualify for present use valuation, which is a separate program filed on Form AV-5 during January listing. A tract removed from that program owes the deferred tax for the current year plus three earlier years, with interest. Builders can apply every January to exclude inventory value, for as long as three years on homes and five on commercial lots.

Selling with taxes owed

Nothing is divided for you. The county does not split or prorate a bill between buyer and seller, so the two of you settle it by contract, through the broker or the closing attorney. When a transfer happens mid-year the seller stays responsible for the bill, and any credit at closing is a private deal.

If you owe earlier years, ask collections for a payoff figure before closing. G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien to the parcel from the listing date, so the buyer's title company will want it cleared.

A sensible order of steps:

  1. Call 919-989-5120 and request the balance for every open year.
  2. Ask your closing attorney to pay the balance from your proceeds.
  3. Confirm the current-year bill and how the contract splits it.
  4. Forward any statement that arrives after closing to the buyer.

If an account stays unpaid, the county sends notices and a pre-foreclosure letter, then gives the file to a private attorney. Auctions are held on the courthouse steps, usually from about ten in the morning, and the winning bidder deposits 5 percent. The sale is not final for ten days, and any upset bid must beat the previous one by 5 percent or $750, whichever is greater. Until the court confirms the sale, you can redeem the parcel by paying the taxes, interest and costs.

A cash sale skips the listing, showings and buyer financing, but the tax lien still has to be paid at or before closing.

Johnston County at a glance

The county seat is Smithfield, and the population is 256,448, up 18.7 percent from 2020. There are about 99,408 housing units, owners live in 76.1 percent of households, and the typical owner-held home is worth $305,600. New building permits numbered 3,002 in 2025, so new construction competes with resales. Clayton, Selma, Benson, Four Oaks and other towns each levy their own rate in addition to the county's.

Frequently asked questions

What is the 2026 tax rate for Johnston County?

The county levies 0.510 per $100 for 2026, down from 0.520 in 2025. The fire protection district adds 0.115, and each town adds its own rate.

When do Johnston County property taxes become delinquent?

They turn delinquent after January 5. Interest begins January 6 at 2 percent for the first month, then three-quarters of a percent per month.

Will Johnston County divide the tax between me and the buyer?

No. The county bills the January 1 owner and does not prorate, so your broker or closing attorney should settle the split on the closing statement.

Can I spread Johnston County taxes over installments?

Yes, for the current year only. Return a payment agreement to collections before the bill goes delinquent, since prior-year balances are not eligible.

Whom do I ask about Johnston County tax relief?

Call 919-989-5130 and ask for a property tax relief specialist. The application is Form AV-9, due before June 1.

Who sends the bill

Your tax bill is mailed by the Lenoir County Tax Department, located in the administration building at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston. The phone is 252-527-7174, and the office is open weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00.

One office carries several jobs. It lists and appraises real estate, keeps ownership and transfer records, tracks exemptions, exclusions and deferrals, and mails the bills. It also bills the special districts layered over the county: fire districts, municipal service districts and drainage districts. Solid waste fees, privilege licenses and permits to move mobile homes run through the same counter.

The county website links to online bill viewing and payment, real property records, GIS maps, a scheduler for real property appeals, and listing forms for business and individual personal property. If you are selling, check the bill there first and then phone for a payoff figure.

Tax calendar and interest

September 1 is the due date, yet nothing extra is charged until January 6. From then, interest is 2 percent through February 1 and 3/4 percent per month after that, and a partial month counts as a full one. For mailed payments the postmark sets the date.

Dates that shape a Lenoir County tax year
StepWhat the law saysStatute
ListingBegins on the first business day in January and ends January 31G.S. 105-307

Next appeal levelNotice of appeal in writing to the state commission, filed within a month after the ruling is mailedG.S. 105-290

How to appeal your value

The Board of Equalization and Review decides real estate appeals. It meets in the spring and adjourns in April. Your next chance comes when the 2027 window opens on January 1, 2027.

Under G.S. 105-322 this quasi-judicial board hears disputes about how real estate and personal property were listed and appraised, and about exemption applications, exclusion requests and present-use classifications.

The deadlines are firm. Request a hearing by letter or in person before the board adjourns, and expect a written decision within 30 days after adjournment. If you are still unhappy, file notice with the state Property Tax Commission inside 30 days of the mailing date, stating your grounds and sending a copy to the assessor. The county site offers a form for scheduling a real property appeal.

Revaluation

Values were reset by a reappraisal effective January 1, 2025, following the one effective January 1, 2017. North Carolina law sets the outside limit at eight years between reappraisals of real property.

In between, a value changes only when the property does, for example through new construction or a removed building. During a reappraisal, certified appraisers visit parcels, confirm characteristics and study sales and costs so every property is measured as of the same date.

Treat the assessed figure as a tax number and not a market price. Weigh it against recent sales when choosing an asking price, and ask the office for the current assessed value on your parcel.

Homestead exemption and relief programs

Kinston's tax office handles the AV-9 form for North Carolina's three homestead breaks. Pick whichever fits, because you cannot stack them. Filing belongs in the January listing period, but the county will still take an application until June 1 of the tax year.

  • Age or disability: shields $25,000 of value or half the appraised value, whichever is greater. You must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with 2026 income at or under $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: takes $45,000 off the appraised value. Neither age nor income matters. Send Form NCDVA-9 through the assessor.
  • Circuit breaker: holds your bill to 4.0 percent of income if income is at or below the limit, or 5.0 percent if it lands between the limit and 150 percent of it. The 2026 limit is $58,200. You need five years of owning and living in the house and a new application every year, and the deferred tax comes due on a sale.

Land used for farming, horticulture or forestry can qualify for present-use value, which lowers the assessment. Lenoir County has an AV-7 form that requests an estimate of deferred taxes, a smart step before selling such land.

What landlords and business owners must list

Anyone holding personal property tied to a business or other income-producing use must file a Business Personal Property Listing Form during January. Examples include machinery, equipment, computers, furniture, fixtures, farm machinery, airplanes, supplies and construction in progress. Rental owners who keep appliances, tools or equipment for their Lenoir County units should read that list.

An account that listed last year receives its form in the mail automatically. If none arrives, ask for one during regular office hours. Organizations seeking an exemption from personal property tax must file their application by January 31.

Before December ends, the tax office also mails abstract listings to every taxpayer who listed the year before. To list real estate for the first time, such as a newly built house, call the Tax Assessor's Office.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lenoir County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Come January 1 a tax lien attaches to the parcel, and it follows the house until someone pays. At a sale, the closing attorney or title company normally asks the Lenoir County Tax Department for the amount and takes it out of the seller's proceeds.

Personal property is treated differently. An unpaid personal property bill can become a lien on every parcel the taxpayer owns in that taxing unit, which means an old boat or equipment bill can turn up against your house. Boats, jet skis, aircraft, mobile homes and unlicensed vehicles go on the January list, and a late listing draws a 10 percent penalty.

Because real estate is on a permanent listing system, you do not have to relist the house annually unless its value changed.

To keep the sale on track, phone 252-527-7174 early and ask what is owed on the parcel and on any personal property account in your name. Hand the closing attorney that number so it shows on the settlement statement. A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but the same balance still gets cleared at closing.

If the tax goes unpaid

To collect, the county can file a court action that mirrors a mortgage foreclosure, brought where the property is located. Owners of record, spouses and other lienholders receive notice.

The foreclosure sale is a public auction outside the courthouse. The steps after the bidding are short:

  • A bidder may be asked to put down as much as 20 percent.
  • The commissioner files a report on the sale within three days.
  • Ten days run from the report for anyone to object or raise the bid.
  • A fee of up to 5 percent of the price goes to the commissioner.
  • Before a judge confirms the sale, redemption is possible for whoever pays everything owed on the parcel.

If a foreclosure notice reaches you, call the tax office and a legal aid provider right away.

Checklist before you list a Kinston-area house

A few calls to the Lenoir County Tax Department can save a closing from stalling. Work through these before you accept an offer:

  1. Look up the parcel on the county site and confirm the owner name matches the deed.
  2. Ask whether any special district, such as a fire, municipal service or drainage district, adds a separate charge to the bill.
  3. Ask about any deferred tax if the land has present-use value.
  4. Find out whether a boat, aircraft, mobile home or unlicensed vehicle in your name is still unlisted or unpaid.
  5. Request the payoff figure in writing for the settlement.

None of this costs anything, and each answer is one fewer surprise for the buyer's attorney.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Lenoir County housing and income

Lenoir County has about 55,837 residents, down from 59,495 in 2010, and 27,402 housing units across 399.09 square miles. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $120,500, owners live in 59.2 percent of homes, and median rent is $861. Median household income is $45,143. At these home values a tax bill is a real share of yearly housing cost, and back taxes can eat much of a house's equity. Only 131 building permits were issued in 2025, so a resale competes mainly with other older houses.

Frequently asked questions

Which phone number reaches Lenoir County tax staff?

Dial 252-527-7174. The office is at 101 North Queen Street in Kinston and keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00.

When can I appeal my Lenoir County real estate value?

Take it to the Board of Equalization and Review, which adjourns in April. The next window opens on January 1, 2027.

Must a Lenoir County homeowner list the house each year?

No. Houses stay on the county's permanent listing system and are relisted only when their value changes. Boats, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles still have to be listed every January.

What does a late personal property listing cost in Lenoir County?

Ten percent of the tax. It applies to any listing filed after the period closes on January 31.

Can a house with unpaid Lenoir County tax be sold?

Yes. The closing pays the balance out of your proceeds. Get the figure from the tax office before you sign so it appears on the settlement statement.

Who runs property tax in Lincoln County

The Lincoln County Tax Department is on the third floor at 100 East Main Street in Lincolnton. Five divisions share the work: Land Records (maps and 9-1-1 addresses), GIS, Appraisal, Listing and Collections.

The Tax Administrator is responsible for listing, appraising and assessing all real and personal property and for collecting what is owed. The same office processes exemption and exclusion requests. For revaluation questions, call the Appraisal staff at (704) 736-8670.

The department values property at true market value, meaning what a knowledgeable buyer and seller would agree on with no pressure on either side. The county applies the uniform appraisal standards in G.S. 105-283.

Tax calendar, penalties and discounts

Bills go out each July to whoever held title on January 1. The due date is September 1. Payment stays penalty-free through January 5, or through the next business day if January 5 falls on a weekend.

An account still open on January 6 picks up a 2 percent penalty. After that, three-fourths of one percent is added on the first day of each month, and the balance becomes eligible for forced collection.

  • Pay between July 1 and August 31 and the county takes 2 percent off.
  • Commissioners set the rate by the end of June.
  • You may pay in pieces, and once this year's bill is closed you can start prepaying next year's.
  • Cash, checks, money orders, cards and e-checks all work, with a convenience fee on cards and e-checks.

Lenders with escrow accounts are not mailed notices. Most pull what they need electronically, though the borrower still gets a paper notice for personal records.

2026/2027 tax rates

Every parcel carries the county rate of 0.499 per $100 of value, plus whatever its fire district or town levies. The county rate page prints a total for each district, so the right line depends on where the parcel sits.

Lincoln County 2026/2027 rates per $100 of value, selected districts

A separate availability fee of $140.00 applies per major structure, and $70.00 per major structure for OAE participants. Maiden levies its own town rate, so owners there should call town hall. Where a house sits changes the bill by more than the county rate alone.

The 2027 revaluation

Lincoln County chose by resolution to reappraise every four years, more often than the eight-year outer limit in G.S. 105-286. The last values date from January 1, 2023, and new ones arrive on January 1, 2027.

Before each cycle, appraisers study arm's-length sales, run statistical tests, and draft a Schedule of Values that the commissioners adopt. Transfers between relatives or related companies, foreclosure sales and gifts may be set aside, since they may not show open-market prices. The 2027 Schedule of Values, Standards, and Rules has been adopted and is posted for owners.

Notices of new value usually arrive in February. The figure is meant to track market value on that January 1, so pull your parcel record before choosing an asking price. Buyers will ask what it says.

How to appeal your assessment

Begin with an informal review, requested within 30 days of the notice date. Email revaluation@lincolncountync.gov, use the online form, phone (704) 736-8670, or mail the Appraisal Division at 100 East Main Street, Third Floor, Lincolnton, NC 28092.

If the informal answer stands, put a written request before the Board of Equalization and Review. A separate 30-day clock starts on the informal outcome. The commissioners name five members and three alternates to that board, and G.S. 105-322 keeps its first session from falling before the first Monday of April. You hear the result in writing within a month.

After the board comes the Property Tax Commission, by written notice within 30 days, and then the Court of Appeals as the last stage. Any appeal can end with a value that is unchanged, lower or higher.

  • Helpful evidence: sales of comparable homes on or before the valuation date, similar parcels carrying lower values, photos of damage and repair bids.
  • Not grounds for appeal: high taxes, trouble paying, thin county services, or the size of the increase.
  • An outside appraisal helps only if it is dated before the valuation date, and the office does not advise buying one for this purpose.

Homestead exemption and relief programs

State law gives three homestead options, and an owner can claim just one. File Form AV-9 with the county tax office. The county takes it through June 1.

  • Age or disability: an exclusion equal to the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value, open to owners 65 and up, or those permanently and totally disabled, earning no more than $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: a 4 percent of income ceiling when income is within the $38,800 limit, or 5 percent from there up to $58,200. The owner must have lived in the home five years, and any excess is deferred.

Landowners who farm or grow timber can ask the office about present-use value. It requires a 5-acre tract for horticulture, 10 for agriculture or 20 for forest, plus average gross income of $1,000 a year over three years for the first two uses.

Taxes at closing

The closing attorney ordinarily prorates the year's bill between the parties, so the seller bears the months of ownership. The settlement statement should show the proration, and your attorney can explain it.

Old balances do not disappear at closing. G.S. 105-355 treats the lien as attached on the listing date, and G.S. 105-374 allows a foreclosure action that works like a mortgage foreclosure and ends in a public sale at the courthouse. Redemption before confirmation costs the tax plus penalties, interest and court costs.

Some long-time owners carry an exclusion or deferral, so ask the Tax Department whether one is attached before you list. A circuit breaker deferral comes due for the previous three years when the owner sells.

Before you list, a simple routine helps. Request the balance for every open year from Collections, check your parcel record against the new values, and give your closing attorney the figures so the settlement statement matches. A cash buyer still expects the lien to be cleared at the table.

Frequently asked questions

What date does a Lincoln County tax bill become delinquent?

After January 5, with the penalty beginning January 6.

Is there a prepayment discount in Lincoln County?

Yes, 2 percent off for payments between July 1 and August 31. Bills usually reach mailboxes in early July.

When will Lincoln County values change next?

January 1, 2027 is the next reset, four years after the one dated January 1, 2023. Owners normally see new notices in February.

Where do I send a Lincoln County value appeal?

Write to revaluation@lincolncountync.gov or call the Appraisal Division at (704) 736-8670 within 30 days of the notice date. If that fails, take a formal appeal to the review board.

Who is responsible for Lincoln County taxes at closing?

The seller pays through the day of closing, since the attorney splits the year. Back taxes sit as a lien on the parcel and are cleared at the table.

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina

Who handles your tax bill

Madison County Tax Administration is in Room 25 at 5707 Highway 25/70 in Marshall, phone 828-649-0734. Posted hours are weekdays, 8:00am to 5:00pm, and the office is closed Saturday and Sunday.

The job is split three ways. The assessor lists and values property, the county commissioners choose the rate, and a separate tax collector sends and collects the bills. Take a rate complaint to the commissioners and a value complaint to the assessor.

A Marshall town lot and a steep mountain tract sit on the same roll yet look nothing alike, so read your own parcel record before an offer arrives.

Madison County tax rates

The county-wide rate is 0.36 per $100 of value, with a fire district charge added for each parcel and a town charge where one applies. The figures below are the 2024-2025 rates. Ask tax administration for the sheet that matches your own bill.

Selected Madison County rates per $100 of value

County, all townshipsnone0.36
MarshallMA0.355
Mars HillMH0.47
Hot SpringsHS0.45
Leicester fire district090.14
Walnut fire district060.10
Laurel fire district110.03

Ten fire districts are listed, running from Laurel at the low end to Leicester at the high end. A solid waste line follows: 180.00 per household for residential, 29.00 after subsidy for elderly or disabled households, and a fee schedule for commercial users. The full list is on the Madison County tax rates page.

How the assessor sets a value

Three methods feed one number: cost, income and market. The assessor weighs what sellers and buyers have been doing and what construction costs, then settles on an assessed value for the parcel.

Land and buildings stay on the roll without re-listing. A homeowner reports only changes, such as an added garage or a demolished shed. Personal property gets listed each January, including single-wide mobile homes, boats, farm machinery, unlicensed campers and unregistered vehicles.

  • The county contracts outside help for its periodic reappraisal.
  • Ownership changes and parcel maps are kept by the assessor.
  • A GIS system shows boundaries and aerial photography.
  • New structures need an E-911 address before a building permit issues.

Compare the record with what you actually own. An outbuilding missing from the card, or the wrong acreage, is simpler to correct now than in the middle of an inspection period.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Madison County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and penalties

Bills are payable from September 1, and face value is accepted into early January. After that a penalty clock runs.

  • January 1 to 31: listing window for personal property.
  • September 1: bills due.
  • January 6: a 2 percent charge is added.
  • February 1 onward: three-fourths of one percent more, monthly.

For mail, the postmark date is the payment date. Early-payer discounts are optional for counties and towns, so ask tax administration whether one is in force. The office's page also links to online payments.

How to appeal your assessment

Complete the county's formal appeal form and send it to the Madison County Assessor's Office, 5707 US 25/70, Suite 3 Box 4, Marshall, NC 28753. The 2026 version asks for your value opinion as of January 1, 2024.

Expect questions on when you bought and for how much, the year built, fire insurance coverage, any inheritance or family sale, and improvements with their costs. Attach an independent appraisal if one exists. A house on the market needs the asking price and the broker's agreement attached, and rental property needs its latest three years of income and expense figures. Anyone filing for an owner submits an assessor-approved, notarized power of attorney.

A bigger bill is no ground for appeal. Argue the value, using comparable sales and repair estimates.

Above the assessor sits the board of equalization and review, usually the commissioners themselves, which convenes in a window running from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May. Request your hearing before it adjourns. Once its decision is mailed, the state Property Tax Commission is the next stop, with 30 days to file.

Homestead exemption and relief programs

Madison County offers an elderly and disabled exclusion, an agricultural and forestry land use program and other exemptions. An owner may draw on only one of the three state programs below.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shields the larger of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value. Applicants are 65 or over, or permanently and totally disabled, with income at or under the 2026 cap of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test on the form.
  • Circuit breaker: a 4 percent of income ceiling, rising to 5 percent when income falls between $38,800 and $58,200 (2026 numbers). Owners must have lived there five years.

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, who must take it through June 1. Circuit breaker applicants file again every year. The form is on the NCDOR Form AV-9 page.

Selling with taxes owed

The debt stays with the land. G.S. 105-355 attaches the lien at the listing date, penalties, interest and costs included, and the title agent will want it cleared when keys change hands.

Circuit breaker owners face one more item. Deferred tax from the previous three fiscal years comes due on a transfer, on the owner's death, or when the owner moves out. Madison County asks attorneys and paralegals for 10 days' notice so tax administration can produce deferred bills, which means a rushed closing can stall on paperwork.

Long-unpaid tax can end in a court foreclosure and a public auction, and tax administration's page links to those sales. Redeeming ahead of confirmation takes full payment of tax, penalties, interest and costs.

What a seller can do before listing

Madison County has about 22,553 residents, and many are long-settled families, which produces back taxes, inherited mountain land and tired houses. These steps help in each case.

  • Request a statement for every parcel, with any deferred amount.
  • Check that the tax record and the deed show the same owner name.
  • Find out which relief or land use status the buyer would inherit.
  • Commission a survey first if the acreage is in doubt.

A cash buyer can settle the tax balance from the proceeds and skip the repair list, which fits owners who want out of an overdue parcel. Closing then follows a short path: the buyer's attorney requests the payoff, the title agent confirms any deferred bill, and the tax is paid from proceeds before the deed is recorded. The same 10 day notice applies, so call tax administration at 828-649-0734 as soon as you have a buyer.

Frequently asked questions

Who answers questions about Madison County property tax?

Call Madison County Tax Administration at 828-649-0734 or stop by Room 25, 5707 Highway 25/70, Marshall. It posts weekday hours, 8:00am to 5:00pm.

Which towns have their own rate in Madison County?

Marshall (0.355), Mars Hill (0.47) and Hot Springs (0.45) each add a charge on the 2024-2025 sheet. The 0.36 county rate covers every township.

Will a larger bill alone win an appeal in Madison County?

No. The 2026 form says a rising bill is not a valid reason. Your case must be about market value on the valuation date shown.

When does Madison County start charging interest on unpaid tax?

It begins on January 6 with a 2 percent charge. Beginning February 1, three-fourths of one percent more accrues monthly.

Can a Madison County owner close a sale with tax still due?

Yes. The lien gets paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for a payoff early, and allow 10 days if deferred bills must be prepared.

Selling in Mecklenburg County?

Who handles your Mecklenburg property tax

Value and billing live in different buildings. Tax Administration sets the number and takes appeals, while the Tax Collector sends the bill and collects the money. Everything lands on one combined bill from the Collector, covering county tax plus the levies of Charlotte, Cornelius, Davidson, Huntersville, Matthews, Mint Hill and Pineville.

With an escrow account, your servicer receives the bill and you only get a notice. Ask the servicer which tax year it has already paid before you sell, so the closing attorney works from real numbers.

Mecklenburg is a large, fast-growing market: 1,233,383 people in mid 2025, with 538,576 housing units. Just over half of homes (55.1 percent) are lived in by their owners, and the median owner-occupied value was $406,800 across 2020 to 2024. Because one reappraisal touches so many parcels, the county posts a lot of guidance online, and the steps below pull the seller-relevant parts together.

Due dates and interest

The yearly pattern is steady. Bills are mailed in late July and are due September 1. Interest stays off until after January 5 (G.S. 105-360 is the rule behind that cutoff). On January 6 the bill picks up 2 percent. Each month after that adds 0.75 percent until the balance is cleared.

Yearly rhythm of a Mecklenburg County bill
DateEvent
January 1Value and ownership fixed for the year
Late JulyBills mailed
September 1Payment due
January 5Final day without interest
January 6Interest of 2 percent begins
February onAnother 0.75 percent each month

If you expect to come up short, contact Tax Administration well before December rather than waiting for interest to start.

Where and how to pay

Four routes exist. A card payment carries a vendor fee, and an e-check carries none.

  • Online at MeckNC.gov/PayTax.
  • By phone at 1-800-994-1026.
  • By post, using the envelope enclosed with the bill.
  • In person at the Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3000, between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. on weekdays. Make checks payable to the Mecklenburg County Tax Collector.

Skip your bank's bill pay if you can. A payment that bounces back cannot have its interest waived, and a bank transfer can take four business days to arrive. Billing questions go to 704-336-7600.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Mecklenburg County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The January 1, 2027 reappraisal

Mecklenburg revalues every four years, twice as often as G.S. 105-286 requires. Commissioners set January 1, 2027 as the value date.

By the fall 2026 update, 428,506 parcels had been through a first review. Median movement was about 15 percent up for houses and about 30 percent up for commercial property. Notices of Value are planned for early 2027, and the county and municipal boards set rates in spring. A higher value need not mean an equal jump in your bill, since the rate can fall.

Your property record card is online at Reval.MeckNC.gov, so look there first. The county's own example is a home credited with three bathrooms that really has two. Fixing a record before notices mail is far easier than arguing with a number afterward.

Appraisers watch market data and compare property sales when they set new values, so recent sales near your house matter once notices arrive.

How to appeal your assessment

Send appeals to the Office of Tax Administration, which passes them to the county's equalization board (BER). During a reappraisal, nothing can be filed until Notices of Value are mailed, and your notice prints its own deadline. Other years, the cutoff is the Board's adjournment. Here is the county's sequence:

  • Sign the Formal Appeal Form and submit it by email, by mail to BER Real Property Appeals, P.O. Box 31127, Charlotte, NC 28231, or in person at the Woodard Center, Suite 3500.
  • Add evidence at filing or within 45 days.
  • Watch the mail for a hearing letter roughly 30 days ahead.
  • Ask for any continuance within 10 days of that letter.
  • A written ruling should arrive inside 30 days. If you still disagree, take the case to the state's Property Tax Commission within another 30 days.

You must prove the assessment is too high. State timing rules for real property appeals sit in G.S. 105-322 and G.S. 105-290.

Vehicles and business property follow other tracks. For a registered vehicle you have 30 days after the due date shown on the combined tax and registration notice. Start with an informal email request, and pay the full tax before any hearing. Business and individual personal property can be disputed in the 30 days after the first notice of value.

Relief programs for homeowners

Three state programs exist, and one is all you may hold. Apply for any of them with Form AV-9 at the county assessor.

  • Age or disability exclusion: cuts the taxable amount by $25,000 or by half the value if that is greater. You must be 65 or over, or permanently disabled, with 2026 income no higher than $38,800 (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: takes $45,000 from the taxable value and asks nothing about age or income (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: once you have lived there five years, the bill is limited to 4 or 5 percent of income and the excess waits, deferred, until a transfer (G.S. 105-277.1B).

Ask the assessor whether your parcel carries a deferral. It becomes payable at transfer, so your attorney needs that amount along with the mortgage payoff.

Selling with taxes owed

Each year's tax becomes a lien on January 1, and penalties and interest follow it (G.S. 105-355). It stays on the parcel and passes to a buyer. If ignored, it can end in a court foreclosure.

Even a fall closing can leave the seller owing that year's bill. Let the settlement statement spell out who pays which months, and request a payoff from the Collector ahead of closing. Recording and excise tax are the Register of Deeds' business and have their own page.

If you are carrying back taxes, an open appeal or a bill you cannot cover, a written cash offer lets you pick a closing date around the tax calendar. Before any call, round up three papers: your latest bill, any AV-9 on file and the deed. Then ask the Collector for the current-year payoff and for any earlier years, and ask Tax Administration whether an appeal is still open on the parcel.

Frequently asked questions

Which date matters more for Mecklenburg County taxes, September 1 or January 5?

Both. September 1 is the due date, and January 5 is the last day with no interest. After that, 2 percent applies from January 6, followed by 0.75 percent each month.

When can I file an appeal after the 2027 notices go out?

Right away. In a reappraisal year filing opens once Notices of Value are mailed, and the notice states your last date. Attach evidence to the Formal Appeal Form or send it within 45 days.

Is there a walk-in counter for paying a Mecklenburg bill?

Yes, at the Valerie C. Woodard Center, 3205 Freedom Drive, Suite 3000, Charlotte, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Cash, cards, money orders and checks are taken.

Will a new value mean my bill rises by the same percentage?

Not necessarily. Tax equals value times rate, and rates are set in spring after values post. Compare the new rates with your new value before reacting.

Do seniors in Mecklenburg County get any property tax reduction?

They can. An owner 65 or older with income at or below $38,800 for 2026 may claim the state exclusion of $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is larger. Apply on Form AV-9 with the assessor, and note that only one state program may be used.

The Bakersville tax offices

Assessing and collecting happen in two adjoining buildings on Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville. Hours for both are 8:00 to 4:30, Monday to Friday.

  • Assessor: Suite 5 at number 26, phone 828.688.2139 extension 1407. Staff list, value and assess real and personal property.
  • Collector: number 61, phone 828.537.1627. Staff mail the bills and accept payment.

The assessor also takes applications for relief, exemptions, exclusions and Present Use Value. Seven fire districts levy a tax that the collector adds to the bill, so what you owe depends partly on where your parcel lies.

Mitchell County housing at a glance

About 15,062 people lived in Mitchell County in July 2025, up slightly from 14,903 in 2020. The county has 8,785 housing units. Owners occupy 76.3 percent of them. The survey for 2020 to 2024 puts the middle home value at $220,100 and the middle rent at $813. Builders took out 44 permits in 2025.

Older owners are a large group here, with 27.6 percent of residents 65 or over, so the relief programs described below come up often.

Tax calendar and interest

Bills fall due September 1, and no interest is added until after January 5. On January 6 the account turns delinquent and 2 percent is added, followed by 0.75 percent for every further month. A deadline on a Saturday or Sunday rolls to Monday.

Mitchell County tax year
Time of yearStep
January 1Assessment date
JanuaryListing month for changes
JulyCurrent bills processed
AugustBills mailed to January 1 owner of record
September 1Payment due
January 5Last interest-free day
FebruaryDelinquent notices go out
MarchDelinquent list advertised

State law behind the interest-free cutoff is G.S. 105-360.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Mitchell County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Paying your bill

Walk-in payers at the Tax Office may use cash, a check, or a debit or credit card. The county's online portal, at mitchell.webtaxpay.com, accepts cards and e-checks, and the vendor that runs it keeps a convenience fee.

Current taxes can be paid in monthly installments. Late balances can be spread out too, once you sign a payment agreement. If you are already behind, call 828.537.1627 before the March newspaper advertisement.

August bills are addressed to the January 1 owner of record. If you sold in, say, June, your name is still the one on the envelope, so make sure the closing papers show who handled that year.

Reporting changes in January

Changes to land, buildings or taxable personal property are reported during January. The commissioners can extend that window, and property listed late carries a 10 percent penalty. The authority is G.S. 105-307.

Taxable items include:

  • business assets,
  • untagged vehicles,
  • boats and personal watercraft,
  • untagged campers and trailers,
  • mobile homes,
  • aircraft.

Print the forms from the state revenue department, complete them and mail them to Suite 5. New construction, a removed outbuilding or a newly placed manufactured home are all worth reporting.

How to contest a valuation

Value complaints go to the equalization board, which is the county commissioners unless a separate panel has been appointed. Under G.S. 105-322 it holds its first meeting no sooner than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May.

  • Ask to be heard, by letter or at the office, before the board adjourns.
  • When a notice goes out fewer than 15 days before adjournment, your deadline is 15 days after it was mailed.
  • The board mails its ruling no later than 30 days after it adjourns.
  • To go on to the Property Tax Commission, file within 30 days (G.S. 105-290).

Real estate has to be reappraised every eight years at most, and in those years the board remains in session through December 1. Phone the assessor to learn when your parcel was last revalued and when the next round is due.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Mitchell County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Relief programs

Each owner may claim one of three state programs. The application is Form AV-9, filed with the assessor.

  • Age or disability exclusion: an exclusion of $25,000 or half the value, if that is higher. Owners must be 65 or older, or permanently disabled, with 2026 income at or under $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 is excluded from value, and age and income are not tested. Start by completing Form NCDVA-9 with a veteran service officer.
  • Circuit breaker: once you have lived in the home five years, the bill is capped at 4 percent of income, or 5 percent when 2026 income runs up to $58,200. Reapply each year.

Anything deferred under the circuit breaker is owed once the house is sold or no longer lived in, so sellers need the deferred total from the assessor. The statute is G.S. 105-277.1B.

Settling the bill before closing

Phone the Tax Collector first, at 828.537.1627. Request the amount due for this year and any earlier year, and find out whether an installment plan or payment agreement is running. An estimate will not do; your closing attorney needs the payoff in writing.

Next, call the assessor at extension 1407 and ask whether the parcel carries an exclusion or a deferred circuit breaker balance, since a deferral comes due at transfer. Collect your own papers too: the latest bill, any AV-9 you submitted, and your deed.

If you added buildings or finished new work, confirm those additions are on the record before a buyer's appraiser sees them.

What happens at the closing table

Taxes are one line among many on the settlement statement, and a few habits keep it clean.

  • Give the attorney the written payoff from the collector at least a few days before closing.
  • Settle who covers the bill mailed in August to the January 1 owner.
  • Hand over the assessor's answer on exclusions or deferred circuit breaker tax, so those amounts are counted.
  • Once the sale closes, tell the assessor where the next bill should go.

A bill that is already delinquent can still be paid out of proceeds, which is often simpler than negotiating a payment agreement while a sale is pending.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with unpaid taxes

On the January 1 listing date a lien attaches, and penalties and costs get added to it (G.S. 105-355). If the county sues under G.S. 105-374 the case ends at a courthouse-door auction.

That process takes time. Three days after the sale the commissioner files a report, and raised bids or objections have 10 days from that report. An owner may still redeem before the court confirms, by paying taxes, penalty, interest and costs. Selling first keeps the price in your hands.

A seller here can handle this in three moves: get a payoff from the collector, ask the assessor about relief or a deferral on the parcel, and pass both figures to the closing attorney. Where repairs are out of reach, a written as-is cash offer can fit that timeline.

Frequently asked questions

When does interest begin on a Mitchell County bill?

January 6. The final interest-free day is January 5. After that the charge is 2 percent for the first month and 0.75 percent for every later month.

Where is the walk-in payment counter?

At the Tax Collector's counter, 61 Crimson Laurel Circle in Bakersville, any weekday between 8:00 and 4:30. It takes cash, checks, and debit or credit cards.

Who answers questions on my assessment or exemption form?

The Tax Assessor handles both, at 828.688.2139 extension 1407. The office is at 26 Crimson Laurel Circle, Suite 5.

May I pay my bill in installments?

Yes, in monthly payments on the current year's tax. Late balances qualify too once you sign a payment agreement.

What happens if I forget to list property in January?

A 10 percent penalty is added. The regular window is the month of January unless the commissioners extend it.

Moore County, NC Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Moore County?
