The Moore County Tax Department

One department covers every step in Moore County, from listing and appraisal through billing and collection. Visit the Historic Courthouse at 1 Courthouse Square, Carthage, NC 28327, on a weekday between 8 am and 5 pm, or call 910-947-2255. Mail goes to Post Office Box 457 in Carthage.

The county's Tax page divides the work along the state statutes. Listing keeps ownership records and personal property accounts, and Appraising values land and buildings. Collecting has a current section for bills in their normal window and a delinquent section for past-due accounts.

  • Send the coupon from your bill by post, pay at the counter, or pay on the county's online page.
  • Phone 1-855-451-2620 with your bill numbers in hand.
  • Walk-in payers may use cash, checks or bank cards.
  • Credit cards and electronic checks run through InvoiceCloud, which adds a convenience fee for the cardholder.

Ask the Tax Department whether any town or district bill applies to your address in addition to the county bill.

Moore County home values

The county's population reached an estimated 110,619 by mid-2025, a 10.9% rise from the 2020 base. Total housing units reached 52,979. For 2020-2024, owners lived in 76.4% of households, and half of owner-occupied homes were valued above $351,400.

At that price level, a small percentage error in your tax value repeats every year. Read your property record card against the house as you know it.

Due dates, interest and listing

Each bill is due September 1. The grace period is set by G.S. 105-360: pay before January 6 and no interest applies; pay later and 2% is added through the end of January, then 0.75% for each month after.

January is also the listing season for personal property, including business equipment, which is listed every year. Real estate, once on the books, stays listed (G.S. 105-307). Statewide, owners list in January, with the window closing on the 31st unless an extension applies.

Selling in the fall does not erase that year's bill. Ask the closing attorney if it will be prorated or paid in full from your proceeds.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Moore County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Revaluation schedule

Revaluation here comes around every four years. The most recent one took effect January 1, 2023. The county has the next on its calendar for 2027, then every fourth year after, unless the market or state law calls for something different.

That is faster than the state floor of one reappraisal every eight years, and counties may shorten the cycle by resolution (G.S. 105-286).

Mass appraisal blends cost, market and income approaches and pins values to January 1 of the revaluation year. Values stay put between revaluations instead of tracking the market. An appraiser may still visit after a building permit, a parcel map change, or a recorded sale priced well away from the assessment. Permit data flows in from the county plus Aberdeen, Pinebluff, Pinehurst and Southern Pines.

Added heated floor area counts as an improvement, as do decks, porches, patios, storage buildings, pools and barns, and the owner is expected to report them.

How to challenge your value

Start with a signed written request or the county appeal form, sent to the Tax Department. For real estate you can appeal from each January 1 until the county's review board adjourns, a date advertised in the local newspaper.

Moore County appeal paths by property type
Property typeWhen to appealHow
Real propertyOpens January 1, ends at board adjournmentSigned request or appeal form, informal review first, then the board
Personal property, business or notThirty days counted from the bill dateSigned written request or personal property form
Registered motor vehicleThirty days counted from the bill dateSigned written request; pay the bill on time regardless

The burden is yours: show with cost, sales or income evidence from before the revaluation date that your value is out of line with nearby properties or above fair market value.

Lose at the board and you can go to the state Property Tax Commission by filing written notice within thirty days of the mailed decision (G.S. 105-290).

Homestead exclusion and other relief

A permanent residence may qualify for one of three state programs, never two. In Moore County the application goes to the county tax office.

  • Elderly or disabled homestead exclusion: an owner who is 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, and within the income limit, has $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is larger, removed from the taxable amount (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran homestead exclusion: $45,000 of value drops out of the bill, and neither age nor income is tested (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: tax is held to 4% of income for owners at or below the limit and to 5% for incomes up to 150% of it, with the extra deferred as a lien (G.S. 105-277.1B).

The 2026 income limit is $38,800, and 150% of it is $58,200. File Form AV-9 with the county, ideally in the listing period; June 1 before the tax year begins is the last day the county must take it.

A sale or move triggers repayment of the circuit breaker deferral for the prior three fiscal years, so include it in the closing payoff.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Moore County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a house that still has tax due

Yes, though the tax stays with the parcel and gets paid at closing. Real property tax becomes a lien on the listing date (G.S. 105-355), and the county may enforce that lien through the foreclosure process in G.S. 105-374.

County court handles a tax foreclosure much like a mortgage foreclosure. The house goes to auction on the courthouse steps, but before confirmation the owner can still redeem by paying the tax plus penalties and costs.

Selling before that point usually costs less. Get a payoff from the Tax Department, check for an open town bill, and pass the total to your closing attorney.

How Moore County sets the value of a house

Every parcel is valued under the 2023 Schedule of Values adopted by the Board of Commissioners, using the features the house had on January 1 of the year in question. The appraiser records those features on a Field Review Document, and owners can pull that document or a shorter property record card from the county GIS site or from the Tax Department.

The land records team builds the ownership side from the paperwork that reaches the recorder's counter or the Clerk of Court, and it also keeps the parcel data that the GIS maps display. Mass appraisal means one set of standard methods is applied to a whole group of properties, then tested statistically. No single appraiser sets a price house by house.

  • Check the square footage, bedroom and bath counts and outbuildings on your card.
  • Look at what similar houses on your street are valued at.
  • Bring sales, cost or income evidence if you disagree, since the proof rests on you.
  • Remember that a recorded sale far from the assessment can trigger a visit.

For a seller, a clean card means fewer surprises when a buyer's agent compares your tax value to the contract price.

Frequently asked questions

What are my payment options?

You can pay at the Carthage courthouse counter, through the mail, on the county website, or over the phone at 1-855-451-2620. The counter takes cash, checks and plastic, and card payments add a convenience fee.

What year did the last Moore County revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2023. The next one is scheduled for 2027, with four-year rounds after that.

How long can I contest a vehicle or personal property value?

The window is thirty days from the bill's date. Send a signed written request to the Tax Department, and pay a vehicle bill on time anyway so no late penalty builds.

Do Moore County values rise and fall with the market each year?

No. The county fixes value on the revaluation year's January 1 date and leaves it alone in between. New improvements can still draw an appraiser and change the figure.

Who accepts the elderly or disabled exclusion application?

The county tax office, on Form AV-9. It is best filed during January listing but is accepted up to June 1 before the new tax year starts, and a household can use just one of the three programs.

Who sends and collects the tax bill

A single Nash County office both sets values and takes payment. Staff there list real and personal property, assess it, and collect what is owed. Visit 120 W. Washington St., Suite 2058, Nashville, NC 27856. The phone is 252-459-9824, answered through the business day from eight until five.

Relief applications under state law go through this office too. Payments go to the collector. Anything about listing, billing or an assessed value is for the assessor's staff.

Commissioners fix the rate in spring, no later than June 30. The bill is that rate times every $100 of taxable value. Statements are mailed in July or August, and a missing one by September 15 is a reason to call the collector.

Nash County housing at a glance

Roughly 99,365 people lived in Nash County in mid-2025, 4.6% more than in 2020. A middle-of-the-market owner-occupied house is worth $191,000, and 63.6% of households own. Rent typically runs $953 monthly across 45,068 housing units.

With about a third of households renting, many local houses are landlord-owned. If that is you, the county still bills the January 1 titleholder no matter what the tenant pays.

Due dates and penalties

The bill is payable starting September 1, with no interest charged until January 5. When that date is a Saturday or Sunday the cutoff slides to the next business day. A postmark by the cutoff is accepted, but the county advises mailing a week early.

Interest on real estate and personal property starts at 2% in January and adds 0.75% each following month, as G.S. 105-360. Registered vehicles follow their own rule: 5% in the first month past due.

  • Between March 1 and June 30 the county may run delinquent real estate in the newspaper and bill the owner for the ad.
  • Enforcement can mean garnished wages, attached bank accounts or rents, foreclosure, or a hold on your state income tax refund.
  • You may prepay toward a bill that has not been issued; ask staff how.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Nash County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Selling does not cancel the year's bill for you. Liability rests on the January 1 titleholder, and a later sale leaves it in place.

Closings usually prorate the tax, but ask your agent or attorney to confirm. To be sure, have a check made out to the Tax Collector's Office at the table. When this year's bill is not yet due, the collector accepts a prepayment figured at last year's rate.

Under G.S. 105-355, the tax lien attaches to the parcel on the listing date, and no buyer or lender will accept title with it open. Once you have a closing date, ask Nashville for a written payoff figure and pass it along to whoever runs the closing.

Selling for cash drops the lender's underwriting and escrow steps, yet the tax bill is still settled out of proceeds or split between the parties.

How to appeal your assessment

Start informally. Only a failed informal appeal moves on to the county review board, and nobody may skip ahead, as the county's revaluation page spells out.

There are four ways to open the informal step.

  • By appointment, face to face with an appraiser at the West Washington Street office in Nashville.
  • Over the phone, once an appraiser agrees to call you back.
  • By mail: fill in the bottom of the appeal notice and send it with your documents to the Tax Office, marked for the Board of Equalization and Review.
  • Online, using the county's informal appeal form.

Once you get the informal answer, the formal route opens for thirty days from the notice date, and the burden is on you to show the value is wrong. Under G.S. 105-322 the board's opening session falls in a spring window, April into early May.

Fairness and accuracy of the value are the only questions before the board; ability to pay is not. Your best exhibit is a set of similar nearby homes assessed lower. A board denial can be taken to the Property Tax Commission, with written notice due one month after the ruling goes out (G.S. 105-290).

Relief programs and filing dates

Four programs exist here: an exclusion for the elderly and permanently disabled, a disabled veteran exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment, and a builder's inventory exclusion. Call (252) 459-1222 for an application, or download one from the tax forms page.

Nash County filing dates
Filing or paymentDeadline or rule
Elderly or disabled, disabled veteran, circuit breakerApplication due June 1
Builders' inventory and other reliefFiling due June 1
Other exemptions for classified parcels (Form AV-10)Filing due January 31
Personal and business personal property listingForms in hand by January 31, or a 10% late penalty
Property tax dueSeptember 1

Income limits for 2026: $38,800 covers the elderly or disabled exclusion and the circuit breaker, and $58,200 is the top of the higher circuit breaker tier. Homeowners who qualify as elderly or disabled see a flat $25,000, or half the appraised value if that is more, taken off (G.S. 105-277.1). A disabled veteran can exclude $45,000 of value regardless of age or income.

How revaluation works

Reappraisals can be no more than eight years apart under state law, each taking effect January 1 of its scheduled year (G.S. 105-286). Nash County says the goal is a fair and accurate value on every parcel.

The project covers more than 53,000 parcels, with an outside firm, Piner Appraisal, doing the work. Its appraisers also hear informal appeals. Owners are mailed the new value, and the thirty-day clock starts on that notice date.

Nash County treats market value as a price a willing buyer and seller reach with no pressure, which rules out foreclosure and family sales. If your own sale was one of those, bring different comparables.

Getting ready to list a Nash County house

Before the sign goes up, do three things in order. First, ask the Tax Collector's Office what is owed on the parcel so no surprise appears at the closing table. Second, look at your latest assessment notice and decide whether the value could hurt a buyer's appraisal; if so, the informal appeal costs nothing but a phone call. Third, tell your closing attorney which of your exemptions or deferments are in place, since those can change what is owed.

Bring the parcel number, a photo ID and any assessment notice when you visit the office on West Washington Street. A buyer paying cash will often ask for the tax payoff within days of an offer, so having it in hand keeps the sale moving.

Other items the tax office handles

The collector also serves vehicle owners, businesses and utility customers, handy if you are closing out a household or a rental.

  • Registered motor vehicle bills are sent monthly rather than in the fall, with a separate interest rule.
  • Business licenses are issued through the Tax Collector's Office.
  • Listing forms for personal and business property are due at the office by the end of January, or a 10% penalty applies.
  • County water and sewer bills can be paid by check or cash at the Tax Collections Office in the Nashville administrative building during regular hours.

The Register of Deeds is in that building too, third floor, so one trip can cover recording a deed and asking about a payoff.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Nash County due date?

Payment opens September 1 and stays penalty-free to January 5, or the next working day if that is a weekend. After that, 2% interest hits for January and 0.75% for each further month.

If I sell partway through the year, do I still owe that year's tax?

Yes, unless closing settles it. Liability follows the January 1 titleholder. Most closings prorate, and you can also pay the Tax Collector directly at the table.

How can I challenge my Nash County assessment?

Ask for an informal review by phone, mail, web form or visit. Unhappy with the outcome? The Board of Equalization and Review will hear a formal appeal filed within thirty days of the informal result.

When must Nash County relief applications arrive?

Applications for the elderly or disabled, disabled veteran, circuit breaker and builders' inventory programs are due June 1. Form AV-10 exemptions for classified parcels are due January 31.

How steep is the Nash County late listing penalty?

Ten percent of the tax. Business and personal property listings are due by January 31, and anything later is charged the penalty.

content:
New Hanover County, NC Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • New Hanover County, NC Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a New Hanover County, NC Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the New Hanover County, NC Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in New Hanover County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy New Hanover County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in New Hanover County?
We buy New Hanover County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Where to go for tax questions

The county Tax Department at 230 Government Center Drive, Wilmington, values real estate, mails the bills and takes payments. Call (910) 798-7300. The reappraisal team also answers email at reappraisal@nhcgov.com.

A bill is built from two pieces: your assessed value and a rate per $100 adopted by the county and municipal boards, normally in June. Assessed value is 100% of estimated market value as of the latest revaluation.

2026-27 tax rates

The county's general rate for fiscal year 2026-2027 is 30.6 cents per $100. Wilmington and three beach towns add rates of their own on top of that.

Rates in cents per $100, fiscal year 2026-2027
Taxing bodyCents per $100
New Hanover County30.6
County fire services (unincorporated areas only)7.25
City of Wilmington33.15
Wilmington Municipal Services District5
Carolina Beach17.12
Kure Beach19.5
Wrightsville Beach5.31

Houses outside town limits also pay a stormwater services fee, shown as a separate line on the bill.

How and when to pay

The due date is September 1. Nothing accrues through January 5; from there, G.S. 105-360 governs interest.

Each bill has four coupons, one per quarter of the total, so you can pay in installments. Ways to pay:

  • Debit or credit card, or an e-check, at the Tax Office counter.
  • InvoiceCloud online, which adds a service fee, or by phone at 1-877-309-0878.
  • The drop box outside, just right of the Government Center entrance.
  • A check mailed to PO Box 18000, Wilmington, NC 28406.

If your lender pays from escrow you will get a courtesy notice. Confirm the lender really paid. Should January 5 be at risk of slipping by, call the office before January 6 and ask about a payment plan.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your New Hanover County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Revaluation schedule

New Hanover reappraises every four years, although state law only requires eight. The commissioners picked four in 2008 because the county was growing fast, and the first four-year round took effect January 1, 2012. Current values are as of January 1, 2025, and the next revaluation is set for January 1, 2029.

Appraisers sort roughly 115,000 parcels into about 1,500 neighborhoods, study home and land sales, review parcels in the field and at a desk, and use aerial imagery and computer models. The result is a Schedule of Values that the commissioners must approve. Between revaluations, a parcel's value changes only for things like new building, damage, corrected records or a new use. Ordinary market swings wait for the next round.

A house still under construction on January 1 is taxed at whatever stage it has reached, then at full value the next year. You do not re-list real property each year, but new improvements must be reported in January, and Tax Department staff will do the listing if you ask.

What the value on your notice means

Assessed value is fair market value: the likeliest price an informed buyer and seller would agree on with neither rushed. What you paid, your insurance value and rebuilding cost are not the measure.

In a revaluation year the local boards publish a revenue-neutral rate, one that would raise the same money as the year before, and may adopt something higher or lower. A jump in value therefore does not guarantee a bigger bill, because the rate can move too. Look at both numbers before deciding to appeal.

How to appeal your value

The county's appeal form is free and you do not need a lawyer. Appeals open the day the value notice arrives and close when the review board adjourns each spring. Filing within 30 days of the notice is encouraged, because it gives staff time to review the file before any hearing.

The burden of proof is on you. Bring:

  • Sales of comparable homes that closed before January 1, 2025.
  • Photos showing condition or defects.
  • Notes on improvements the record gets wrong.
  • Optionally, a formal appraisal dated before January 1, 2025.

A dispute that survives informal review goes to the Board of Equalization and Review. Its members are local residents from brokerage, appraisal, construction and law, sitting in smaller panels. You may appear or send papers instead. The board meets from April to early May and issues a written ruling within 30 days. A further appeal goes to the state Property Tax Commission.

Any joint owner can file for the group. A business owner may send an officer, manager, W-2 employee or 25% owner. Other non-attorney helpers are limited to hardship cases such as illness, a death in the family or military deployment. Commercial owners are asked for three years of income and expense statements and a rent roll dated before January 1, 2025.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy New Hanover County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exclusions for older and disabled owners

Three state programs help older owners, disabled owners and disabled military owners. You can claim only one, and the application is Form AV-9, filed with the assessor.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes $25,000 or 50% of appraised value from taxation, whichever is larger, if 2026 income is within $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes the first $45,000 of value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: caps the bill at 4.0% of income, or 5.0% for income above the ceiling and up to $58,200, for owners with five years in the home.

File in January if you can, though forms are accepted through June 1 before the tax year. Circuit breaker enrollees reapply yearly. Taxes above the cap are deferred, not waived, so a sale brings back the preceding three years.

Selling with back taxes

Under G.S. 105-355 the lien follows the parcel, even through a sale. Call (910) 798-7300 for the balance and give the figure to the attorney or title agent running your closing.

If nothing is paid, the county can foreclose through the courts under G.S. 105-374. Paying the balance from sale proceeds closes off that path.

Get the payoff in writing, make sure it appears on the closing statement, and afterward confirm that the Tax Department posted the payment. A cash buyer can close quickly and skip lender steps, but the lien must still be cleared at the table.

Checklist before you list

Pull your latest value notice and note the assessment date. Ask the Tax Department whether your parcel has a pending appeal or any unreported improvements. Check which municipal rates apply to your address, since a Wilmington house and a Kure Beach house are billed differently. Then request a payoff figure for the closing attorney. September 1. The county takes payment without interest until January 5, and interest starts January 6.

What is the county rate this fiscal year?

Who gets paid for taxes still owed at a sale?

Onslow County, NC Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Onslow County?

Who handles billing at the Onslow Tax Office

One office does the whole job: listing and valuing property, then sending and collecting bills. Its Collections Division covers the county plus Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro, and it also takes vehicle tax on the sliver of Surf City inside Onslow.

Visit 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville any weekday; service runs from 8 until 5. Extensions: 910-989-2200 (Administration), 910-989-2201 (Listings), 910-989-2202 (Collections), 910-989-2204 (Land Records) and 910-455-7431 (Appraisal). Cash and checks work at the counter. Cards and e-checks go through the web payment portal, where a convenience charge applies.

Before you list, call Collections. A parcel may owe both a county charge and a municipal one, and Land Records handles boundary and owner name questions.

Onslow County housing snapshot

Onslow grew from 177,772 residents in 2010 to 204,576 in 2020, with an estimated 217,175 in 2025. There are 91,470 housing units and 75,265 households, 63.7 percent of them owning (2020 to 2024). Owned homes sit around $236,400 and rents around $1,265. Roughly one household in five moves in a given year, and 1,372 building permits went out in 2025.

With people moving in and out steadily, payoff and title questions come up often. Contact the tax office before you sign a contract, and ask whether any improvements you made are on the record yet, since unreported work can change the value later.

Billing calendar and interest

Bills are mailed in July and are due September 1. A bill turns delinquent once January 5 passes without payment. Registered vehicles go through the state's tag and tax system.

Interest begins January 6 under G.S. 105-360: 2 percent through February 1, then 0.75 percent a month. Liens can be advertised from March through June under G.S. 105-369.

For 2026 the due date stayed at September 1, with delinquency after January 5, 2027, even though mailing ran later than usual.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Onslow County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why are Onslow's 2026 values unchanged?

The reappraisal dated January 1, 2026 was postponed a year, so this year's bills rest on the prior reappraisal's values. Session Law 2026-8 and Session Law 2026-47 allowed the delay, and new values arrive in 2027.

Onslow reappraises every four years under a 2001 resolution, starting January 1, 2006. State law allows counties to shorten its eight year maximum.

  • Your 2026 value should mostly match 2025, with changes only for construction or other alterations as of January 1, 2026.
  • Your bill can still rise, since the tax rate set by the Board of Commissioners and by any city or fire district also drives it.
  • An appeal already filed against the 2026 reappraisal value stays alive, and the outcome applies when that value takes effect in 2027.
  • December 31, 2026 is the final day to contest the value in use this year, the delayed reappraisal value, or both.

For the 2027 tax year, the usual appeal deadlines and steps return. For the current rate on your parcel, ask the Tax Office or read the rate in the county's adopted budget, since a rate is only final once the Board of Commissioners adopts it.

How to appeal your value

Ask for an informal review first. The formal route under the Machinery Act differs by property type.

A real estate review must be requested before the spring formal appeals begin. Yearly personal property and vehicles get 30 days from the bill date.

Appeal sequence for an Onslow County parcel
StageTiming
Informal reviewBefore spring formal appeals (real estate); 30 days from billing (personal property, vehicles)
County board hearingBoard's first session falls between early April and early May; request a hearing before adjournment
State commissionWritten notice within 30 days of the mailed board ruling

The statutes behind this are G.S. 105-322 and G.S. 105-290. Because of the delay, confirm current dates with the Tax Office.

Exclusions and deferment

The county's exemption page points to exclusion and deferment options, and the General Statutes define them. Only one of these three can apply to a household.

  • G.S. 105-277.1 applies to owners who are 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled and whose income stays within $38,800 for 2026. It excludes $25,000 or half the home's value, whichever is greater.
  • G.S. 105-277.1C excludes $45,000 for a disabled veteran, whatever the age or income.
  • G.S. 105-277.1B limits tax to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent for incomes above the limit up to $58,200, with the remainder deferred as a lien.

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, ideally in January; the assessor takes it through June 1 before the tax year. The circuit breaker must be renewed annually. A sale triggers repayment of up to three years of deferred tax, so those owners should request the total before listing.

Active duty families can read the county's military page, which covers vehicles, boats and mobile homes. It asks for a current Leave and Earnings Statement at each tag renewal from anyone claiming a different home state.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Onslow County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Documents to collect before you sell

Closings move faster when tax documents are in hand. Gather these while the house is on the market.

  • The current bill for every taxing unit on the parcel, including any town that bills separately from the county.
  • A payoff from Collections with a good-through date, and a second one if closing might slip past a month end.
  • Any open appeal, since appeals filed against the delayed 2026 reappraisal value remain pending and will apply when that value takes effect in 2027.
  • Any AV-9 paperwork, if you receive an exclusion or circuit breaker benefit.
  • Land Records contact details for any boundary or owner name mismatch between the deed and the parcel record.

Commissioners adopted the FY2027 budget on June 29, and tax rates come out of that budget, so request the current rate for your parcel.

Selling with taxes owed

Unpaid tax sticks to the parcel from the listing date, together with interest and costs. If ignored, it can be advertised and foreclosed under G.S. 105-374 or 105-375, and Collections can tell you which route would apply.

Request a payoff that names each taxing unit and gives an expiry date, since interest changes on January 6 and after February 1. Add the seller's deed tax ($1 per $500 of price, paid to the register) and the recording fees in G.S. 161-10. A private cash sale lets you control price and timing and skips lender steps. If the house is empty, inherited or worn, Cash Home Buyers can quote an as-is price for comparison.

Frequently asked questions

When do Onslow bills fall due?

September 1. Bills become delinquent when unpaid after January 5 of the next year, and interest begins on January 6 under G.S. 105-360.

Where is the Onslow Tax Office?

At 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville. It opens at 8 on weekdays and closes at 5. Call 910-989-2202 for Collections or 910-989-2200 for Administration.

Is the 2026 Onslow appeal window still open?

Yes, appeals can be filed through December 31, 2026, for the value in use this year, the delayed reappraisal value or both. The usual deadlines return for 2027, so call the Tax Office.

Which towns does the Onslow County Tax Office bill for?

The county, plus Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro. Only vehicle tax is collected for the Onslow portion of Surf City.

Must a seller pay what is owed on the parcel?

Yes, until the balance is paid. Unpaid tax is a lien from the listing date. Ask Collections for a payoff and have the closing agent settle it at closing.

Who runs billing and valuation

Orange County Tax Administration handles both. The office is in the Gateway Center at 228 S. Churton Street, Suite 200, Hillsborough, and the mailing address is P.O. Box 8181, Hillsborough, NC 27278-8181.

Call 919-245-2100 or write to tax@orangecountync.gov. The Revenue and Collections division bills property tax and ambulance fees, and its counter serves weekdays until 5 p.m. A drop box outside the building takes checks and money orders but never cash.

  • Valuation, listing and appeals: Tax Administration, Suite 200
  • Bills and payment: Revenue and Collections, same suite
  • Phone payment line for cards: 919-583-6137
  • Mobile option: the MyOrangeCountyNC app for bills and scheduled payments

Revaluation dates

The latest countywide revaluation is dated January 1, 2025, the one before it January 1, 2021, and the next is set for January 1, 2029.

Four years between revaluations is shorter than the state's eight-year ceiling, which lets a county pick a quicker cycle. Appraisers used market sales, building costs and income and expense data to estimate what each parcel would have sold for on the effective date. This is mass appraisal, not an inspection of individual homes. Until 2029 your value stays pegged to January 1, 2025, whatever the market does in between.

The county's revaluation page offers a property record card search, a comparable-sales tool, the 2025 schedule of values, a sales bank, a heat map of percent increases and a map of appraisal neighborhoods. Pulling up your neighborhood before you list helps you judge whether the assessment is near a likely sale price.

Tax rates by area

Rates depend on where the house sits. Each parcel carries a rate code that stacks the county tax with any city, fire district and school special district taxes.

The county posts combined rates for the 2026 tax year per one dollar of value and updates them each July. Call 919-245-2100 to confirm what applies to your parcel.

How do you appeal a property value?

There are three steps. A county appraiser handles the informal review first, a citizen board hears formal appeals next, and the state Property Tax Commission is an optional third stop. Filing with the county costs nothing, and a lawyer is optional.

The calendar repeats each year. The most recent cycle opened informal requests January 1 through March 31, started board hearings April 30, and closed formal filings June 30. The county posts new dates on its appeals page, so check there before planning a filing.

  • You have to show the value is off from market on January 1, 2025, or out of step with comparable parcels.
  • The size of the increase and your ability to pay are not grounds for a change.
  • Useful evidence includes comparable sales near January 1, 2025, appraisals from that period, closing statements, photos and repair estimates.
  • A state appeal is due 30 days after the board's letter.

File through the online portal, by email to Reval@orangecountync.gov, by mail to P.O. Box 8181, or in person at 228 S. Churton Street.

Listing personal property each January

Owners list personal property every year and report changes to their land or buildings. The deadline is January 31, and a late filing draws a 10% penalty.

Real property stays on the books once listed, so you only return the form when you built, added on or removed a structure. Personal property that must be listed includes manufactured homes, boats, aircraft, unlicensed vehicles and the appliances or furnishings you supply in a rental. Licensed vehicles with an annual registration are not listed. Do not enclose a tax payment with the form. Pay separately using the bill instructions.

Tax relief programs

Orange County administers three state programs: the elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferment. It also points to present use value, exempt property, a builder property tax exclusion and help with the solid waste fee.

  • For tax year 2026 the income ceiling is $38,800. The disabled veteran program shields the first $45,000 of value.
  • The elderly or disabled program shields $25,000 or half the value of a primary home, whichever is larger.
  • The circuit breaker limits the bill to a slice of income and parks the remainder as a deferred lien.

An owner may use only one program. The evaluator tool on the county's relief page gives a quick read on which one fits, but you can skip it and file the application with the Tax Office.

How and when to pay

Bills fall due September 1. Interest begins January 6 under state rules, so any payment in the fall and early winter avoids it.

Payment channels are the website, the phone line, a mailed check made out to Orange County Tax Collector, the drop box and the counter, where Apple Pay and Google Pay also work. For a bill of $100 or more, five coupons let you pay in equal parts on the last day of each month, usually August to December. Other options include a pre-payment program that builds toward an estimated bill, a bank draft program and a post-billing plan. Card payments may add a convenience fee, and the county warns that it never asks for gift cards.

Selling with tax still owed

The tax stays with the parcel, so it is paid out of proceeds at closing. Get the balance and any delinquent amount from the Tax Office first.

Your closing attorney will usually pay it directly. The seller also covers the deed stamp tax at the Register of Deeds. If you cannot cover the bill, call 919-245-2100 (Option 2) and ask about the payment assistance programs before the account goes delinquent.

A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting and appraisal, but the payoff works the same way: the Tax Office confirms the amount and the closing agent pays it from your proceeds.

Orange County housing context

Orange County had about 152,498 people in July 2025, up 2.5% on 2020, across 397.56 square miles of land. The median household earns $90,089 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, and owners with a mortgage report monthly costs near $2,221. Builders pulled 666 permits in 2025.

Where do I pay Orange County property taxes?

Pay online, by calling 919-583-6137, by mail to Orange County Tax Collector at P.O. Box 8181, Hillsborough, NC 27278, at the Gateway Center drop box, or at Suite 200 of 228 S. Churton Street.

What is the next Orange County revaluation date?

January 1, 2029. Current values reflect the January 1, 2025 revaluation, and the previous one was January 1, 2021.

When can I appeal my Orange County assessment?

Appeals follow an annual calendar. Call 919-245-2100 or email reval@orangecountync.gov to learn when the next window opens.

Is there a penalty for a late listing in Orange County?

Yes. A 10% late listing penalty applies to personal property or property changes not listed by January 31.

Does a seller owe the property tax bill at closing?

In practice, yes. Any unpaid bill sits against the parcel, so the closing attorney normally pays it out of the seller's proceeds after the Tax Office confirms the amount.

Tax Office location and phone numbers

The office is inside the Pamlico County Courthouse, 202 Main Street, Bayboro, NC 28515. Letters go to Box 538 there, and the counter is staffed weekdays from eight until five.

One office does the work of both assessor and collector. It lists property, sets values, records ownership changes and collects current and past-due tax. The county commissioners appoint the Tax Administrator. The office email is tax.office@pamlicocounty.org, and three direct lines split the work.

  • Listing, for personal and business property: 252-745-3105
  • Collections and payment plans: 252-745-4125
  • Land Records: 252-745-3791
  • Fax: 252-745-4042

Yearly tax calendar

The office's key dates run from January to September and repeat each year. Ownership is fixed on January 1 and bills are due September 1.

  • January 1: ownership is declared as of this date.
  • January 5: the deadline for paying with no interest.
  • January 31: listing period ends.
  • April: the Board of Equalization and Review begins hearing appeals.
  • May 31: the deadline to settle overdue tax before the newspaper ad.
  • June 1: final day for exemption and exclusion applications.
  • July: bills go out in the mail.
  • September 1: bills come due.

After a missed January date the state adds 2% starting January 6, and from February 1 interest grows by three-fourths of one percent per month or part of one.

When is the next reappraisal?

The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2020. Call 252-745-3105 for the date of the next one.

The county calls its schedule the Octennial Plan, after the state's eight-year limit. Values track the market as of the last reappraisal date and are adjusted only at the next one. The assessor handles more than 17,000 real property parcels, plus business personal property, mobile homes and aircraft, and all of it must be valued by the same standard.

Property tax rates

The county rate is 0.7000 for 2026, up from 0.645 in 2025. Town and fire district charges stack on that, which makes location decisive.

Pamlico County has 12 tax districts, and the money pays for schools, roads, police and fire protection. The county's worked example multiplies a $100,000 value by the town and fire rate per hundred dollars for a house in Bayboro in the Triangle Fire District. Call the Tax Office to confirm which rates apply to your parcel.

Rate changes from 2025 to 2026

The county column moved from 0.645 to 0.7000, and most fire districts moved up as well. Town rates mostly held still.

A house on Goose Creek Island, one near Reelsboro and one in Bayboro can therefore draw very different bills from the same county value. Ask for the rate sheet that matches your district before you estimate what a buyer will carry.

How to contest a value

Put the request for a hearing in writing and deliver it to the board's clerk before the panel adjourns. The Tax Administrator serves as that clerk, at P.O. Box 538, Bayboro, NC 28515.

The board meets in the spring, beginning in April and adjourning in May, and the county's real estate appeal form is marked for a January through May window. You must show that the value or location was wrong or that the property was taxed in error. A taxpayer who loses at the board can go to the Property Tax Commission in Raleigh by sending written notice within a month of the mailing date, 30 days to be exact.

Relief programs and forms

The forms page carries applications and instructions for the elderly or disabled exclusion, the circuit breaker deferment and the disabled veteran exemption. It also has forms for present use value, a property tax exemption and a business property exemption.

  • The state's income ceiling for the 2026 tax year is $38,800.
  • Under the elderly or disabled program, the larger of $25,000 and half the appraised value comes off the taxable amount.
  • For a disabled veteran the first $45,000 of value is excluded, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker owners pay at most 4.0% or 5.0% of income, based on how income compares with the ceiling, and the remainder is deferred.

Applications must reach the office by June 1. Call the Listing line to ask for forms.

Selling with the tax bill outstanding

The bill follows the parcel, so closing must clear it. The yearly tax becomes a lien when property is listed, and penalties, interest and costs ride along with it.

Before picking a closing date, call Collections at 252-745-4125 for the balance. Overdue accounts get advertised after May 31. Where the county forecloses, the sale happens at the courthouse door. The seller also pays the deed stamp tax, $1 for each $500, at the deeds office ahead of recording. A closing attorney usually collects both from the proceeds.

A cash sale skips lender underwriting and appraisal, but it does not skip the tax payoff. Ask for the balance in writing so the closing agent can pay it from your proceeds.

Steps before you list

Start with the Land Records line at 252-745-3791 to confirm the parcel record matches your deed. Next ask Collections for the balance on every open year. Then check your district on the rate sheet so you know what a buyer will carry. If you receive an exclusion or deferment, ask the Listing line how a sale affects it, since circuit breaker owners repay deferred tax when they sell. Finally, hand the payoff figures to your closing attorney so they can be paid from proceeds.

Taking these steps before the sign goes up avoids delays at the closing table, whether the buyer is using a loan or paying cash.

Pamlico County housing context

Pamlico is a small, mostly owner-occupied county with an estimated 12,758 residents in 2025, 4.0% above 2020. Owners live in 82.9% of homes, and the middle value among them is $216,800. Median rent is $752. The county counts 5,456 households in 7,610 housing units, and building permits totaled 97 in 2025. District lines weigh heavily on a bill, since the rate page lists eight fire districts plus Goose Creek Island.

When are Pamlico County property taxes due?

September 1. Mailing happens in July, and January 5 is the final interest-free day.

Which number reaches the Pamlico County tax staff?

Call Collections at 252-745-4125 for payments and payment plans, or Listing at 252-745-3105 for personal and business property. The office is at 202 Main Street, Bayboro.

What is the Pamlico County tax rate?

The county rate is 0.7000 for 2026, with separate town and fire district figures added on top. Call the office to confirm your parcel's combination.

When can I appeal my Pamlico County assessment?

In spring. The Board of Equalization and Review opens in April, and the written request must reach the clerk before the board adjourns in May.

What is the deadline for tax relief applications in Pamlico County?

June 1 for exemption and exclusion applications. Use the Listing line, 252-745-3105, for forms.

Who to call about a Pender bill or a value

Both property tax offices are at 803 S. Walker Street in Burgaw. Tax Administration keeps the appraisal and listing records. Tax Collections sends the bills and takes the money. Questions about listing, billing and assessed values go to the assessment side, not to collections.

  • Value or record questions: the assessment line, (910) 259-1221.
  • Payments and balances: Tax Collections, (910) 259-1222, or P.O. Box 1047, Burgaw, NC 28425 by mail.
  • Office hours: weekdays from eight in the morning until five.

One wrinkle in Pender: some towns bill separately. Collections handles the county levy plus Burgaw, Watha, St. Helena and Atkinson. Surf City and Topsail Beach run their own billing, and their real and personal property taxes also fall due September 1. A coastal house can carry both a county bill and a town bill.

The 2026 Pender revaluation

Every real property parcel was repriced to its market value as of January 1, 2026. The previous effective date was January 1, 2019, so seven years went by between the two.

In 2023 the commissioners passed a resolution moving Pender to a four-year cycle, so the county plans to revalue again every four years after 2026. State law alone only demands an eighth-year reappraisal under G.S. 105-286. Ask Tax Administration for the next scheduled date.

A few dates from this cycle still matter:

  • Owners have until December 31, 2026 to appeal.
  • A revaluation sets worth, not the bill. Rates come later, set by the commissioners and town boards, normally by July.

Any tax figure quoted before then is a guess.

How to contest a Pender value

File the 2026 Tax Appeal Form. You can complete it online, or print it and send it to Pender County Tax Department, P.O. Box 67, Burgaw, NC 28425. Walking it into the Walker Street counter also works.

The county suggests three steps. Start by reading the property record card on the public access site for errors in square footage, features or condition. Next, run the county's sales comparison tool against your value. If the record is accurate and the number still seems too high, request a hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review and wait for the written decision.

An appeal has to be about value. A big jump or a feared tax increase is not a ground. Strong files usually include:

  • comparable sales dated before January 1, 2026
  • photographs or plans showing condition and upgrades
  • a recent fee appraisal from a purchase or refinance, if you have one

If you lose, the state Property Tax Commission is the next stop. Written notice is due a month after the county board mails its ruling (G.S. 105-290).

Pender payment calendar

Bills are mailed in late August and the tax comes due September 1. You owe no extra charge until after January 5.

Pender property tax dates
WhenWhat happens
January 1 to 31Personal property listing
Late AugustBills mailed, before September 1
September 1Real estate and personal property due
January 5Final day before interest, penalties and legal remedies
January 6Interest begins: 2% for January, then 3/4 of 1% monthly
First Wednesday in MarchUnpaid real estate taxes listed as delinquent

Vehicles on the registration cycle follow other dates. The statewide interest rule is G.S. 105-360.

Payment options are eCheck online, phone, the counter, or the box outside the building. For mail, only a Postal Service postmark sets the date, and a business meter stamp will not. Early payers can write "prepayment" plus the parcel number on a check before the bill arrives. Installment schedules are possible while no legal action is pending.

Relief programs for Pender homeowners

The state offers three tax relief programs on a primary residence, and one owner can use only one. In Pender you apply to the county assessor on Form AV-9. The form tells counties to take applications up to June 1.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or half the home's value comes off the taxable amount. Income must stay under $38,800 for 2026 (NCDOR form).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 is removed for a qualifying owner. No age or income test applies.
  • Circuit breaker: your bill is capped at 4% of income (5% if income runs up to 150% of the ceiling) and the remainder is deferred.

Full rules sit in G.S. 105-277.1 and G.S. 105-277.1C. A deferral is recorded as a lien and is repaid when the house sells. Before listing, ask the assessor whether yours carries one.

If a Pender payment bounces or runs late

A returned check or failed online payment adds a fee of 10% or $25, whichever is greater (G.S. 105-357(b)(2)), plus any interest and penalty. The county voids the receipt and wants cash, a money order or certified funds to fix it.

Collections uses the full range of remedies the general statutes allow. Its combined collection rate was 97.23% for the year closed June 30, 2025, so nearly every bill gets paid and the office follows up on the rest.

  • Delinquent real estate taxes are listed on the first Wednesday of March.
  • The last interest-free day is January 5, so a payment dated January 6 already carries the 2% charge.
  • Dates can change, so confirm with the office.

Unpaid tax can end in a foreclosure sale at the courthouse door, and G.S. 105-374 lets the owner redeem before confirmation. Contact the office long before that point.

Selling with Pender taxes owed

The year's lien rides with the land (G.S. 105-355), so your closing attorney orders a payoff and takes it from your proceeds.

  • Find out whether a town bills the parcel in addition to the county.
  • Look for a delinquent balance on the March list.
  • Verify that monthly prepayments reached the right account.
  • Ask about any deferral lien from a relief program.

If you sell ahead of the September 1 due date, you and the buyer still need to agree on who covers that year. Owners who are behind and in a hurry can request cash offers, then compare each against the net after the payoff the collector quotes. A cash sale skips the lender's timeline, though the tax payoff still comes out at closing.

Steps before you list a Pender house

A short round of calls up front keeps tax surprises off the closing table. Work through the list in order and hand the answers to your closing attorney.

  1. Call the assessment line, (910) 259-1221, and ask what value sits on the record and whether the 2026 repricing changed it.
  2. Pull the property record card online and compare square footage, features and condition with the house as it stands today.
  3. Call Tax Collections, (910) 259-1222, for the balance on each parcel and ask whether any prepayment was posted.
  4. Ask whether Surf City or Topsail Beach, or any other town, bills the parcel separately.
  5. Ask whether an exclusion or circuit breaker deferral is attached, since a sale can end it.

Bring the parcel number and your latest bill to any counter visit. Staff can then pull the account in a minute instead of searching by name.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Pender County tax office?

803 S. Walker Street in Burgaw. The office keeps weekday hours and an outside drop box for payments after closing time.

Is the 2026 appeal window still open?

Owners have until December 31, 2026 to appeal. Confirm the status with the tax department at (910) 259-1221.

Which Pender towns send their own tax bills?

Surf City and Topsail Beach bill and collect their own real and personal taxes. The county collector handles the county plus Burgaw, Watha, St. Helena and Atkinson.

Will Pender reappraise again soon?

Under the 2023 resolution, the cycle is every four years from the 2026 date. Ask the tax office to confirm the next effective date.

Does Pender allow installment payments of tax?

Yes, while no legal action is open on the account. Call before the bill turns delinquent, since the window shrinks afterward.

Roxboro tax office contacts

Value questions go to the Tax Office at 13 Abbitt Street in Roxboro. Mail goes to the Tax Assessor, PO Box 1116, Roxboro, NC 27573, and the phone number is (336) 597-1721.

Each year the commissioners set a rate once the budget is finalized in June. They pick it to raise the yield the budget needs for services such as law enforcement, solid waste, emergency services, elections, the library, health and social programs, recreation and agricultural extension.

  • Email for informal appeals: tax@personcountync.gov, the county's preferred route.
  • Mail: Person County Tax Assessor, PO Box 1116.
  • In person: the Abbitt Street office.

Before you list, the same office can tell you the value on the record and whether a relief program touches the parcel.

Person County housing at a glance

The county has 19,023 housing units and 16,063 households, with about 40,636 residents, up 4.0% from the 2020 base. Owners live in 77.3% of homes, and the typical owner-occupied house is worth $213,900. Median household income is $63,300.

Those are countywide estimates and say nothing about any one parcel. Your own assessed value on the county record is what the tax bill uses.

The latest Person County reappraisal

Values were last reset as of January 1, 2025. Owners who disagreed with a notice of value had a short window that has since closed, so the route now is the informal review described below.

The county builds a number from comparable local sales, the cost to rebuild, potential income, location, property type, and the age, size, quality, condition and style of the improvements. An owner who finds the number fair does not need to do anything.

The state requires a reappraisal at least once every eight years, and a county may choose a shorter cycle (G.S. 105-286). The 2025 schedule of values stays in force until the next one, so ask the office when that will be. The property record card shows how a given house was priced.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Person County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Informal review and formal appeals

Start by returning the form that came with your value notice to the Assessor. Appraisers on staff look it over, no hearing is held, and most owners begin this way.

Reviewers may recheck year built, square footage, bathrooms and other features. Write a daytime phone number on the form and enclose every document you want weighed. The county will not open the file until the completed form arrives.

You get a letter reporting any change. Trying the informal route first does not cost you the formal one, so decide after you read the reply.

Formal appeals go to the county equalization board. It convenes between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May and accepts requests until adjournment (G.S. 105-322). To go beyond the board, appeal to the state commission within 30 days of the mailed decision (G.S. 105-290). Call for this year's meeting schedule.

Homestead relief for Person County owners

The state has three programs, each limited to a primary residence. File by June 1. Income limits in the table are for 2026.

Person County homestead relief, 2026
ProgramMain terms
Elderly or disabled exclusionIncome $38,800 or below; 65 or totally and permanently disabled before January 1; reduction of $25,000 or 50% of value, whichever is greater, on the home and one acre
Disabled veteran exclusionHonorably discharged and 100% disabled from a service injury; $45,000 off the value of the home and one acre
Circuit breaker65 or disabled; five years of ownership and occupancy; income up to $58,200; tax limited to 4% of income at $38,800 or less, 5% above that; annual application

Under the circuit breaker, the tax above the cap is deferred and held as a lien. It is repaid, with interest, for the latest three years if the owner dies, the property changes hands, or it stops being a permanent home. When several owners hold title, all must apply and qualify, though a married couple holding as tenants by the entirety does not count as multiple owners.

Farm and forest land can qualify for a separate use-value deferral. Losing eligibility brings back the current year plus three prior years of tax. Pick up homestead applications at the Tax Office.

Due dates and interest

The bill is due September 1, and paying through January 5 costs only the face amount. After that, interest starts on January 6 (G.S. 105-360). It opens at 2%, then adds three-quarters of 1% for every month or part of a month from February 1.

  • Personal property listing runs through January 31.
  • A good-cause extension for an individual cannot go past April 15.
  • A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

Ask the Person County Tax Office for its bill mailing date, payment methods and any prepayment discount for the year you are selling.

How a Roxboro-area sale treats the tax bill

Each year's tax lien attaches as of the listing date, and penalties, interest and costs get added to it (G.S. 105-355). A buyer inherits unpaid tax unless closing clears it.

Your closing attorney will request a payoff figure from the office. When this year's bill has not gone out, buyer and seller usually agree on a split. Years of nonpayment can bring a foreclosure suit and a courthouse-door auction, with a right to redeem before confirmation (G.S. 105-374).

  • Request a balance for each parcel, farmland included.
  • Ask about deferrals tied to relief or use-value programs.
  • File the paid receipts with your closing papers.

A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval, but the tax payoff still comes out of your proceeds at closing.

Questions for the Roxboro tax office before listing

One phone call can head off a closing delay. Jot down what you hear and pass it to your attorney.

  • What is the assessed value on the record, and does the record match the house today, including any addition or demolished outbuilding?
  • Is there any balance, interest or prior-year bill on the parcel?
  • Was an informal appeal still open when the last notice was mailed?
  • Does the property carry an elderly, disabled, veteran or circuit breaker benefit, and will the sale end it?
  • Are deferred taxes recorded against the land?

Also ask how a change of owner affects any benefit. Relief applications are due June 1.

What to bring to the Tax Office

A visit goes faster with paperwork in hand. Bring your value notice or latest bill, the parcel number, and photo ID. If you plan an informal appeal, bring the completed form with comparable sales, photos of condition and any recent appraisal attached. The Abbitt Street office is also the place to pick up homestead applications.

For a sale, ask the staff to print the current balance and keep it with your listing file. That one page answers most of what a title company will ask about taxes, and it shows a buyer that the account is clean.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where do I send a Person County informal appeal?

Email tax@personcountync.gov, mail it to PO Box 1116, Roxboro, NC 27573, or drop it at 13 Abbitt Street. Include your phone number and supporting records.

What value date did the latest reappraisal use?

January 1, 2025. Ask the office when the next one is scheduled.

What income ceiling applies to the elderly exclusion?

$38,800 for 2026, and owners must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled before January 1. Filing closes June 1.

How large is the disabled veteran exclusion?

It removes $45,000 from the value of the home and one acre for an honorably discharged veteran who is 100% disabled by a service injury.

What happens if I miss the January 5 deadline?

Interest starts January 6 at 2%, then three-quarters of 1% monthly. Continued nonpayment lets the county enforce its lien through court, so call early.

Who handles what at Pitt County Tax Administration

Tax Administration in Greenville lists, appraises and assesses property, and it also collects current and delinquent taxes. Appeals mail goes to PO Box 43, Greenville, NC 27835-0043, and the phone number is 252-902-3400.

Work is split by division. Real Property takes builder exemption forms, Business Personal Property covers farm equipment and similar items, and a Tax Relief Division receives applications for exclusions and deferrals. The county posts an email address for relief questions.

  • Appeals: the formal appeal form and the clerk to the county appeals board.
  • Relief: the Tax Relief Division, or the assessor by mail.
  • Billing and payment methods: Tax Administration.

Ask which jurisdictions tax a given parcel, since a house inside a town may carry more than one bill.

The Pitt County housing market

The county has 86,063 housing units and 74,533 households. Owners occupy 51.4% of homes, so renting is nearly as common as owning, and the middle owner home is worth $208,900. The estimated population is 182,936, up 6.5% from the 2020 base.

Ask the tax office how a change of ownership affects any relief or present-use file on a parcel before you list.

The next Pitt County revaluation

The current schedule of values took effect January 1, 2024 and runs until the next revaluation, set for 2028. Improvements made in between are priced under the same statutory standards.

The schedule is a manual of rates, value ranges and guidelines that commissioners must adopt. It covers construction adjustments, market adjustments and land schedules. The Machinery Act defines market value as what a willing and able buyer and seller would agree on without pressure and with reasonable knowledge of the property's uses.

State law (G.S. 105-286) also calls for a review in the fourth year after a reappraisal, using percentage adjustments by category or area instead of appraising each parcel. Ask the assessor whether one is planned before 2028.

Appealing to the county board

Submit a formal appeal form to the county board. Appeals can be filed from January 1 until the board formally adjourns, usually in April or May.

The board is made up of residents chosen by the commissioners and serves as the first step of review. It hears from the owner and from the assessor's office. There are three grounds: a value above market, unequal treatment against similar properties, and factual errors in the record.

Hearings are held at the Eugene James Auditorium, second floor, Pitt County Administration Building, 1717 W. 5th St., Greenville. The request deadline and hearing dates shift each year, so read the current notice, and note that anything filed after adjournment is untimely.

Bring comparable sales, an appraisal if you have one, and photos of the house. You may speak yourself or send a representative.

If you dislike the ruling, you can go to the statewide Property Tax Commission with a written notice filed a month after the ruling is mailed, copied to the assessor (G.S. 105-290).

Homestead and other relief programs

Relief covers seniors, disabled owners, military service, farmland, builders, nonprofits and vehicle owners. The homestead programs require that you own the home and live in it.

Pitt County homestead relief for 2027, based on 2026 income
ProgramBenefitIncome limit
Age-or-disability exclusionSubtracts $25,000 or 50% of the home's value, whichever is larger, from the house and up to one acre$39,900
Circuit breakerTax limited to 4% of income at or under $39,900 and 5% from $39,901 to $59,850; the remainder is deferred as a lien$59,850
Disabled veteran exclusion$45,000 off the value for a 100% permanent service-connected disability, or an unmarried surviving spouseNone

File Form AV-9 with the assessor from January 1 through June 1. Late requests from June 2 through December 31 can be considered when you document a reason, and they go to the appeals board. Nothing filed after December 31 can be taken for that year. The circuit breaker is renewed every year, and every owner on the deed has to qualify. Deferred tax, up to three years plus interest, is payable on a sale or a death.

Land in the present-use program carries its own rules: 10 acres for agriculture, 5 for horticulture and 20 for forestry under a written plan. Removal brings rollback of the current and prior three years.

Other exemptions that can touch a sale

Several exemptions matter when the property is not an ordinary house. Each has its own form and timing.

  • Builder inventory: a residential builder's gains from subdividing, grading or building a new single-family home or duplex are excluded for up to three years after first listing, and a commercial builder's for up to five, ending sooner at a building permit or a sale. The form is AV-65.
  • Nonprofit and special-use property: the AV-10 application goes to the Tax Relief Division during January of the year you apply.
  • Antique automobiles: a vehicle that meets the county's conditions is valued at $500, with the application due a month after the tax due date.
  • Antique airplanes: assessed at the lower of true value or $5,000.

A sale ends the builder exclusion, so confirm with the Real Property Division how the end date is handled on a particular parcel, and whether the new owner must file a fresh application.

What you owe at a Pitt County closing

Real property tax is due September 1, interest-free through January 5, with interest starting after that (G.S. 105-360). A same-day postmark now requires a visit to a Postal Service retail counter, so do not count on a late drop in the mail.

The year's lien follows the land (G.S. 105-355). Your closing attorney requests a payoff and takes it from your proceeds.

  • Get a payoff for each parcel and taxing jurisdiction.
  • Check present-use or circuit breaker deferrals, which can come due.
  • Confirm any late relief application was decided.

A cash buyer can close quickly, so request the payoff early. Keep the paid receipts in your closing file in case a question comes up later.

Steps before you list a Pitt County house

A few calls early on keep the tax side of a sale simple. Work through them in this order and keep the answers for your closing attorney.

  1. Ask Tax Administration, 252-902-3400, which jurisdictions bill the parcel, since a house inside a town may carry more than one bill.
  2. Request a current balance and a payoff for each bill.
  3. Ask the Tax Relief Division whether an exclusion or circuit breaker deferral is attached to the property, because a deferral comes due on a sale.
  4. If the land is in the present-use program, ask what rollback would apply once the sale takes it out.
  5. If you plan to contest the value, check the current appeals notice for the filing deadline before you list.

With those answers in hand, a buyer's attorney has little to chase, and the payoff at the table matches what you expected. A cash buyer does not need loan approval, but the same tax payoff is still deducted from your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

When will Pitt County revalue next?

The current schedule of values holds until the next revaluation in 2028. Confirm the date with Tax Administration.

How do I challenge an assessment?

File the formal appeal form with the county appeals board any time from January 1 until it adjourns, typically April or May. The clerk's number is 252-902-3400.

What is the senior exclusion income cap?

$39,900 for 2027, based on 2026 income, for residents who are 65 or over, or totally and permanently disabled, and live in the home.

Is a filing after June 1 hopeless?

Not always. Requests from June 2 to December 31 may be reviewed by the appeals board when you give a documented reason, but nothing after December 31 counts for that year.

What happens to deferred tax if I sell?

Circuit breaker deferrals for up to three years plus interest become payable on a sale, and present-use land owes rollback taxes if it leaves the program.

How the layers stack up for an Asheboro address

An address in Archdale, Franklinville or Seagrove draws on a different city figure, and a house outside every town skips the city layer entirely. That spread is why two Randolph County houses with the same assessed value can get different bills. When you list, tell a buyer which district you sit in, since the combined rate shapes the monthly payment on the buyer's loan.

Randolph County revaluation schedule

Randolph revalues every four years, shorter than the state's eight-year minimum. The last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2027.

A proposed 2027 schedule of values and a proposed present-use schedule are posted, so treat them as drafts until commissioners act. The county aims for full market value on every parcel. A revaluation year is when many sellers see the biggest swing in assessed value, so read the notice when it arrives.

How the county values a house

Appraisers study sales in the county, record each property's size, construction, heating and cooling, plumbing, age and condition, and weigh the income a property could earn. Values do not move evenly. Depending on recent sales in a market area, an assessment may rise, fall or stay about the same.

A reappraisal sets only one half of the bill, the assessed value. Elected officials set the rate.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Randolph County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What the 2027 reappraisal means for a seller

It resets the assessed value that a buyer's first full bill is built on. Market value means the price both sides would accept without pressure. If your house is priced below what the county's appraisers see in nearby sales, expect a higher notice. If you have made repairs or additions, report them so the record matches.

  • Check your parcel in the county's real property search.
  • Read the reappraisal value notice as soon as it comes.
  • Use the informal appeal form mailed with the notice before moving to a board hearing.

Valid reasons to appeal in Randolph County

Randolph accepts two: an assessment far above market value, or one out of line with similar properties nearby. A value that simply feels too high, high taxes, or an owner who cannot afford the bill are not valid reasons.

The path runs through an informal appeal, mailed with each reappraisal notice, then Randolph's review board, the state commission that hears property tax cases and the appellate court. A commission appeal is due 30 days after the board mails its ruling (G.S. 105-290). Ask the tax department for the board's meeting dates.

Who is billed when a Randolph County house sells?

Whoever owned it on January 1. The bill is always generated for that owner. Randolph uses a permanent listing system, so land is listed automatically as soon as the register of deeds records a deed. Building changes still must be reported in the listing period.

You can pay the face amount through January 5. Interest of 2 percent starts January 6, with 0.75 percent per month from February 1 (the collection statute). Who shares which part of that year's bill is a closing negotiation.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Relief and collection rules for sellers

Randolph posts a relief page and an application form. The state programs are the senior and disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker deferment, and an owner can use only one. They sit in G.S. 105-277.1, G.S. 105-277.1C and G.S. 105-277.1B.

The circuit breaker defers the excess tax as a lien, and deferred tax for the three prior years comes due on a sale. If a bill stays unpaid, the county can foreclose through an action filed where the land lies, with a public auction at the courthouse door under G.S. 105-374. Selling first, even to a cash buyer, avoids that path.

Reporting building changes

The state listing period opens the first business day of January and closes January 31 (G.S. 105-307). Extensions are available for good cause but not past April 15. Land is listed on its own in Randolph, so the window matters for added rooms, removed structures and business equipment.

Checklist before listing a Randolph County house

A few quick checks keep the tax side from slowing the sale. Pull up your parcel in the real property search and confirm the record matches the house. Look up the tax bill online and write down any balance. Ask the tax department which city, school and fire rates apply. Find out whether a relief or deferral is attached. Then give all of it to your closing attorney.

If the house is inherited, vacant or needs work, a cash sale can close faster, but the tax payoff is still taken from your proceeds at the table.

Frequently asked questions

What is Randolph County's reappraisal schedule?

A four-year cycle. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023, and the next is scheduled for 2027.

What county rate does Randolph County list for 2026-2027?

0.50, with city, school and fire rates listed apart from it. Call the tax department to confirm your total.

Is high tax a valid reason to appeal a Randolph County value?

No. High taxes and an owner's inability to pay are not valid reasons. An appeal has to show the value exceeds market or is inconsistent with similar properties.

What is the Asheboro city rate?

0.71, plus a school rate of 0.1153. Other towns carry different rates, so match the figure to your parcel.

Who receives the tax bill after a Randolph County sale?

The bill goes to the January 1 owner. How the buyer shares the cost is a closing matter.
