Who values and bills property

A single department handles valuing and billing. The Robeson County Tax Administrator holds both the assessor and collector roles. That covers listing and valuing real property, personal property and motor vehicles, collecting the tax, keeping land records and maps, and running reappraisals.

The office has three divisions. Assessment handles real property, reappraisal, personal property, individual and business listings, and motor vehicles. Collections has a customer service section and a delinquent collections section. Land Records and GIS keeps the maps and addresses.

The Lumberton office answers at 910-671-3060. The county's online tools let you look up real and personal property bills and search public land records. Before you search, gather the parcel number, the owner's name or a copy of the bill. Any one of them will pull up the record, and the parcel number is the fastest. A phone payment line (1-866-249-0705) also takes payments, and it carries a convenience fee.

When did Robeson County last reappraise?

The latest reappraisal took effect January 1, 2024. State law requires one at least every eight years, and the county commissioners have considered a four-year cycle so that fast-rising and slow-rising neighborhoods stay closer to market.

About 560 appraisal neighborhoods organize the work. Appraisers weigh cost, sales and income figures to produce a schedule of values, which the Board of Commissioners then adopts. Family sales, gifts, trades and deals between related companies are set aside as non-market transfers. A seller under pressure may also accept less than market value, so one sale price does not set an assessment.

Between reappraisals, your value moves only if something changes: new construction, demolition, remodeling, rezoning or a fix for a county error. Real property is listed permanently. You do not file a yearly listing unless you built, tore down a structure, or lost a program benefit.

Due dates and penalties

Robeson mails real and personal property bills each August. They are due September 1, but interest does not start until after January 5. On January 6 a 2 percent charge applies, and the county adds three-fourths of a percent on the first of each month after that.

Robeson County real and personal property billing sequence
StepTiming
Bills mailedAugust
DueSeptember 1
Last day without interestJanuary 5
First interest charge2 percent, January 6
Added monthlyThree-fourths of 1 percent
Newspaper advertisingMarch, with a fee added to the bill

State law (G.S. 105-360) uses the same due date and interest steps. Once a bill is delinquent, collection can start with wage garnishment, bank attachment, foreclosure, income tax refund set-off or levies on rents.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Robeson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Listing boats, mobile homes and business equipment

Personal property must be listed every year by January 31. Miss it and a 10 percent penalty is added. A written request postmarked by January 31 can win an extension to April 15.

  • Individual property: boats, motors, jet skis, mobile homes, aircraft and unlicensed vehicles such as trailers, campers and motorcycles.
  • Business property: machinery, equipment, computers, furniture, fixtures, supplies, farm machinery and race cars.
  • Anyone who owned these items on January 1 must list them.

If you listed last year, a form comes in the mail. If it doesn't, getting one is your job. Call 910-671-3060 and ask for extension 7320 or 7321 for individuals, or 7319 for business property.

Car and truck tax bills

Vehicle taxes ride along with the tag. Bills are mailed monthly, and each one is due at the start of the fourth month following a renewal or new tag. You then get 30 days of grace before 2 percent interest and the monthly three-fourths of a percent kick in.

An unpaid bill puts a state registration block on the vehicle, and the tag can't be renewed until you pay and the collector gives you a MAV-2 form. If you sell a vehicle and surrender the tag to the state, bring the bill of sale and the DMV receipt to the collector, because a refund or prorated bill may be due. A vehicle moved out of North Carolina needs the new state's registration card and the DMV surrender receipt. Keep these papers with your tax records until the collector confirms the account is closed.

How to appeal your assessment

Your appeal must be postmarked before the Board adjourns. That is usually late April, and the date is advertised ahead of the first meeting. Request the form in writing from the Tax Administrator at the Administration Center in Lumberton.

State law (G.S. 105-322) sets the board's first sitting between early April and early May. If you're still unhappy afterward, the next level is the state Property Tax Commission, and G.S. 105-290 allows 30 days from the mailed decision to give written notice.

Back your case with papers such as a purchase price or damage records. A recent closing statement, repair estimates or photos of problems the appraiser may not have seen all help. Check the date on your own notice, since the board's calendar is set and advertised each year. Keep a copy of everything you mail, and use a postmark you can prove.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Robeson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax relief programs

The state offers three ways to cut a homeowner's bill, and you get to use just one of them. File Form AV-9 with the county assessor. January is the best month, though the office takes applications until June 1.

  • Elderly or disabled: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of a home's appraised value comes off. It applies to owners aged 65 or over, or with a permanent and total disability, under an income cap listed as $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of value is excluded, and neither age nor income matters. The county contact at 910-671-3071 helps with the NCDVA-9 certification.
  • Circuit breaker: the bill is limited to 4 percent of income at or below the cap and 5 percent between the cap and 150 percent of it ($58,200 for 2026). Anything above is deferred. You reapply yearly, and five years of ownership and residence come first.

Farm and forest land taxed at present use value is really a deferment. Take the land out of the program and the tax saved comes due, for the current year and three earlier ones, with interest. Property designated historic by local ordinance is taxed at half its appraised value.

Selling with taxes owed or due

The owner of record on January 1 is responsible for that year's tax. A June sale doesn't shift the bill off the seller. The buyer and seller normally divide the bill by agreement, but the invoice still goes to the seller.

Paying the collector directly at closing removes doubt. If the current bill isn't due yet, the office accepts a prepayment using the previous year's rate. Unpaid taxes on a house sold during the year can lead to both names being advertised.

The same office certifies your deed before recording, so one call can cover the balance and the certification. Ask for a written payoff figure, and keep it with your closing papers so the buyer's attorney can check it. For the current tax rate, call the office.

Frequently asked questions

When does a Robeson County tax bill come due?

September 1 is the due date. You can pay through January 5 without interest, and 2 percent is added starting January 6.

When was the last Robeson County reappraisal?

It took effect January 1, 2024. The state minimum is every eight years, and commissioners have talked about a shorter four-year cycle.

Who owes the bill when a Robeson house sells in midyear?

Whoever owned it on January 1. The seller gets that year's bill, and closing papers usually prorate the cost.

How do older or disabled owners claim a Robeson County exclusion?

Submit Form AV-9 to the Tax Administration office, plus the NCDVA-9 certificate for a veteran claim. January is the target month, and June 1 is the last day accepted.

When must a Robeson County valuation appeal be filed?

Your appeal needs a postmark before the review board adjourns, usually in late April. Write to the Tax Administrator for the form.

Which office bills and assesses property?

Tax Administration handles both sides of your bill. Rockingham County combines the assessor and collector jobs under one Tax Administrator, with an assessment division and a collection division. The office is in the Rockingham County Governmental Center, 371 NC Hwy 65, Reidsville, and is open weekdays. Call 336-342-8305 or write to PO Box 68, Wentworth, NC 27375, which is also the payment address.

The assessment division lists, appraises and assesses real property, business personal property and individual personal property. It also processes ownership transfers and keeps the records current. The collection division bills and collects current and delinquent taxes for the county, the City of Eden, the City of Reidsville, the Town of Madison, the Town of Mayodan, the Town of Stoneville and 18 rural fire districts. A house inside a town can therefore carry several levies.

Rates are set separately by the Board of County Commissioners, each fire district and each city or town council. They are established in June, and bills are mailed in late July.

Due dates and how to pay

Bills are due September 1 each year. You can pay with no interest through January 5, and the state rule starts interest on January 6.

After January 5 the state adds a flat two percent. From February 1 on it adds three-fourths of a percent for every month or part of a month. A prepayment discount exists only if the county or a town adopted one, so ask the collector about your current bill. A mailed payment counts on its postmark date.

Rockingham County accepts these payment methods:

  • A card payment online through the county's payment-service link, or an e-check through a second link
  • A call to 1-866-251-3264, with the bill in hand
  • A check mailed to Rockingham County Tax Collector, PO Box 68, Wentworth, NC 27375-0068
  • Counter service at the Governmental Center, which you should confirm with the office first

Since the budget sets the new rate in June and bills follow in late July, a spring listing still reflects last year's rate. Tell buyers to expect the figure to change.

The four levels of appeal

You begin with an appraiser and, if needed, finish at the state Court of Appeals.

The informal step means calling the Real Property Division so an appraiser can recheck your record. It is open from January 1 until the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. The Board is chosen by the county commissioners, is separate from the tax office staff, and starts hearing cases in April.

Rockingham County property value review levels
LevelWho decidesWhat to expect
1Real Property DivisionAppraiser review, January 1 through Board adjournment
2Board of Equalization and ReviewAppointed by the commissioners, hearings from April
3NC Property Tax CommissionFive members in Raleigh, hearings by application and appointment
4NC Court of AppealsLast resort for a dissatisfied owner

State statute requires the written request to arrive before the Board adjourns. An appeal to the Commission must follow within 30 days of the mailed decision. Between reappraisals, changes in value are limited by G.S. 105-287.

The 2024 reappraisal and what it means for you

Rockingham reappraised early because state sales ratio studies forced it. A ratio below 85% or above 115% requires a reappraisal within three years, and the county's ratios had fallen to 91.25% for 2020 sales, 77.86% for 2021 sales and 69.55% for 2022 sales. Tax values were far under market prices after the strong market that began in 2020.

Tax Administration worked with Piner Appraisal on the new values. The appraisers compared property cards with what they saw on site, tracked sales since the last reappraisal and studied rents and building costs. To value land, they grouped the county into about 500 zones called neighborhoods and set a land rate for each from local sales.

  • The new values took effect for 2024 tax bills and stay fixed until the next reappraisal, apart from changes the statutes allow.
  • Appeals for that cycle were heard in the spring of 2024, so a new appeal now needs a new notice of value.
  • A property card is available at the Tax Administration office in Wentworth or on the county website.

Here is a quick fairness test. When the assessed figure sits near the price you'd reasonably ask for the house, the appraisal is about right. Ask the office when the next reappraisal is scheduled.

Homestead and other tax breaks

Three state programs exist, and each owner may use just one. The county's Tax Forms page carries the 2026 Application for Property Tax Relief, the disability certification for the homestead exclusion and the certification for the disabled veteran exclusion. The same page lists a Present Use Value deferment application, a builder's exclusion and a Tax Certification Request form.

The homestead exclusion protects the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value for older or disabled owners who stay under the $38,800 income limit printed on the 2026 state form. The disabled veteran exclusion takes off the first $45,000 regardless of age or income. The circuit breaker caps the bill at a share of income and defers the rest as a lien.

A deferral stays on the property. It comes due for the preceding three years if the owner sells, dies or stops living in the house, so a seller on that program should get a payoff early. For exemption questions, call the Tax Office at 336-342-8250.

Selling with taxes owed

Expect to cover your share of the current year's bill plus any earlier balance. The lien for a year's tax attaches to the parcel as of the January listing date, and interest and costs ride along with it. An overdue amount has to be cleared before a buyer gets clean title.

If a bill stays unpaid, the county can sue much as a lender would, and a courthouse auction may follow. Redeeming before the court confirms the sale means paying the tax plus penalties, interest and costs.

Before listing, ask the collection division for a payoff on every parcel number, fire district charges included. Your closing attorney then prorates the current year. When a house with back taxes sells fast, expect the title company to pay the balance from your proceeds at settlement.

A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender's appraisal, but the tax lien still has to be paid or cleared at the table.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Rockingham County property taxes?

You pay the Rockingham County Tax Collector, online, by phone at 1-866-251-3264, or by mail to PO Box 68 in Wentworth. Keep your bill handy, since the phone option requires it.

Is the Tax Assessor a different office from the Tax Collector in Rockingham County?

No. Rockingham County combines the assessor and collector roles under one Tax Administrator, with an assessment division and a collection division inside the same office.

Can I appeal my value by phone?

Yes for the informal step. Call the Real Property Division and an appraiser will review the record and value. The formal step before the Board of Equalization and Review must be requested in writing on the county form.

What if I sell my Rockingham County house with unpaid taxes?

The lien follows the parcel, so the balance must be paid for title to pass cleanly. Your closing attorney normally pays it from your sale proceeds, so request a payoff amount from the collection division before closing.

Which towns send a tax bill collected by the county?

Besides the county bill, the collection division collects for the City of Eden, the City of Reidsville, the Town of Madison, the Town of Mayodan, the Town of Stoneville and 18 rural fire districts, so one parcel can carry several levies.

Selling in Rowan County?

Who assesses and bills property in Rowan County

Rowan County Tax Administration has two divisions, the Assessor's office and the Tax Collector's office. The Assessor lists, assesses and bills all taxable property in the county, and the collector takes payment. Real property appraisers answer at 704-216-8586, and listing questions go to 704-216-8558.

An electronic online listing process is being built and should be ready for the 2027 listing season. Until then, call the office to ask how to list personal property such as a boat, a camper or a mobile home each January.

The Tax Assessor pages link to a land records map tool. A parcel may also carry a municipal or district bill on top of the county bill, so check the tax record for every levy before you list.

Revaluation schedule

Rowan revalues every four years. The last revaluation took effect January 1, 2023, the next is January 1, 2027, and another is set for January 2031.

State law sets only an outer limit of eight years. The shorter cycle softens sticker shock, and a revaluation never sets a rate, because the commissioners set rates in the yearly budget. Values come from actual sales.

Rowan County revaluation timeline
EventDate or result
Last revaluationJanuary 1, 2023
Average real property increase at that revaluation44.96% since the period that ended December 31, 2018
Next revaluationEffective January 1, 2027
Following revaluationScheduled for January 2031

If you sell near a revaluation date, expect buyers to study the new assessed value, because it drives the bill they will inherit. Value follows the condition of a parcel on January 1, so tell the assessor about any building added, moved or torn down.

What the 2023 revaluation did

Real property values rose by an average of 44.96% from the prior period. Almost 12,000 residential and 700 business property sales from January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2022 went into that work.

The county's total taxable base moved from about $14.4 billion to a projected $18.5 billion, with real property revalued to about $15.5 billion. Vehicles, personal property and utilities fell, so the total base rose 28.5% against a 44.96% jump for real estate alone. County law also required a revenue-neutral rate to be reported to the commissioners, who could lower the rate to ease the increase.

A revaluation can reset a buyer's bill sharply even when the rate drops. Check the current assessed value on the county's parcel tools before you set a price, and remember the next reset in 2027.

The COMPER comparison tool

COMPER is an online tool that shows the valid sales the tax office uses to help set values for the 2027 cycle. Enter a property address and you get a list and a map of valid sales within a five-mile radius, covering January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2026.

From that list you can pick sales similar to your home and turn them into a printable or PDF report. The map includes a street view of each comparable property. A seller can use the report to test a listing price against what the assessor treats as valid sales, though it can't replace an agent's or appraiser's opinion.

How to dispute an assessment

Call the tax office first, then use the written form if the call doesn't settle it. Informal talks usually happen from January through March. Fill in the Real Property Appeal Form and attach supporting papers. A review can leave the number alone, cut it or raise it.

The formal stage works like this:

  • Real property appeals must arrive before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns for the year.
  • That Board meets for the first time sometime between early April and early May. The county publishes notice in a local paper three times, beginning at least 10 days ahead.
  • Each side gets time to speak. The Board may rule at once or deliberate, and you should receive the ruling in writing.
  • Beyond that sits the Property Tax Commission, which meets monthly in Raleigh and behaves like a trial court. The owner carries the burden of proof, and companies and LLCs need a North Carolina attorney.

Personal property follows a shorter clock of 30 days from the first notice of value. When no separate notice goes out, the bill itself is the notice. After the Board adjourns it may still take up discovered property, classified vehicles, audits and personal property cases.

When taxes are due

September 1 is the due date under state law, and no interest accrues until January 6. After that, two percent applies through the end of January, then three-fourths of a percent for each additional month or part of one.

Counties may adopt a prepayment discount by resolution before May 1. Confirm any discount, card fee or payment channel with the Rowan County Tax Collector, since those details are set locally.

Personal property listing takes place in January, and the commissioners may extend it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Rowan County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Relief programs

Three state programs exist, and each applicant is limited to one. Applications for the elderly or disabled, disabled veteran and circuit breaker programs are due by June 1 of the year of application. Other exemptions are filed in January.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of the first $25,000 or half of appraised value, for owners aged 65 or up or fully and permanently disabled, with 2026 household income no higher than $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: up to the first $45,000. An unremarried surviving spouse can qualify, and age and income play no role.
  • Circuit breaker: an owner of five years or more with income up to $58,200 may defer tax above 4% of income at or under $38,800, or above 5% in the higher band.

Under the circuit breaker, multiple owners must all qualify, and you reapply each year. The deferred tax is a lien. The most recent three years come due with interest if the owner transfers, dies or stops using the home as a residence. Present-use value applications are filed each January, or after a value change notice.

Selling with unpaid taxes

The sale proceeds cover them. Each year's lien sticks to the parcel from the January listing date, along with interest and costs. A lien for personal property tax can reach all of the owner's real estate inside the taxing unit.

Left unpaid, a bill can lead to a suit and an auction of the parcel. Until the court confirms that sale, the owner can still redeem by clearing the tax and its extras.

Ask the Rowan County Tax Collector for a written payoff on each parcel and hand it to your closing attorney. Do this first if you plan a quick sale, since back taxes shape both price and timing.

Frequently asked questions

When is Rowan County's next revaluation?

The next revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, and the following one is scheduled for January 2031 on a four-year cycle.

What is the first move if my Rowan County value looks wrong?

Call the tax office, since informal reviews usually run January through March. If that fails, send the Real Property Appeal Form with your evidence before the county board adjourns.

Thirty days from the first notice of value. Without a separate notice, the tax bill serves as that notice.

What is COMPER?

COMPER is the county's online comparison tool. Enter an address to see valid sales from January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2026 within five miles, and build a report from similar homes.

Real property appraisers are at 704-216-8586, and listing questions go to 704-216-8558. The Tax Assessor page also has an email contact.

Sampson County, NC Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Sampson County, NC Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Sampson County, NC Property Tax Guide sale

Selling in Sampson County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Sampson County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Sampson County?
We buy Sampson County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Who bills the tax

The Sampson County Tax Office gathers county, fire district and school district levies, and for now it also collects for Clinton, Autryville, Harrells, Newton Grove, Salemburg, Turkey and Garland. One bill can therefore stack several levies.

Bills for land, buildings and personal property go out by mail in July or August. The state DMV sends the registered vehicle bills. Phone the office at (910) 592-8146 or write to PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329.

Two online tools help: a property record search and a site to search, view and pay bills. Sellers can confirm the parcel, owner and balance there before listing. Print the bill history for your files, since a buyer's agent will usually ask whether the current year is paid. The county's GIS viewer searches by owner name, address or parcel ID and helps you match the tax record to the right lot. That matters when a single address can sit in a town, a fire district and a school district at once.

Payment dates and late charges

Payment is due September 1. A 2 percent discount applies to land and personal property paid or postmarked by August 31, and a weekend deadline shifts to the following business day.

  • A bill turns delinquent after January 5, and nothing accrues before then.
  • After that, January adds 2 percent, and each later month adds three-quarters of 1 percent.
  • The office takes partial payments until the delinquency date.
  • A postmark counts as the receipt date for mailed checks.

Parcels still unpaid are advertised in a local newspaper under the owner's name, typically early in April, and the ad cost joins the lien. Collection tools include wage garnishment, bank attachment, seizure and sale, debt setoff and foreclosure.

Tax rates by area

The county's Tax Rates and Fees page lists these figures under a 2026 heading. Budget years change them, so check with the tax office before relying on any one.

Sampson County rates per $100 of value
Area or districtRate
County-wide0.685
Clinton school district0.115
Clinton city0.34
Clinton special downtown0.18
Garland0.48
Newton Grove0.40
Autryville0.47

The page also lists some extras. Clinton shows a $25.00 sticker fee, Garland $10.00, Roseboro $9.00, and Newton Grove and Salemburg $5.00 each. Harrells charges $111.00 for trash collection for one and $50.00 for each additional. Fire district rates appear for Plainview, Halls, Coharie, Goshen and Taylors Bridge, and town rates for Harrells, Turkey, Roseboro and Salemburg. Franklin, Turkey and Autryville fire charges apply inside the limits of Harrells, Turkey and Autryville respectively.

Your total depends on which district and town the parcel sits in. Ask the tax office to confirm which ones apply to your address before you quote a figure to a buyer. A bill adds the county-wide rate to the school, fire and municipal figures that apply to it.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Sampson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Value date for houses

Assessed values track market conditions on January 1, 2024, and hold until the next countywide revaluation. The county names 2028 for that, on an eight-year cycle that state law sets (section 105-286).

Market changes after the valuation date cannot lawfully enter an appeal. A sale price well above or below the assessment since 2024 does not by itself move the figure. Facts that existed on the valuation date, such as wrong square footage or a building listed that is gone, make firmer grounds.

How to appeal your assessment

Real estate appeals open each January 1 and close when the review board adjourns, typically in early May. An owner told of a changed value only after adjournment has until December 31.

  • Informal review: open to owners whose value moved since the last bill and who are seeing the new figure for the first time. Call (910) 592-8146 or write to Sampson County Tax Department, Attention: Real Estate Appeal, PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329.
  • Formal appeal: phone for a board application. The county commissioners sit as that board, and your application must arrive before adjournment.
  • Next level: the state Property Tax Commission, which needs an application within 30 days of the board mailing its decision.

After you ask for the informal step, an appraiser reviews the parcel again, and you may accept the recommendation or press on to the board. Keep photos or a contractor estimate showing the condition on January 1, 2024 with your request. Write down the date and time of every call, and the name of the person you spoke with, in case you need to follow up.

Personal property appeals run on a 30 day clock from the notice of value. Vehicle appeals need a postmark within 30 days of the notice's printed due date. Vehicles are valued at retail, so supply dealer paperwork and photos in place of web book values.

Relief programs

Three state programs exist, and each owner gets only one. Apply on Form AV-9 at the county assessor's office, not in Raleigh. June 1 is the acceptance deadline.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion (section 105-277.1): shields the larger of $25,000 or half of a permanent home's appraised value. The 2026 income ceiling is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion (section 105-277.1C): $45,000 of value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker (section 105-277.1B): caps tax at a percentage of income, 4.0 percent for lower incomes and 5.0 percent for incomes up to 150 percent of the ceiling, and defers the rest.

Deferred circuit breaker tax for the three prior years comes due when the owner transfers the home, dies or stops living in it. A sale triggers it, so get the figure from the tax office before you close. The buyer's title agent will want that amount paid from your proceeds, which lowers what you take home.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Sampson County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Settling tax when you sell

Settle the tax through your closing attorney. The county lien attaches on the listing date (section 105-355), so the buyer's title agent will want the year's balance cleared or prorated. Request a payoff for each parcel in the sale from the Sampson County Tax Office.

If the parcel was advertised in April, the ad cost is part of the lien and is owed too. Should a foreclosure follow, the parcel is auctioned at the courthouse door, and a redeeming party pays tax, penalties, interest and costs before confirmation (section 105-374).

After closing, the deed is recorded and the seller owes deed excise tax under section 105-228.30. Buyer and seller can split the year's tax by contract, so write the proration terms down. If you sell before the bill arrives, agree on who pays it and how the figure will be confirmed afterward.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Sampson County payment deadline?

September 1 is the due date. Paying or postmarking by August 31 earns a 2 percent discount, and the account is delinquent after January 5, when 2 percent interest starts for January.

Where can a Sampson County owner contest a real estate value?

Begin with an informal review by phone at (910) 592-8146 if the value changed, or ask for a Board of Equalization and Review application. The cutoff is board adjournment, usually in early May.

When is the next Sampson County revaluation?

In 2028. Until then, assessed values reflect market value on January 1, 2024.

What is the mailing address for Sampson County tax appeals?

Appeals on real estate and personal property go to the Sampson County Tax Office, PO Box 1082, Clinton, NC 28329, marked with the appeal type. Vehicle appeals may also be emailed to the address on the county's appeal page.

Can a Sampson County homeowner combine a disabled veteran exclusion with another relief program?

No. State law lets an owner benefit from only one of the three programs. File Form AV-9 with the county assessor for the one that fits.

How a Stanly County homeowner is taxed

Stanly County Tax Administration values property, mails the bills and collects the money. The county has more than 42,000 parcels and ten municipalities. Population is 68,830, up 10.1% from 2020. Owners live in 74.5% of homes, the typical value is $242,400 and typical rent is $861, so the tax touches most households.

Sellers should watch four things: the January 1 valuation date, the late-summer bill, the tax certification needed to record a deed, and any relief that comes due on a sale.

  • Value is locked in on New Year's Day, and the bill follows whoever owned the parcel that day.
  • County and town rates apply to that value, with fire district and solid waste charges added on top.
  • No deed gets recorded until the county confirms nothing is owed.
Stanly County housing snapshot, 2020-2024 survey period
Housing measureStanly County
Residents, 2025 estimate68,830
Housing units, July 202529,780
Homes lived in by their owners74.5%
Typical home value$242,400
Typical monthly rent$861

New construction is one reason an assessed value can shift between revaluations. The county logged 336 building permits in 2025.

Tax office location and what each division does

The department works from the county courthouse, 201 South Second Street in Albemarle, with counter service weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 5. In spring 2008 the commissioners merged the former tax collector's and tax assessor's offices into this single department.

  • Real property staff value land and buildings at what the latest reappraisal says they would sell for.
  • Personal property staff list and audit boats, aircraft, untagged vehicles and business equipment, then prepare the yearly bills.
  • The collector gathers county, municipal, fire district and special district taxes.

Phone lines: collections on the first floor, Room 104, 704-986-3619; real and personal property on the second floor, 704-986-3626; mapping and land records at 1000 North First Street, Suite 20, 704-986-3637.

Bills, due dates and 2026 rates

Statements arrive in late July or early August. For 2026 the county rate and every town's rate held steady, one fire district (Aquadale) rose from 10 to 12 cents, and the yearly solid waste fee stayed at $99. Your bill depends on your town and fire district, so ask the tax office for the figures that apply to your address.

Tax is due each September 1, with a late charge on real estate after the first week of January: 2% in the first month, then a smaller monthly rate. Personal property runs on a January listing schedule. Listing opens January 2 and ends January 31, and a 10% penalty applies to late listings.

Individual personal property is not prorated, except registered motor vehicles, and the assessment reflects the property's condition at the start of the year.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Stanly County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your value

Start with an informal appeal at the administrator's office, then take the dispute to the county's review board if you still disagree. Schedule informal appeals for 2027 before May 1, 2027, after which the board may have to hear them formally.

An informal review is a meeting with a certified appraiser, and you need evidence such as recent sales or an appraisal; a plain claim of overvaluation is not accepted. Written appeals go to the Tax Assessor at 201 South Second Street with your notice attached and a phone number where staff can reach you in the daytime. The five-member board is appointed by the commissioners. After it rules, the state Property Tax Commission in Raleigh is next, then the courts.

Market swings after the last reappraisal date of January 1, 2025 cannot be weighed until the next reappraisal, which the county schedules for January 1, 2029. For personal property, the office must hear from you within 30 days of the bill date.

Relief programs and present-use value

The county runs three homestead programs plus a present-use program for working land. An owner who qualifies for several may choose only one, and filing runs January 2 through June 1.

  • Seniors and disabled owners: an exclusion removes up to half the value of a permanent residence, or $25,000 if that is more. The county prints a $39,900 income ceiling for 2027 applications, based on 2026 income, and a married applicant reports both spouses' income.
  • Disabled veteran: a fixed $45,000 of value comes off the bill. An unmarried surviving spouse can qualify, and the VA must complete a disability certification to go with the form.
  • Circuit breaker: limits the bill to 4% of income, or 5% in the band up to $59,850, deferring the remainder. Five full years of ownership and occupancy are required, and the current year plus three prior deferred years become a lien due with interest on transfer, death or a change of use.

Present-use value taxes farmland and forest by its use rather than its market price. Agriculture needs ten acres in commercial production, horticulture five acres, forestry twenty acres with a written management plan, and wildlife land between twenty and one hundred acres. Changing the use of such land can end the benefit, so ask the tax office about back tax before a sale.

What a seller must clear before recording

The first step is a Tax Certification Form. The seller or the closing office fills in the top portion, the assessor or mapping office completes the middle, and the Tax Collector certifies that nothing is delinquent and stamps the deed so the deed office will take it. Plan for this step on closing day.

North Carolina's deed excise tax falls on the seller and is paid at filing, and the filing fees are uniform across counties. The current year's property tax is usually shared by buyer and seller, and your attorney can calculate each side and pay from proceeds.

If the property carries back tax, a cash buyer can buy it in its present state and pay the balance at closing. The state ties the lien to the listing date, and a tax foreclosure action can follow if the bill stays unpaid.

Preparing for a Stanly County closing

Allow a day or two to collect the stamp, since three offices touch the form. Start at the Tax Collector in Room 104 for a balance, ask the assessor's floor for the middle section, and bring the completed form to your attorney or the deed office. If you have boats, aircraft or business equipment, remember they are listed separately each January and a house sale does not cancel a listing already due.

Before you list, ask the office which taxing districts bill your parcel, what the fire district and solid waste figures are, and whether any relief or present-use enrollment is attached. Those answers affect your payoff and a buyer's questions.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I go to pay or ask about a Stanly County bill?

The Stanly County Courthouse, 201 South Second Street, Albemarle, NC 28001, weekdays 8:30 am to 5 pm. Collections sits in Room 104 downstairs and answers at 704-986-3619.

When will Stanly County reappraise next?

The county schedules the next revaluation for January 1, 2029. The latest one is dated January 1, 2025, and state law caps the gap between reappraisals at eight years.

Will delinquent tax stop a deed from being recorded?

Yes. The Tax Collector must certify on the Tax Certification Form that nothing is owed and stamp the deed before it reaches the Register of Deeds. Clear the balance first.

How do I file for Stanly County's senior and disability exclusion?

Submit Form AV-9 to the tax office from January 2 to June 1, attaching proof of income. A disability claim needs a physician's certificate on Form AV-9A. The county prints $39,900 as the income limit for 2027 applications.

Do boats and untagged vehicles go away if I sell my house?

No. Personal property is listed each January and assessed as of January 1, and it is not prorated except for registered vehicles. A sale of the house does not cancel a listing already due.

Which Stokes County office runs property tax?

Tax Administration, in the county Administration Building at 1014 Main Street, Danbury. Mail goes to P.O. Box 57 and the office is open weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00.

Its web pages offer a search and payment portal, property record cards, land and home values, an online listing service and a form to request a listing extension. Owners who want paperless bills can sign up for e-statements using the registration ID printed on the statement.

Tax dates

Bills carry a January 5 deadline, and mail needs that postmark. Under state law the tax is payable September 1, and interest starts January 6.

Stokes County yearly tax calendar
WhenWhat happens
All of JanuaryProperty listing
Through April 15Extension for good cause, if asked in January
By January 5Payment without interest
From January 6Interest accrues

A bill for your year of sale stays on the parcel, so settle the split with your closing attorney.

What if a Stokes County owner skips listing?

The county adds a 10% penalty to the total tax levied. In a year without a general reappraisal, the commissioners may add up to 30 days to the listing period.

Most homeowners need to do nothing in a quiet year. Anyone who built or demolished a structure, bought a business asset or owns a boat or similar item should list, and the online listing service is the quickest route. The department's extension request form is also on its page.

North Carolina requires everyone to list taxable property each year (G.S. 105-287). Someone who bought a house in the past year typically has the real estate already on the books, so the main item to list is personal property such as a boat or business equipment. Individual extensions for good cause can run as late as April 15, but only if you ask during January.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Stokes County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How often Stokes County reappraises

Every four years, even though G.S. 105-286 allows up to eight. Between reappraisals the assessor may change a value only to fix a clerical or math error or a misapplied schedule, or to reflect real changes to the property.

Normal depreciation, countywide economic swings and minor upkeep such as repainting or landscaping do not justify a change in between. Check your notice for the effective date of the current reappraisal.

What can I do if my Stokes value looks wrong?

Phone Tax Administration first. If that fails, take it to the county board that reviews values. State law has it meet first no sooner than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May, and your request must reach it before adjournment.

  • Decisions are mailed within 30 days of adjourning.
  • You get 30 days from that mailing to notify the state commission.
  • Stokes sets dates yearly, so ask for this year's schedule.

Bring an appraisal, comparable sales or proof of an error in the county's data. In a year without a general reappraisal the board finishes by the third Monday after its first meeting unless more time is needed, and it cannot sit past July 1 except for certain requests. In a reappraisal year it has until December 1. Because Stokes reappraises every four years, one year in four gives owners a longer window.

Homestead relief

Owners 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, may exclude $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is higher. The county sets an income cap of $38,800. The state adds a disabled veteran exclusion of $45,000 and an income-linked deferment.

  • No age or income test applies to the veteran program.
  • The deferment requires five years living in the home.
  • One program at a time.

Application forms are on the county tax pages and go to the assessor.

Income starts with adjusted gross income under section 62 of the Internal Revenue Code, then adds every other dollar from every source except gifts or inheritances from a spouse, parent, grandparent or descendant. Married couples sharing a home combine incomes, even when only one name is on the deed. Age and disability are judged on January 1 before the tax year, and the applicant must live in North Carolina. A disabled applicant needs a certificate from a physician or an agency, and a couple gets the full exclusion if one spouse qualifies.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Stokes County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What if a Stokes bill stays unpaid?

A lien attached on the listing date, and the county may sue as in a mortgage foreclosure. Property sells at a courthouse auction to the top bidder, with up to 20% down.

Challenges or raised offers must come within 10 days of the report. Until the court confirms, you may redeem by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Call early, since an open balance also blocks the deed certification.

After a tax sale

Within 10 days after the commissioner's report, anyone may file a higher bid, at least 5% above the last with a minimum raise of $750, and a deposit of at least 5% (never under $750). Each new bid restarts the clock, and rights lock when no bid arrives in time.

The commissioner's fee can reach 5% of the price, and money left after taxes goes to the court for those entitled. Selling before this stage almost always leaves more behind.

How personal property is valued

Owners report original cost by year of purchase. The county trends it up to current replacement cost and then applies straight line depreciation using state schedules. Manufacturer, retailer, wholesaler and contractor inventories are exempt, as is non-business personal property. The same appeal path of county board, then state commission, applies.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Offices a taxpayer will need in Danbury

They cluster at the Administration Building, 1014 Main Street.

  • Tax Administration, P.O. Box 57, weekdays 8:30 to 5:00.
  • Register of Deeds, (336) 593-2414, recording until 4:45 on weekdays.
  • Planning and Inspections, (336) 593-2444.
  • Finance, (336) 914-9188.

The deed certification rule means the first two will often be visited on the same day.

Selling with taxes owed

An open balance does not block a sale, but it does block the deed. Tax Administration must certify that no delinquent tax is owed before the Register of Deeds will record, and that office is in the same building. Ask for a current figure, then have the closing attorney pay it from your proceeds at the table.

The current year is different. A house that sells in autumn, after bills go out, usually has an open current-year balance, and buyer and seller divide it at closing. A cash buyer can take the house with back tax attached and settle it from the price, which is often the fastest way out of a lien. Waiting for a tax sale almost always leaves you with less.

What a buyer or seller should look up first

The tax website carries property record cards and land and home values, and the county GIS site shows parcel lines. Together they reveal acreage, building details and the value the county uses. Compare those with the listing, since an error in square footage is easy to correct at the assessor's office.

Ask Tax Administration which taxing districts bill the parcel, and request the current balance before you set a closing date.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Stokes payment deadline?

January 5, with a postmark of that date for mail. Interest begins January 6.

What is the Stokes County listing window?

January 1 through January 31, with individual extensions up to April 15 for good cause.

Is there a late listing penalty in Stokes County?

Yes, 10% of the total tax levied.

How often does Stokes County reappraise real estate?

On a four year cycle, although state law would allow up to eight years.

Where do I pay a Stokes bill in person?

At Tax Administration, 1014 Main Street, Danbury, open weekdays 8:30 to 5:00. An online portal is also on the county site.

How Surry County appraises about 44,000 parcels

Appraisers sort the parcels into roughly 370 neighborhoods of similar homes, price land and buildings from sales, check the results in the field and office, then mail notices of value. The commissioners must approve the Schedule of Values, the manual of rates and adjustments, before it applies.

The county defines value as the most probable price in a competitive, open market. Periodic revaluation keeps some owners from paying more than their share while others pay less, which is the county's stated reason for reappraising.

The latest revaluation

The current revaluation took effect January 1, 2025. In 2017 the commissioners moved the county from the eight-year state maximum to a five-year cycle, producing an effective date of January 1, 2021, and the county now calls itself a four-year county.

Values hold until the next revaluation except for changes to a property. Call the tax office to learn when the next one takes effect.

Where do I take a Surry County value dispute?

Ask the Tax Department for an informal review, or file with the county's special review board. The board has existed since 1982, the commissioners reappoint it each January, and it sits by the first Monday in May.

  • The board can change any value it finds out of line.
  • Each timely appellant may appear.
  • A losing appellant can go on to the state Property Tax Commission.

Bring documents showing why the value differs from market value, or facts about the property that affect it. The Real Estate page of the tax website has a link to submit an informal appeal for real property online, along with the 2025 appraisal manual, the use value manual and the revaluation FAQ.

When Surry County tax goes delinquent

Interest is added to payments made on or after January 6 following the due date: 2% the first month, then 0.75% for each month. The county treats the tax and interest charges as non-negotiable.

Its collection tools are garnishment, bank attachment, seizure of personal property and foreclosure under G.S. 105-365 to 105-368, and remedies on real property must begin within 10 years of the due date. A delinquent real property list is posted on its collections page.

Circuit breaker and homestead relief

The circuit breaker caps tax at 4.0% of income up to the eligibility limit and 5.0% above it, up to 150% of the limit. The revenue department's 2026 figures are $38,800 and $58,200, and an application is needed every year.

The owner must be 65 or disabled and must have lived in and owned the home for five years. Deferred tax becomes a lien, and three prior years come due when the owner sells, dies or moves out. The other two homestead programs, the elderly or disabled exclusion and the $45,000 disabled veteran exclusion, are filed on AV-9 with the county assessor, and an owner may use only one.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Surry County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Ask Collections for a payoff before accepting an offer, because the lien on the parcel dates to the listing date and rides along until paid.

If the bill is behind, the county can bring an auction action, with commissioner fees up to 5% of the price. Redemption before confirmation requires all taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Paying at closing is the usual fix, and a cash buyer can take the house with the balance attached and clear it from the price.

How Surry County runs tax foreclosure sales

The county directs private attorneys to start formal foreclosure proceedings under G.S. 105-374 against real property with unpaid tax. Properties listed for sale are being foreclosed under a court judgment, and the sales are not the county selling its own surplus land.

  • Property is sold as is, where is, with no warranties from the county.
  • A 20% deposit is due at the time of sale.
  • The upset bid period is 10 calendar days from the sale.
  • Redemption is possible at any time before confirmation, and redeemed parcels are pulled from the process.

Call (336) 401-8100 for the status of a parcel, and check the court file, since the posted list can lag behind real events.

Present use value for farm or woodland

Land enrolled in a use value program is taxed on what it produces rather than what it would sell for, and the county publishes a use value manual for farm, horticultural and forest land. The Tax Department handles enrollment at its Dobson office.

If you are selling enrolled land, ask the department what happens to the enrollment when ownership changes and whether any deferred tax is due. A buyer who plans to build or subdivide will want that answer before the contract is signed.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Other tax office services useful to a seller

Beyond real estate, the Tax Department handles business personal property, personal property, motor vehicles and present use value. Owners can print a motor vehicle tax receipt through the state's MyDMV portal, request a mailing address change, and send public records requests online.

The department also runs GIS mapping and downloadable data. For a seller, the mapping and parcel data are handy for checking acreage and lines before a buyer's survey. For anything the website leaves open, call (336) 401-8100.

A seller's order of operations

Start with the tax office and work outward. Request a payoff figure from Collections, check whether any relief or use value enrollment is attached to the parcel, and ask the appraisal office whether your assessment looks right before you set a price. Then bring the payoff to your closing attorney, who can pay the current bill and any delinquency from your proceeds.

A cash buyer will usually accept the house with its balance and repairs, and the offer reflects both. If you list on the open market, expect the buyer's attorney to ask for the same payoff figure.

  • Call the Tax Department at the main number and ask Collections for the payoff figure in writing.
  • Check the delinquent real property list on the collections page to see whether your parcel appears.
  • If the assessment looks wrong, ask for an informal review or file with the special review board before you set a price.
  • If the land is enrolled in use value, ask whether deferred tax comes due on the sale.
  • Give the closing attorney the payoff so current and past bills are paid from your proceeds.

A cash sale skips the open-market wait, and the balance is simply taken out of the price at closing.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Surry County Tax Department?

915 East Atkins Street, Dobson, NC 27017, open weekdays 8:15 to 5:00.

When does interest start on Surry County property tax?

On payments made on or after January 6, at 2% for the first month and 0.75% each month after.

When did Surry County's current revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2025, following one effective January 1, 2021.

When does Surry County's value review board meet?

It convenes each year by the first Monday in May.

Can I pay Surry County property tax in person?

Yes, at the drive-thru window at 915 East Atkins Street, or through the online portal.

Union County, NC Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in North Carolina
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Union County, NC Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Union County, NC Property Tax Guide sale

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Union County?
We buy Union County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Who handles your Union County tax bill

Two offices matter. Tax Administration oversees property tax, and its Revenue Division sends and collects the bills. Find the Revenue Division in Monroe at 500 N. Main Street, Suite 119, phone 704-283-3848, or write to P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111-0038.

For a question about your value, or to appeal it, contact the Tax Administrator's Office, Suite 236 in the same building, 704-283-3746. Paying by hand? The collector's counter inside the Government Center takes payments Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

Ten towns let the county bill for them as well: Fairview, Hemby Bridge, Lake Park, Marshville, Marvin, Mineral Springs, Stallings, Waxhaw, Wesley Chapel and Wingate. If your house is inside one, you receive one combined bill from the county. A parcel in any other town needs a quick call to find out who sends its bill.

Market context

Union County is one of the faster-growing places in the state. Its July 2025 population estimate is 267,674, which is 12.4% higher than the April 2020 base, spread over 632.74 square miles of land (376.6 people per square mile).

Owned homes have a median value of $417,300, and 81.6% are lived in by their owners. Housing units total 95,683 and builders pulled 2,707 permits for 2025. Median rent is $1,496, and median household income is $102,900. All that growth means your assessed value may look quite different from what you paid.

The 2025 revaluation

The latest countywide reappraisal lifted taxable value from $32.38 billion (2021) to $60.05 billion at the January 1, 2025 valuation date. That is a 60.05% jump. Homes gained 63.45%, while commercial and industrial property gained 45.59%.

The parcel count rose from 104,057 to 114,182, and the median home value went from $293,377 to $403,000.

In the years between reappraisals, you only get a new notice if the property itself changes: new construction, an addition, a teardown, a remodel, a rezoning or a change in acreage. State law sets reappraisal at least every eighth year, so ask Tax Administration when the next one is due.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Union County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates and interest

Real and personal property bills are payable from September 1. You can wait through January 5 without penalty, and a check postmarked by then counts as on time. If that date is a Saturday or Sunday, you get until Monday.

Beginning January 6, a 2% charge applies for the rest of the month, followed by three-fourths of 1% each month thereafter. Car and truck tax is paid when you register or renew the tag, so it is not part of this bill.

Union County payment calendar
DateWhat happens
September 1Bills fall due
January 5Final interest-free day
January 6 to 312% interest
Each month afterAnother three-fourths of 1% monthly

Call the office for this year's rate and ask whether a prepayment discount applies.

Other charges the Revenue Division collects

The division handles more than property tax. Your closing agent may ask about any of the following for the house you are selling.

  • Bills on land, buildings, and business or personal property.
  • Delinquent motor vehicle tax bills.
  • Gross receipts taxes.
  • Current and delinquent water and sewer bills.
  • Landfill fees and other utility payments.

The division also values every registered motor vehicle owned by a county resident. Phone 704-283-3848 to find out whether the property carries an open water, sewer or landfill balance.

Ways to pay

Union County accepts payment five ways.

  • Mail: use the return envelope or write to P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111.
  • Drop box: on Stewart St. Extension, behind the Historic Post Office.
  • Phone: 1-855-497-0718.
  • Web: the county's pay online link.
  • Counter: the Government Center.

At a sale, your closing agent can settle the current bill so the property passes to the buyer free of tax debt. Have the closer ask the Revenue Division for a payoff number.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Union County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Appealing your Union County assessment

Your first stop is an informal review with Tax Administration. If that does not settle it, request a formal hearing before the county's equalization board. A staff appraiser reviews what you submit and mails a written decision. Return the form printed at the foot of that letter and the case moves up to the board.

Five local citizens sit on the board, listen to you and to the staff, and rule within 30 days. Still disagree? The board's letter lays out the next step, the statewide Property Tax Commission, and G.S. 105-290 allows 30 days from the mailing date of that notice.

Evidence that helps: appraisals as of the revaluation date, sales of similar properties, photos of unusual damage, and letters about septic limits from Environmental Health or a soil scientist. The percentage of change since a prior assessment cannot be considered. Neither stage costs a fee, and hiring a lawyer is optional. Windows to file follow the mailing of notices, so call Tax Administration to learn the dates that apply now.

Programs that can reduce what you owe

An owner can pick one of three state programs to shrink a bill, never more than one. Apply to the county assessor using Form AV-9. On the 2026 form, the income limit is $38,800 and the upper circuit breaker band is $58,200.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion, G.S. 105-277.1.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion, G.S. 105-277.1C, with no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker, G.S. 105-277.1B: tax is held to a share of income and the rest is deferred as a lien.

Ask Tax Administration which one fits and when to file. A sale ends eligibility for the circuit breaker, so deferred taxes become payable at closing.

A short checklist before you list

Pull your latest bill and confirm whether you pay it yourself or through a lender's escrow account. Look up whether the parcel sits inside one of the ten towns, because that changes who sends the bill. Phone the Revenue Division for a balance on any water, sewer or landfill account. If you think your value is too high, gather comparable sales and photos before you call Tax Administration, since the evidence is what moves a reviewer. Then tell your closer which relief program, if any, you currently use, so a deferred amount is not a surprise at settlement.

The Government Center is the one building you may need for most of this, since the tax offices and the collector's counter are both there, so a single trip can cover a payoff request, a question about a value and a payment. Give yourself time. A payoff request to the Revenue Division is simple, but the closer needs the number before the settlement statement is drawn up, and a bank or the mail can add days. Starting a week or two ahead of the closing date keeps the sale on schedule.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

If tax is still due when you sell

Unpaid tax travels with the parcel. G.S. 105-355 puts a lien on it from the listing date, adding penalties, interest and costs, and that is why a buyer's lender will insist on payoff at the closing table.

A long-unpaid bill can end in a foreclosure suit (G.S. 105-374) and an auction held at the courthouse door. You can still redeem ahead of confirmation by paying the tax plus the added penalties, interest and costs.

Order a payoff from the Revenue Division, have the closer send it from your sale proceeds, and hold on to the receipt. Deed stamp tax is its own charge against the seller, taken by the register of deeds when the deed is filed.

With a cash buyer there is no lender underwriting or appraisal to wait on. Taxes still get paid from your proceeds, so request the number early and hand it to your closer. Raise utility balances in the same call, because those can hold up a closing if they surface late.

Frequently asked questions

When does Union County need my tax payment?

Due September 1. Interest stays off until January 6, when 2% applies for the month, and three-fourths of 1% is added monthly after that.

Where do I pay Union County property tax in person?

Use the collector's counter at the Government Center, open weekdays 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. Mailed payments go to the Monroe post office box.

Can I appeal my Union County value?

Yes. An informal review with Tax Administration comes first, and an equalization board hearing is next if needed. Call 704-283-3746 for dates.

Does Union County have a veteran property tax exclusion?

Yes, for a qualifying disabled veteran: the first $45,000 of value is excluded. Apply through the county assessor.

Who owes deed stamp tax on a Union County sale?

Seller pays it, at the register's office before the deed is recorded. Check the settlement statement for the amount.

Who sends your Wake County tax bill

Wake County Tax Administration sets values and collects payment. Its help desk answers at 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov.

A single bill can carry several charges. Under a local agreement the county also collects for the towns and special districts inside its borders, so questions about a town's own rate go to that town hall.

If your lender pays from escrow, no bill is mailed to you. Check the amount online anyway, because as the seller you should know the actual figure.

The Fiscal Year 2027 county rate

Commissioners adopted a $2.28 billion budget on June 1 for Fiscal Year 2027. A 2-cent increase lifts the county rate to 53.71 cents. That covers the county share only, and town and district rates are added on top.

The county's own illustration is a $90 increase for the owner of a $450,000 home. For your parcel, ask Tax Administration.

Rate changeUp 2 cents to 53.71 cents
Municipal and district chargesCollected by the county on one bill
Pay without interestFull balance by January 5, 2027

Due dates and penalties

Bills are due September 1, and January 5 is the last no-interest day. State law adds 2 percent from January 6, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or part month from February 1.

The county is flexible before that date. You can pay in pieces of any size with no approval, as long as the balance clears by January 5, and each payment brings a statement of what remains. Short-term plans exist too, and earlier calls get better options. Once a bill turns overdue, the office cannot help, and state law allows collection from wages, accounts or rent.

  • Pay online by bank draft, digital wallet or card.
  • Escrow accounts: the lender pays and no bill arrives.
  • Questions about a bill: 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wake County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Which value the September 2027 bill uses

The bill due September 1, 2027 uses values as of January 1, 2027, and rates approved by elected officials in June 2027. The bill due September 1, 2026 rests on January 1, 2024 values and the rates approved in June 2026.

A tax bill is two numbers multiplied together: assessed value and the rate per $100 set by county and municipal officials. The county's own worked example uses a house assessed at $450,000 at the 53.71 cent county rate. A revaluation changes values, not rates.

State law also makes local governments publish a revenue-neutral rate during the budget process, meaning the rate that would bring in about the same revenue as before the revaluation. Officials are not required to adopt that rate.

How often Wake County revalues

Every two years from here. The commissioners voted in March 2025 to phase in a two-year cycle, with the first two-year revaluation effective January 1, 2029. The idea is that long gaps let increases pile up and land on owners as one sudden jump.

Thirty-seven counties, Wake among them, have revaluations effective January 1, 2027. A rulebook called the Schedule of Values, approved by the commissioners, sets the rates and ranges used to value property between revaluations, and the county posts the PDF at wake.gov/sov.

  • Look up your current assessed value at wake.gov/realestate.
  • Report wrong property data at wake.gov/rehelp, with your address or account number and any documents.
  • Expect occasional appraiser visits: badges, county-marked vehicles, usually 15 to 30 minutes, and photos of the exterior.

Tax Administration address and phone numbers

The office is at 301 S. McDowell St., Ste. 3800, Raleigh, NC 27601. Mail goes to P.O. Box 2331, Raleigh, NC 27602. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding county holidays.

  • Property tax: 919-856-5400. Fax: 919-856-7128.
  • Gross receipts: 919-856-5999.
  • Online help center and chat: taxhelp.wake.gov/hc, or taxhelp@wake.gov.
  • Revaluation and appraisers: 919-857-3800 or revaluation@wake.gov.

The county also runs a Residential Sales Search tool that can filter by distance, sale date, heated area and year built, and a comparable sales tool is planned for January 2027. A seller preparing for a buyer or an appeal can use these listings to see what nearby houses sold for.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wake County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What the 2027 revaluation means for a seller

Values reset January 1, 2027, replacing the January 1, 2024 set, and later resets follow every two years. Buyers in 2027 will be pricing the tax on the new number.

The aim is for each assessed value to match fair market value, the most probable open-market price. Work runs through neighborhooding, pricing from sales, field and office review, then notices and appeals. About 460,000 parcels fall into 5,400 neighborhoods.

  • Results go to the commissioners on January 19, 2027, and notices follow that week.
  • The planned appeal deadline is April 30, 2027.

These are published targets. Confirm them at 919-857-3800 or revaluation@wake.gov.

How to appeal your assessment

Appeals go to the county's Board of Equalization and Review. Notices of value go out first, and owners can then appeal informally.

State law sets the board's first meeting between the first Mondays of April and May, and a hearing request must arrive before adjournment. Beyond the board lies the state Property Tax Commission, with 30 days from the mailed decision to file. Revaluation-year boards finish by December 1.

Gather nearby sales and repair estimates first. If the appeal will outlast closing, ask your attorney about handling a later change.

Tax relief for owners

Three state programs are available: Senior and Disabled, Tax Deferment and Disabled Veteran. Eligible groups are low-income owners 65 or older, low-income owners who are 100 percent disabled, and owners with a total, permanent service-connected disability (or their unmarried surviving spouses).

The state sets the dollar terms: a 2026 income limit of $38,800 on the state form, a $45,000 disabled veteran exclusion, and a circuit breaker that defers part of the bill as a lien. An owner may use only one program.

The application deadline is June 1. Late applications may be considered for good cause such as illness, a death in the immediate family, military deployment or delayed disability certification. Forgetting is not accepted.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

The debt stays with the parcel. State law attaches the lien as of the listing date for the tax year, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure action.

At closing, the attorney gets the amount due from Tax Administration and pays it from your proceeds. Interest starts January 6, so settle before then if you can.

With an inherited house in arrears, call Tax Administration first and ask what options remain. A cash buyer will still expect the tax payoff to come out of your proceeds, but you skip a lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the payoff figure is often the main item to settle before closing.

Frequently asked questions

Until when can I pay Wake County tax interest-free?

January 5, 2027 for the 2026 bills. Interest begins the next day.

Can I pay a Wake County bill in pieces?

Yes, in any amount, without approval, as long as the bill is paid by January 5. Short-term plans are available to early callers.

What is the next Wake County revaluation date?

January 1, 2027, after the January 1, 2024 cycle. Later ones follow every two years.

Who answers Wake County tax questions?

Tax Administration, 919-856-5400 or taxhelp@wake.gov. For revaluation, call 919-857-3800 or email revaluation@wake.gov.

Do older or disabled Wake owners get relief?

Yes: Senior and Disabled, Tax Deferment and Disabled Veteran. The deadline is June 1.

Paying a Warren County tax bill

The tax office is at 117 S. Main St. in Warrenton, 27589, beside the courthouse. Mail goes to PO Box 240, Warrenton, NC 27589. The office observes most national holidays.

Some payment routes carry fees, so it helps to know the free ones.

The 2026-2027 county rate and revaluation

The county rate on real and personal property for 2026-2027 is $0.5950 per $100. Confirm it with the tax office before you rely on it for a sale.

Warren last revalued in 2025. Those assessments stay in place until 2032 unless an owner adds something such as a garage, a room or a new house, and the next revaluation is slated for 2033. A private appraisal company assists the county.

The long gap affects a sale. A buyer's tax value stays on the 2025 appraisal, whatever the contract price, until the building changes.

Due dates and interest

The 2026 bills are due September 1 but not delinquent until January 6, 2027, so January 5 is the last clean day. Then 2 percent applies for January, plus three-fourths of one percent for each later month.

The county's yearly calendar shows what follows if you fall behind.
