Recording a deed with taxes owed

You need either a tax certification or an attorney's statement. Since January 7, 2026, a commissioners' resolution under G.S. 161-31 bars the Register of Deeds from accepting a transfer deed unless the Tax Collector certifies that no delinquent taxes are a lien.

The alternative is a statement added by the closing attorney that delinquent taxes will be paid at closing. Bring the deed to the Tax Collector between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. so staff can research the parcel and stamp it if warranted.

Check the tax account well before closing. Several unpaid years do not block a sale, but the arrears come out of your proceeds and the office needs research time.

How a Warren County value appeal works

Each January 1 opens the real property appeal window, which closes when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. An informal appeal form is posted under Forms on the county site.

State law puts the board's first meeting between the first Mondays of April and May. Ask for your hearing before adjournment. A losing owner has 30 days from the mailed decision to notify the Property Tax Commission.

Two more points apply here. The owner bears the burden of showing a substantial overstatement, and market-value arguments are allowed only in a revaluation year. Vehicles, boats, trailers, aircraft and business equipment follow a different clock: 30 days from receiving the bill.

Appeal steps and acceptable evidence

The path has three steps: informal appeal, formal appeal and the state Property Tax Commission. File a separate informal appeal form for each parcel, give your own opinion of value, and attach support for it.

  • Recent sales offered as support must have closed before the 1/1/2025 effective date of the revaluation. Later sales do not count.
  • Appraisals, photos of deferred maintenance and contractor estimates can go with the form.
  • Attorneys and tax representatives must supply a Power of Attorney.
  • Arguments based on the percentage increase from the last appraisal, the tax bill's size, economic conditions or the owner's ability to pay are not grounds for appeal.

If the informal review does not satisfy you, the formal appeal goes to the Board of Equalization and Review, a quasi-judicial setting where taxpayers give sworn testimony. A formal appeal filed after the board adjourns is heard the following tax year. From there, the Property Tax Commission requires Form AV-14, received or postmarked within 30 days of the board's mailed decision, and non-attorney representatives file Form AV-63.

The prior revaluation was effective 1/1/2017, so the 2025 change reflected eight years of market movement in one step.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Warren County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Listing and farm-use rules

Personal and business personal property is listed each January 1 to 31, with a 10 percent penalty for lateness. That list includes single wide mobile homes, farm equipment, unregistered vehicles, boats, aircraft, billboards and short-term rentals.

Land and buildings remain on the list for good, so nothing needs refiling each year unless the property changed. Request extensions by January 31. Mailed listings need a postmark by then, or April 15 with an extension. Get a mailing receipt.

Present use value matters to owners of working land. The minimums are:

  • Agricultural land: at least ten acres in commercial production of crops or animals.
  • Forest land: at least twenty acres meeting the forest requirements.
  • Horticultural land: at least five acres in commercial production of fruits, vegetables, nursery or floral products.
  • Agricultural and horticultural income: an average gross of $1,000 per year over three years; forest land has no income test.

Applications are due January 31. A buyer must apply within sixty days of a transfer, so mention enrollment to the buyer's attorney.

If a Warren County owner falls behind

Collection steps begin after January 6. Delinquent tax letters are mailed in March, and accounts still unpaid at the end of that month are advertised in the local paper in April. The tax office says enforced collection, up to and including foreclosure, can follow.

The tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, with penalties, interest and costs added, and the county can bring a foreclosure action in the county where the property lies. A sale goes to the highest bidder at the courthouse door, where the commissioner may ask for a deposit of up to 20 percent of the bid. Exceptions or an increased bid may be filed within 10 days after the report of sale. A person redeeming before confirmation pays all taxes plus penalties, interest and costs.

Selling before any of this starts sidesteps the whole sequence. Phone the Warrenton tax office for your balance, then have your closing attorney pay it at the table. A cash sale moves quickly, so ask for the balance before you accept an offer.

Relief for older, disabled and veteran owners

File by June 1. A senior aged 65 or older can pick up an application beginning January 2. Owners claiming disability, or disabled veteran status, attach the A-9A or NCDVA-9 form as well.

The state's terms: $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is greater, for the elderly or disabled, with a $38,800 income limit for 2026; and $45,000 off for a disabled veteran with no age or income test. Only one of the three programs may be used. Present use value can save up to 90 percent.

If you inherited a Warren County house, ask the tax office whether a new application is needed.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When does Warren County tax interest begin?

January 6, 2027 for the 2026 bills. January 5 is the last interest-free day.

Does Warren County check taxes before recording a deed?

Yes. Either the Tax Collector certifies the taxes or the closing attorney adds a statement that delinquent taxes will be paid at closing. The rule took effect January 7, 2026.

How can I pay Warren County tax free of fees?

By mailed check or the drop box at 117 S. Main St. Card and eCheck payments carry fees.

When is Warren County's next revaluation?

The last one was in 2025, and the next is slated for 2033.

When can I appeal my Warren County value?

Each January 1 opens the window for real property, and it closes when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. Start with the informal appeal form.

Which Watauga County office handles your tax bill

Two sets of staff share Suite 21 of the courthouse at 842 West King Street in Boone. Tax Administration appraises and lists property. The Tax Collector's Office alone collects taxes and fees. Both are open weekdays, 8:00 to 5:00, closed on holidays.

Call the listing department at 828-265-8021 and collections at 828-265-8036.

Boone is the seat, and Blowing Rock, Beech Mountain and Seven Devils are the other towns with their own rates. Your bill depends on which town, if any, and which fire district contain the parcel, so that is the first thing to pin down on a mountain property.

Watauga County tax rates

The rate schedule has a row for the county, each town and each fire district. The 2026 figures are below. Ask the tax office to confirm the current rates and their units before you quote them to a buyer.

Watauga County 2026 rates by tax district
Tax district2026 rate
Watauga County (G01)0.318
Boone (C02)0.44
Blowing Rock (C03)0.44
Seven Devils (C04)0.47
Beech Mountain (C05)0.65
Boone Fire Service District (F02)0.06
Municipal service district (MS1)0.1575

Most fire districts are 0.05, while Stewart Simmons is 0.085 and Todd is 0.07. Other charges include a $30.00 Boone municipal vehicle fee and a solid waste fee of 115.00 a year. A parcel's bill draws on the county row, then the town, then the fire district, whichever apply.

How the rates have moved

The county line is 0.318 for every year from 2022 through 2026, after 0.403 in 2021, 2020 and 2019. Earlier years were 0.353 for 2018 and 2017, and 0.313 for 2016.

  • Boone went from 0.36 in 2022 to 0.375, 0.39, 0.40 and 0.44 in the following years.
  • Blowing Rock was 0.37 for 2022 and 0.44 for 2026.
  • Seven Devils holds at 0.47 across 2022 to 2026.
  • Beech Mountain was 0.68 for 2022 and 0.65 afterward.

The solid waste user fee rose from $80.00 in 2022 to 102.87 in 2023 and 2024 and 115.00 in 2025 and 2026. A buyer comparing towns will notice that town rates differ more than the county's does.

Due dates and penalties

Payment is due September 1. Under G.S. 105-360, nothing extra is added before January 6, then two percent applies, and three-fourths of one percent is added for each month from February 1.

The collector adds a mailing rule. A check must reach the collector's counter or carry a postmark dated no later than the due date. A meter stamp is not a postmark, so metered mail counts as received only when someone delivers it.

The listing department also mails listing forms, prices personal property, and keeps billing records for farm use, elderly or disabled and exempt properties. Forms go out in the opening week of January, and the regular listing window runs to the final working day of the month. Untagged vehicles, real estate improvements and business personal property get listed, and farm use or exempt requests are also due by month's end.

How to pay

There are six ways: mail, counter, web, e-check, card and phone. For mail, address the check to the Watauga County Tax Collector, 842 West King Street, Ste. 21, Boone, NC 28607, and write the account number and parcel ID on it. A drop box waits at the courthouse's front entrance.

  • E-check adds $1.50.
  • A credit card adds 2.50 percent with a $2.00 floor, and the county does not keep that fee.
  • A consumer debit card adds a flat $3.50.
  • The phone line is 1-828-540-6193, on the same fee terms.

Under G.S. 105-321(b), the collector receives a yearly order that works like a court judgment without court involvement, and enforcement begins once a bill is delinquent. Whoever runs your closing usually pays the bill out of the price.

When a bill goes unpaid

A lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, with penalties and interest added (G.S. 105-355). The county may foreclose on real property for delinquent taxes. That needs a court order and is handled by a Boone law firm.

Unpaid real estate accounts are advertised from March 1 through June 30, at extra cost to the owner.

Back taxes do not bar a sale. They are settled from the price, and the collector can supply a written payoff before closing day.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Watauga County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to contest your valuation

Disputes begin with the county's equalization panel, which the commissioners staff unless a separate board exists (G.S. 105-322). Its sessions start in April or early May. Ask for a hearing, by letter or in person, while the panel is still sitting.

Beyond the county sits the state Property Tax Commission, which takes a written notice of appeal with your grounds shortly after the county mails its ruling (G.S. 105-290). The state's reappraisal rule is every eighth year (G.S. 105-286). Ask Tax Administration for Watauga's next reappraisal date, the hearing calendar and the exact filing deadlines.

Gather nearby sales, photos and any repair estimates before the hearing. Evidence of that kind is what moves a panel, and you can bring it whether or not you hire anyone.

Tax breaks for owners

North Carolina runs three relief programs for a permanent residence, and an owner picks one. The elderly or disabled exclusion is G.S. 105-277.1, the circuit breaker is G.S. 105-277.1B and the disabled veteran exclusion is G.S. 105-277.1C. NCDOR's 2026 form prints an income limit of $38,800 for the first two programs, and $58,200 as the upper figure for the circuit breaker.

Apply on Form AV-9 at the county assessor's office. Seniors age 65 and older use that same form. Ask the assessor how much of the exclusion applies to your home, and when to file.

Selling with taxes owed

Whatever is unpaid stays attached to the parcel until closing. Owners on the circuit breaker should know deferred taxes for the previous three years fall due on a transfer. Check the parcel's jurisdiction first, since a Boone address and a rural fire-district parcel pay different combinations.

Request a written payoff from the Tax Collector's Office, hand it to your closing attorney, and have the attorney pay it from your proceeds. A cash buyer will expect the same payoff, only on a faster timeline, so ask early and keep the receipt.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to gather before you call

Have your account number, parcel ID and the town or fire district name in front of you. With those, staff can tell you the rate rows that apply, the current balance and any open fees. If you plan to sell, ask in the same call whether a farm use or exempt status is in place, since those records are kept with the listing department and may need to be updated for the buyer.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay at the counter in Boone?

At the Tax Collector's Office, Suite 21 of the courthouse at 842 West King Street in Boone. A drop box sits at the courthouse front entrance.

Does a meter stamp count as a postmark for Watauga County tax?

No. Metered mail is not treated as postmarked, so it counts as received when it reaches the collector's office.

When do Watauga County listing forms go out?

The first week of January. The regular listing period lasts through the last working day of January.

What does paying a Watauga County bill by card cost extra?

Credit cards add 2.50 percent with a $2.00 minimum, and consumer debit cards a flat $3.50. The county does not receive the fee.

What is the deadline to carry a Watauga County valuation dispute to the state commission?

Thirty days from the day the county mailed its decision. File a written notice stating your grounds and send the assessor a copy.

Who sends and collects the bill

Wayne divides the work between two desks. Tax Administration decides what your property is worth. The Tax Collector sends the bill and receives the money; mail goes to P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533. Both are reached from the county tax page.

That page links a billings search, rates, forms, maps, relief programs and a list of tax foreclosure sales, which lets you check what you owe before the sign goes up.

  • Collector: balances, payoff letters, payment options
  • Administration: value, appeals, relief applications
  • Register of Deeds in Goldsboro: deeds and deeds of trust

The site also posts downloadable appraisal data and the 2025 schedule of values, which shows the unit prices the appraisers applied to land and buildings.

Wayne County housing at a glance

Goldsboro anchors a county of 122,278 people over 553.92 square miles. There are 55,106 housing units and 47,507 households, and owners hold 61.5% of occupied homes. Rent runs a median $965 a month, and roughly four homes in ten are rentals, which makes landlords a large share of local sellers.

Growth has been slow: 122,623 residents in 2010, then 117,333 in 2020, with the newest estimate 4.2% over 2020. New building has been modest, with 954 permits for 2025. Because 86.1% of residents kept the same address last year, plenty of owners have no recent sale to go by, and the revaluation notice may be the first price signal they have had in years.

The 2025 reappraisal

The county revalued every parcel as of 2025 and mailed notices in March. Its revaluation page describes a base of more than 64,000 parcels. Revaluation changes assessed value only. The commissioners and city or town boards set rates later, in budget season.

Appraisers compared recent sales, priced the cost to rebuild, and used an income method on commercial parcels. The county did not apply a flat percentage. Its example is two matching 2019 houses that ended up worth different amounts by 2025.

Revaluation notices for Goldsboro houses and for rural Wayne parcels arrive together, but the numbers rarely move in step. Check the land line and the building line separately, since an error in square footage or condition shows up there first.

Wayne is above the 75,000 population line in G.S. 105-286, so the state can require an earlier reappraisal if the sales ratio drifts outside .85 to 1.15.

A reappraisal looks at local sales, so a neighborhood with new construction and steady buyers can move differently from a farm district. Set your notice beside sales on your own street before you decide to contest it.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wayne County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Fill out the review form that came with your notice and get it to the Tax Office within 30 days of the notice date. An appraiser then looks at it.

When that informal review changes nothing, a second notice lays out the formal hearing in front of the county's Board of Equalization and Review, and the state Property Tax Commission sits above it. Hold on to copies of whatever you send, since the board hearing starts from that same file.

  • Strong evidence: an appraisal, written repair bids, dated damage photos, nearby sales
  • Weak grounds: your ability to pay, or a value already close to market

Outside revaluation years, use the county's non reappraisal year appeals page instead.

Due dates and penalties

Tax calendar for a Wayne County parcel
EventTiming
Owners list propertyAll of January, starting the first business day
Bill comes dueSeptember 1
Interest startsJanuary 6, at 2%
Hearing board startsOpens sometime from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May
State appeal30 days after the board mails its decision

From February 1 on, interest accrues at three-quarters of one percent a month. Early payment discounts are a local option, so the Tax Collector can tell you whether one is offered.

Tax relief programs

Homeowners can cut or postpone a bill three ways, and every one begins with Form AV-9 filed with the county assessor. The Department of Revenue's 2026 form lists a $38,800 income cap, with $58,200 applying to the upper circuit breaker band.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shields $25,000 or half the appraised value, whichever is more (G.S. 105-277.1).
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: $45,000 off the value, and income does not matter (G.S. 105-277.1C).
  • Circuit breaker: caps the bill at 4% or 5% of income and defers whatever is left (G.S. 105-277.1B).

File during the January listing season. The assessor has to take applications up to June 1 before the tax year. Anything deferred turns into a lien and is due when the house sells.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wayne County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If you sell with taxes owed

Wayne's lien attaches every January 1 (G.S. 105-355), and it stays on the house through a sale, which is why the title company settles the balance from your proceeds.

If nobody pays, the county can sue and sell the house at the courthouse (G.S. 105-374), but paying the full amount owed still redeems it until the sale is confirmed. Wayne keeps a tax foreclosure sales page of its own.

Get the payoff in writing from the Tax Collector, and let the closing office know about any deferral or open appeal.

What to ask before you list

  • What is owed on the parcel today, and has this year's bill gone out?
  • Does a Goldsboro special assessment or nuisance abatement charge sit on it?
  • Is an appeal of the 2025 value still open?
  • Is a circuit breaker deferral on the account?

Call the Tax Collector, or try the billings search on the Wayne tax site. With an inherited or empty house in Goldsboro or the country, find out who the county shows as owner before anything else.

Steps to take before closing

  1. Find your parcel in the billings search and write down the balance and the tax year.
  2. Ask for a written payoff that stays good through closing day.
  3. See whether an appeal or a circuit breaker deferral is attached.
  4. Give the figure to the closing attorney or title company.
  5. Afterward, make sure the tax office has the new owner's name and mailing address.

A cash sale runs through the same checklist, minus the lender's appraisal and underwriting. With those gone, the tax payoff is often the one item with a hard date, so settle the account early.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Heirs and landlords

Wayne mails each bill to the owner of record. When an heir never recorded anything, the late owner can still be on the account, so ask the Tax Collector whose name is listed and where the mail goes.

A rented house and an empty one get the same bill. Add up each year's balance before you settle on a closing date.

Deed history sits with the register of deeds, and the county's real estate search shows parcel details. Used together, they let a buyer or attorney see who really holds title before a contract is signed.

  • Open the parcel in the real estate search
  • Get the payoff on paper
  • Ask who handles the January listing after the sale

Frequently asked questions

What day does interest begin on a Wayne County bill?

January 6. The bill is due September 1, but interest holds off until that January date. It then runs at 2% through February 1 and 3/4 of 1% a month afterward.

How many parcels did Wayne County revalue in 2025?

The county cites more than 64,000 parcels. Owners received notices in March 2025.

Does revaluation set my tax rate?

No. Revaluation updates value. Elected boards set the rate during budget work, and the county tax page links a Tax Rates page.

Who qualifies for the $45,000 veteran exclusion?

A qualifying disabled veteran owner and certain unmarried surviving spouses, with no age or income limit. Apply on Form AV-9 with the assessor, after a county veteran services office completes the VA portion.

Where do I mail a Wayne County tax payment?

Wayne County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1495, Goldsboro, NC 27533. Online payment is also linked from the county tax page.

Where to take tax questions

Wilkes County Tax Administration works out of the county offices at 110 North Street in Wilkesboro. The appraisal department handles revaluation and appeal calls at 336-651-7301, weekdays from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM. Appeals staff sit on the second floor (see the county's appeals FAQ).

The Tax Administration page pulls the tools together: online payment, a parcel and real property search, GIS maps, personal property forms, occupancy tax information and the Board of Equalization and Review.

  • Listings department: personal property and business listings
  • Appraisal department: assessed value and appeals
  • Online payment link: bills for the current year

The 2025 revaluation

The county's last two revaluations were in 2019 and 2025, the newer one effective January 1, 2025. The county estimated that real property values rose about 75% to 80% overall, though the spread was wide. Notices went out on March 17, 2025, showing land and structure values as of January 1, 2025. Owners with present use value land saw both the use value and the gross land value on the notice.

Higher values do not turn into a proportional tax increase, because the county, fire districts and towns set their rates in June. Wilkes also reappraises more often than the eight year minimum state law requires, so ask the tax office when the next one is due before you price a house.

Which areas moved the most

Estimated 2025 value change by area
AreaEstimated increase
Countywide75-80%
Town of North Wilkesboro75-80%
Town of Wilkesboro56-61%
Town of Elkin88-93%
Town of Ronda101-106%

These ranges were estimates made before notices went out, so your own notice and property record are the figures that count. A house in the Town of Wilkesboro and one in the Town of Ronda started from very different places.

The gap is large. Ronda and State Road township sat near 100% or more, while Ferguson township and the Town of Wilkesboro stayed in the 50s. Elkin and Traphill landed at 88% to 93%. If you are selling in one of the faster rising areas, expect buyers to ask what the new value means for their bill, and have the revaluation notice ready.

The area figure explains why a neighbor's notice looked different from yours. It does not replace the sales evidence you would bring to an appeal.

How to appeal your assessment

Once a change of value notice reaches you, file the appeal online with your supporting documents. That window closes within weeks of the mailing, so do not wait.

The review period in a revaluation year can stretch to December 1, and hearings may come later. If you have a bill but no decision yet, a later reduction applies back to that year's bill, and a paid bill that gets cut produces a refund.

Filing an appeal does not forfeit the early payment discount. In 2025 the 1.5% discount for paying by August 31 stayed available as long as payment came before September 1, and interest did not begin until January 6.

At the state level, you can ask the county board for a hearing before it adjourns. A Property Tax Commission appeal must be filed within 30 days after the board mails its decision.

Due dates and penalties

The due date is September 1, and a payment made before January 6 carries no interest. From January 6 to February 1 the charge is 2%. After that it is three-quarters of one percent for each month.

The listing period closes January 31 unless the commissioners extend it, and they have pushed back the personal property deadline before. The listings department can give you this year's date. Bills usually go in the mail during the summer.

Paying the bill and the early discount

Wilkes takes payment online through a link on the Tax Administration page, and the tax office can also take it in person at North Street. The bill is due September 1. In 2025, paying by August 31 earned a 1.5% discount, which rewards a seller still living in the house for paying ahead of the due date.

When the house sells before you pay, the balance gets settled at the closing table. Hold on to any online payment confirmation, since the attorney may want it to compare against the county's records.

Relief programs

Three programs run through the Wilkes tax office: an elderly or disabled exclusion, a disabled veteran exclusion, and the circuit breaker deferment. You can pick up an application from the forms page or the tax office. Every year has its own cutoff, so ask early.

  • Elderly or disabled: $25,000 or 50% of appraised value, whichever is larger.
  • Disabled veteran: the first $45,000 of value is excluded, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: bill limited to 4% of income (5% in the upper band), and the excess becomes a deferred lien.

The Department of Revenue's AV-9 form for 2026 sets an income limit of $38,800. Pick one program, since owners cannot combine them.

Selling with taxes owed

Wilkes taxes become a lien on the January 1 listing date, and the buyer's lawyer will want it cleared by closing. Left unpaid, the lien lets the county foreclose and auction the property. Until the sale is confirmed you can still redeem, by paying tax, penalties, interest and costs.

Start with a call to the tax office for the total owed. If a circuit breaker deferral sits on the parcel, tell your closing attorney, because the deferred years come due at the sale.

Towns, townships and districts

Results from the revaluation are broken out by four towns, North Wilkesboro, Wilkesboro, Ronda and Elkin, and by township. Inside a town, one bill carries both town and county tax, and a fire district can add its own charge. Rates come from separate boards, so give the tax office your parcel number and ask which districts apply. Buyers in Wilkesboro, North Wilkesboro, Elkin or Ronda will want to see the town portion separated from the county portion, and a rural buyer will ask about the fire district charge instead.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to ask the tax office before you list

Call 336-651-7301 or visit Tax Administration with the parcel number. The answers decide what your closing attorney holds back from your proceeds.

  • What is the current year's balance, and has the bill been mailed?
  • Is any appeal on the parcel still undecided?
  • Is there a relief program deferral, such as the circuit breaker, on the account?
  • Is present use value land part of the sale?
  • Which fire or town districts apply?

A pending appeal does not pause the bill. Pay by the due date and let any reduction come back as a refund. Wilkes County takes online payment, so save the receipt for the closing file.

Closing day checklist

  1. Ask the tax office to put the payoff figure on paper.
  2. Pass it to your closing attorney along with any deferral details.
  3. Check where an appeal stands so a lower value is not lost.
  4. File away the receipt and the recorded deed.

Selling for cash can shorten the timeline, yet the tax balance still comes out of your proceeds, so the same calls apply.

Frequently asked questions

When was the latest Wilkes County revaluation?

The county revalued effective January 1, 2025, and its previous revaluation was in 2019. It estimated a countywide increase of 75% to 80%, varying by property.

Does an open appeal cost me the early payment discount?

In 2025, no. The 1.5% discount applied if the bill was paid before September 1, even with an appeal pending. Ask the tax office whether a discount applies to the current year.

What happens if the county lowers my value after I paid?

You get a refund of the overpayment. A reduction on appeal applies back to the bill for that year.

Is there an interest-free period on Wilkes County bills?

Yes. Bills are due September 1, but no interest accrues until January 6. After that, 2% applies to February 1, then three-quarters of a percent monthly.

Does Wilkes County give a break to a disabled veteran who owns a home?

Yes. A disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of appraised value under state law. File with the county assessor and ask the tax office for the current form.

Who collects property tax

Wilson County Tax Administration lists, values and collects property tax for the county. It also collects for nine municipalities, two solid waste taxes, two special districts and fifteen fire districts, so one bill can carry several layers. Details are on the tax administration page.

The counter is at 113 Nash Street East in the city of Wilson, and there are four ways to pay, online among them. Bills go out by mail in early August. Owners of residential dwellings outside a municipality now get a solid waste permit with that bill.

Mail is processed by the USPS postmark. A drop box or a small post office may not stamp the same day, so send payments, listing forms and appeals several days early or ask the counter clerk for a postmark.

Wilson County housing at a glance

The county covers roughly 373 square miles east of Raleigh. Its seat, the city of Wilson, has more than 50,000 residents on about 14.2 square miles, and the county carries roughly 43,000 parcels in its real estate listing system.

  • 81,150 people, a 2.4% rise since the 2020 count.
  • 38,463 housing units, with owners living in 60.0% of occupied homes.
  • Typical owned homes valued at $186,000 and typical rent of $953.

Six in ten occupied homes have owner residents, so most of your buyers will be buying to live in the house, while a sizable minority of sellers are landlords.

Payment deadline

Bills fall due September 1. Payment at face amount works up to the day before January 6, and balances left after that are delinquent.

Late interest begins at 2% for the first weeks and then climbs by three-fourths of a percent each month. Ask the tax office whether any early payment discount applies, since a county may adopt a discount schedule by a resolution passed before May 1.

One common seller question has a simple answer. The person on the deed as of January 1 receives the bill, and a later sale usually changes the name only for the following year.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wilson County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The revaluation and your assessment

Wilson County reappraised real property as of January 1, 2024, its first reappraisal since 2016, and it works on an eight year cycle. North Carolina law requires counties to reappraise at least that often.

The revaluation covered more than 41,000 real property parcels. Personal property has been split onto its own bill, apart from real estate, since the 2024 bills.

The county's Comper tool lets an owner compare a house with neighborhood sales as of the revaluation date. Those sales are the best evidence to bring to the tax office if a value looks high.

How to appeal your assessment

Get the current form and cutoff from the tax office. Each real property window closes when the review board adjourns, and a new one opens the following January.

State law sets the outer frame. The commissioners normally sit as the review board in spring, and an owner who loses at that stage has a month to go on to the state commission.

Personal property has its own appeal cutoff, set each year. The appeal has to be in writing, by email or postmarked by that deadline, so ask the tax office for the date before you rely on it. Keep a copy of whatever you send, and note the postmark date.

Tax relief for owners

Three state relief programs exist, and one owner draws on only one of them. The county tax office takes the application, and the state AV-9 form names June 1 as the cutoff.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half a home's appraised value for older or fully disabled owners under the income ceiling, printed by NCDOR as $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes $45,000 of value for a qualifying disabled veteran, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: holds the bill to 4% or 5% of income, with the $58,200 ceiling, and defers the rest as a lien.

The rules are on the NCDOR form.

What else can appear on the bill

Besides the county levy, a parcel may carry a municipal tax, a fire district tax, a special district tax or a solid waste charge, because the county collects for all of them. Which ones apply depends on where the house stands, so read the bill line by line. If a line surprises you, call the tax office before closing so the buyer is not caught off guard by a charge that was never mentioned.

A seller with a vehicle, boat or business equipment may receive two separate bills, since personal property is billed apart from real estate. For homes outside a municipality, the solid waste permit arrives with the annual bill, so a buyer taking over such a house should ask the seller to hand it over at closing.

A house inside the city of Wilson is billed for city tax through the same office, and the tax calculator on the county site lets owners test the combined result with their assessed value.

Selling with taxes owed

A balance follows the parcel into the sale, so closing is the moment to clear it. The lien arises on the listing date each year, and collection can end in a court-supervised sale.

Wilson County adds a local step. Under G.S. 161-31 and a 2004 commissioners' resolution, the Register of Deeds takes a deed for recording only if it carries a statement about delinquent taxes. An attorney can complete the statement personally, or the deed goes first to the Collections Division of the tax department, where a clerk checks the parcel for delinquent tax. The county asks that taxes and recording fees go in separate checks. Questions go to the tax office at 252-399-2900, option 2.

Tax calendar

Wilson County property tax calendar
StepTiming

Listing periodJanuary 1 to 31 (extensions possible)
Relief applicationsThrough June 1
Taxes dueSeptember 1
Face amount payment endsDay before January 6

If your closing falls in the fall, the settlement agent should show the bill as paid or credit it from your proceeds.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps before you close

  1. Call 252-399-2900, option 2, and ask for the balance on your parcel.
  2. Decide with your attorney which route you will use for the delinquent tax statement.
  3. Write two checks, one for taxes and one for recording fees.
  4. Ask for the solid waste permit hand-off, if the house is outside a city.

A cash buyer still needs the deed recorded with that statement, so a clean tax account shortens the closing no matter how the buyer pays.

Frequently asked questions

How can I send a payment to the Wilson County tax office?

Visit the counter at 113 Nash Street East in Wilson, or use the county's online payment site. Four payment methods are offered in all.

Who receives the bill if I sell during the year?

The January 1 owner. A mid-year sale normally shows up the next tax year, so buyer and seller settle the split at closing.

Is the Wilson County cutoff January 5 or January 6?

January 6 is the last day, and par payment is allowed before January 6. Confirm the exact cutoff with the tax office before you pay late in the season.

Is an appeal still open to me?

Ask the tax office, because the window depends on the year. Real property windows close when the review board adjourns, and a new one opens the next January.

Do I need a clearance before recording a deed in Wilson County?

Yes, in the sense that the deed needs a delinquent tax statement. An attorney can sign it, or a tax department clerk can verify the parcel first, and the Register of Deeds then records it.

Where to pay in Yadkin County

The Yadkin County Tax Department is in Yadkinville. The in-person payment counter is in the Magnolia building across from the courthouse at 101 South State Street, and the office line is 336-849-7903. The tax office page has the rest.

There are four ways to pay:

  • Online, through the county's bill lookup and payment site.
  • By telephone at 866-249-4184, with the year and bill number.
  • In person at the Magnolia building.
  • By mail to Yadkin County Tax Department, P.O. Box 1217, Yadkinville NC 27055, with a printed copy of the online bill.

Contact the office for address changes, value changes and general questions. Deed work belongs with an attorney.

Yadkin County housing at a glance

Yadkinville is the county seat, and the tax counter sits there. Most sellers will deal with the office by phone first, then visit the Magnolia building only if a payment or form has to be handed over in person. The county covers roughly 335 square miles of land, with about 111 residents on each. The 2025 population estimate is 38,325, a 3.0% gain over 2020.

  • Owners occupy 76.9% of homes.
  • The typical owned home is valued at $181,200, and typical rent is $766.
  • About 22.4% of residents are 65 or older, so age-based relief matters here.

Only 116 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction is modest and resale homes dominate. Many households stay in place, which means a lot of owners have not seen a recent sale price on their own house.

The 2027 revaluation

A 2027 revaluation is underway. State law keeps every county on a cycle of at most eight years, and the 2023 reappraisal notices are posted in the county's document center.

Revaluation moves each parcel's assessed value to its market value as of the new January 1 date. State law defines true value as the price a willing buyer and willing seller would agree on. Owners often see bigger changes than usual in a reappraisal year, and the review window is the time to compare the new notice with recent nearby sales.

Ask the tax office when notices will be mailed and how to reach an appraiser. Once a new notice arrives, set it beside the 2023 value and beside what similar Yadkinville and rural houses recently sold for, and note any change that looks out of line. The county keeps a reappraisal appeal form in its online form center.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Yadkin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Due dates, discount and fees

The county offers a 2% discount for paying in August, ahead of the September 1 due date. Interest starts after the grace period that ends the day before January 6.

Solid waste fees are billed separately: $76.00 per household, $38.00 for a household with the elderly exemption, and $10.00 for extra stickers. They are not part of the value-based tax, so ask whether they are paid up at closing. The bill goes to whoever held title at the start of the year, so a seller who closes in the fall still owes the tax for that year unless the settlement statement shifts it.

How to appeal your assessment

Your first move is a phone call or email to the tax office, since it handles value changes. A failed informal request goes to the county's review board as a formal appeal. The commissioners usually serve as that board.

A hearing can be requested in writing or in person before the board adjourns. Its decision is mailed within 30 days after it adjourns. In a reappraisal year the board calendar runs longer, so ask which dates apply. A stronger case includes recent sale prices of similar homes nearby, photographs and repair estimates.

Beyond the county, the Property Tax Commission takes a written notice filed within 30 days of the mailed decision.

Relief programs

The Yadkin tax office takes applications for state exemptions and exclusions. The three below use NCDOR's 2026 figures. An owner picks one, because they cannot be combined.

North Carolina relief programs open to Yadkin County owners
ProgramQualificationBenefit
Elderly or disabled exclusionAge 65 plus or fully and permanently disabled, income no higher than $38,800 for 2026Greater of $25,000 or 50% of value excluded
Disabled veteran exclusionA qualifying disabled veteran or unmarried surviving spouse, no age or income testFirst $45,000 of value excluded
Circuit breakerSame age or disability test, five years living in the home, income up to $58,200Tax capped at 4% or 5% of income, excess deferred

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor, which accepts it through June 1.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Yadkin County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Who to contact for what

The tax office has three email links: one for assessor and payment matters, one for appraisal, and one for exemptions. Pick the link that matches your question. Use the appraisal link for a value question and the exemptions link for relief forms, so the message reaches the right person quickly.

You can also pull printable parcel maps from the county's GIS site and download property record cards from the tax page. The record card lists what the county has recorded about a house, so read it for errors in square footage or condition before a buyer's appraiser does. Deed questions belong with an attorney and the Register of Deeds.

Selling with unpaid tax

Settlement takes the balance from the seller's side. The lien is dated to the first of the year, so a sale does not wipe it out, and an unpaid parcel can be collected through a courthouse auction.

Request a payoff amount that includes solid waste fees before you list, and pass it along to the closing attorney. The payoff should be dated close to closing, since interest keeps adding to a late balance every month. Rural land can carry extra layers, so ask for the whole parcel record.

Solid waste fees and business listing

Count the $76.00 household fee among the yearly carrying costs of a Yadkin property. A purchaser's lawyer may want proof that stickers and fees are current, so check with the tax office.

Business personal property, such as tools or equipment kept at a rental or workshop, is listed in January. The listing period runs from the first working day of January through its end, and commissioners may extend it. Anyone with good cause may request more time in writing. Anything not listed can draw a penalty, so ask the office how to list.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Timeline before listing a home

Sellers in Yadkin County do best when they plan backward from the first day of September. A seller who plans a fall or winter closing should confirm the bill status in August, when the 2% discount applies, and again before the end of the year.

  • January 1: ownership and value fixed for the year
  • January 1 to 31: personal property listing
  • August: 2% early payment discount
  • September 1: taxes due
  • January 6: interest begins

Buyers and sellers usually split the bill by closing date, and the attorney's settlement statement should show the split.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Yadkin County tax office phone number?

336-849-7903. The counter serves walk-ins on weekdays, with the day ending at 5:00 pm.

Does Yadkin County offer an early payment discount?

Yes, a 2% discount applies when taxes are paid in August. Confirm the current terms with the office.

Can I pay Yadkin County taxes by phone?

Yes, call 866-249-4184 and have the year and bill number ready.

When is the Yadkin County revaluation?

A 2027 revaluation is underway. Ask the office when notices will be mailed.

How much is the Yadkin County solid waste fee?

$76.00 per household and $38.00 for households with the elderly exemption, with additional stickers at $10.00.
